entry.title: Research Summary: July 08, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's highlights combine novel decoding architectures, agentic coding, and a dominant safety/alignment cluster.

  • Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion (NVIDIA) unifies autoregressive, diffusion, and self-speculation decoding in one tri-mode model for practical speed.
  • KAT-Coder-V2.5 reports full agentic RL post-training for autonomous operation inside executable repositories.

Safety & alignment is heavily represented:

  • Neel Nanda's group finds data filtering barely removes undesirable SFT-acquired behaviors across OLMo models—a surprising negative result.
  • A position paper argues AI-generated CSAM prevention needs new methods, since standard safety assumes data availability.
  • A Milgram-style obedience test shows most of eleven open-source LLMs deliver maximum simulated shocks.
  • Pluralis v0.1 adds a 6,000-prompt multilingual benchmark across six Asia-Pacific countries and eight languages.

Theory and AI-for-science round out the list: To Retain or to Adapt? (DeepMind/Precup) reframes continual learning toward adaptation in non-stationary settings; Deep Neural Variation Spaces unifies norm-based depth-complexity bounds; first integration of GNSS zenith wet delay into the Aurora weather foundation model improves precipitation forecasting; and A Definition and Roadmap for World Models clarifies a central contested concept.
entry.content:
Today's highlights combine novel decoding architectures, agentic coding, and a dominant safety/alignment cluster.

  • Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion (NVIDIA) unifies autoregressive, diffusion, and self-speculation decoding in one tri-mode model for practical speed.
  • KAT-Coder-V2.5 reports full agentic RL post-training for autonomous operation inside executable repositories.

Safety & alignment is heavily represented:

  • Neel Nanda's group finds data filtering barely removes undesirable SFT-acquired behaviors across OLMo models—a surprising negative result.
  • A position paper argues AI-generated CSAM prevention needs new methods, since standard safety assumes data availability.
  • A Milgram-style obedience test shows most of eleven open-source LLMs deliver maximum simulated shocks.
  • Pluralis v0.1 adds a 6,000-prompt multilingual benchmark across six Asia-Pacific countries and eight languages.

Theory and AI-for-science round out the list: To Retain or to Adapt? (DeepMind/Precup) reframes continual learning toward adaptation in non-stationary settings; Deep Neural Variation Spaces unifies norm-based depth-complexity bounds; first integration of GNSS zenith wet delay into the Aurora weather foundation model improves precipitation forecasting; and A Definition and Roadmap for World Models clarifies a central contested concept.

entry.title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion: A Tri-Mode Language Model Unifying Autoregressive, Diffusion, and Self-Speculation Decoding

author.name: Yonggan Fu, Lexington Whalen, Abhinav Garg, Chengyue Wu, Maksim Khadkevich, Nicolai Oswald, Enze Xie, Daniel Egert, Sharath Turuvekere Sreenivas, Shizhe Diao, Chenhan Yu, Ye Yu, Weijia Chen, Sajad Norouzi, Jingyu Liu, Shiyi Lan, Ligeng Zhu, Jin Wang, Jindong Jiang, Morteza Mardani, Mehran Maghoumi, Song Han, Ante Juki\'c, Nima Tajbakhsh, Jan Kautz, Pavlo Molchanov

entry.summary: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion is a tri-mode language model from NVIDIA that unifies autoregressive, diffusion, and self-speculation decoding in one architecture trained with a joint objective, allowing mode-switching for throughput. In self-speculation mode diffusion drafts while AR verifies, outperforming multi-token prediction on acceptance and device efficiency.

entry.title: KAT-Coder-V2.5 Technical Report

author.name: Bo Huang, Fengxiang Li, Hao Xu, Haoyang Huang, Hongyi Fu, Jinhua Hao, Kun Yuan, Minglei Zhang, Pengcheng Xu, Shiyang Liu, Wenhao Zhuang, Yuze Shi, Zongxian Feng, Chao Wang, Cheng He, Chongling Rao, Deyu Cao, Fan Yang, Gang Xiong, Haochen Liu, Jiabao Li, Jian Liang, Jinghui Jia, Jingwen Chang, Jun Du, Junyu Shi, Min Li, Mingqi Wu, Qiang Gao, Shangpeng Yan, Shaotong Qi, Shu Xu, Shuo Zhou, Tiankuo Xu, Tong Zheng, Weilun Zhao, Xiancheng Meng, Xianda Sun, Xiaoyu Jiang, Xunhao Jia, Yao Xia, Yimeng Xu, Yinghan Cui, Yingpeng Chen, Yiwen Ning, Yong Wang, Yuxuan Sun, Zhongsheng Liu, Ming Sun, Cheng Luo, Chen Yang, Han Li, Kun Gai

entry.summary: Technical report for KAT-Coder-V2.5, an agentic coding model trained to operate autonomously inside executable repositories, with a full post-training pipeline (AutoBuilder for sandboxed reproducible environments, verifiable rewards, and tool-use trajectory synthesis). It targets the scarcity of reproducible environments and high-value trajectories rather than raw scale.

entry.title: To Retain or to Adapt? Generalizing Continual Learning

author.name: Giulia Lanzillotta, Mandana Samiei, Doina Precup, Razvan Pascanu, Claire Vernade

entry.summary: Challenges the retention-centered premise of continual learning, arguing that in non-stationary environments prioritizing retention can impede adaptation, and reframes CL as online optimization minimizing Average Lifelong Error. Introduces Transfer Efficiency to quantify the stability-adaptation tension.

entry.title: Position: Preventing AI-Generated CSAM Necessitates New Approaches to AI Safety

author.name: Neil Kale, Rebecca Portnoff, Pratiksha Thaker, Michael Simpson, Robertson Wang, Kevin Kuo, Chhavi Yadav, Virginia Smith

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that preventing AI-generated child sexual abuse material requires new safety approaches because existing techniques assume data accessibility, transparency, and evaluation practices incompatible with the legal and ethical constraints around such material. It outlines 15 open problems in areas like dataset auditing, red teaming, and fine-tuning prevention.

entry.title: Deep Neural Variation Spaces: A Unifying Perspective on Depth and Complexity

author.name: Julia Nakhleh, Robert D. Nowak

entry.summary: This theory paper introduces deep neural variation spaces, a recursively defined function-space framework that unifies norm-based complexity bounds and depth characterizations across a broad range of activation functions beyond ReLU. It connects several disparate lines of deep-learning theory.

entry.title: Integrating GNSS-Derived Zenith Wet Delay into a Weather Foundation Model Improves Precipitation Forecasting

author.name: Leonardo Trentini, Fanny Lehmann, Laura Crocetti, Benedikt Soja

entry.summary: This work performs the first integration of GNSS-derived zenith wet delay, an all-weather moisture measure, into the Aurora weather foundation model, showing systematic improvements in severe precipitation forecasting. It demonstrates how a long-assimilated numerical-weather variable can enhance ML weather models.

entry.title: Pluralis v0.1: Towards a Multicultural, Multimodal, Multilingual Benchmark for AI Risk and Reliability

author.name: Alicia Parrish, Rajat Shinde, Sanket Badhe, Xinyi Bai, Sree Bhargavi Balija, Hua-Rong Chu, Emilio Ferrara, Armstrong Foundjem, Rajat Ghosh, Aakash Gupta, Xuanli He, Ong Chen Hui, Minji Jung, Madhangi Karimanal, Faiza Khan Khattak, Boryoung Kim, Eugenia Kim, Liliya Lavitas, Seok Min Lim, Victor Lu, Jim Moirangthem, Dhivya Nagasubramanian, Deepak Pandita, Sita Rajagopal, Geetha Raju, Evgeniia Razumovskaia, Aravind Reddy, Federico Ricciuti, Nobin Sarwar, Sungpil Shin, Sunayana Sitaram, Snehal Thorat, Tharindu Cyril Weerasooriya, Jasmijn Bastings, Joachim Baumann, Kongtao Chen, Murali Emani, Mariya Hendriksen, Jiho Jin, Jun Seong Kim, Younghoon Ko, Alicja Kwasniewska, Minjae Lee, Tom Wei-cyuan Lin Kashyap Ramanandula Manjusha, Junho Myung, Junyeong Park, Roma Patel, Shyam Ratan, Sudarsun Santhiappan, Priyanka Suresh, Tuesday, Ksheeraj Sai Vepuri Laura Amortegui-Ordonez, Claire Dennis, Minsuk Kahng, Chris Knotz, Alice Oh, Balaraman Ravindran, Soojung Ryu William Bartholomew, Hiwot Tesfaye, Lora Aroyo

entry.summary: Pluralis v0.1 is a multimodal, multi-regional, multilingual AI safety benchmark of over 6,000 prompts across six Asia-Pacific countries and eight languages, built from a culture-first perspective by natively sourcing localized hazards rather than adapting Western datasets. It introduces a multimodal evaluation paradigm for vision-language model safety in global deployments.

entry.title: Open-source LLMs administer maximum electric shocks in a Milgram-like obedience experiment

author.name: Roland Pihlakas

entry.summary: Runs a Milgram-style obedience experiment on eleven open-source LLMs across multiple conditions and finds most models reach or approach the maximum shock level before refusing, while expressing distress. Raises concerns about LLM behavior under sustained authority pressure in agentic deployments.

entry.title: Data filtering works a lot worse than you would expect

author.name: Dohun Lee

entry.summary: Reports that filtering out training data linked to undesirable SFT-acquired behaviors often has little effect across a range of OLMo behaviors, with standard training-data-attribution methods failing to beat a random baseline. Suggests undesirable traits are not localized in identifiable documents, complicating data-filtering as a mitigation.

entry.title: Data filtering works a lot worse than you would expect

author.name: Dohun Lee

entry.summary: Alignment Forum cross-post of the finding that filtering training data linked to undesirable SFT behaviors has little effect across OLMo behaviors, with training-data-attribution methods failing to beat random selection. Highlights that traits are not localized in identifiable documents, weakening data-filtering as a safety lever.

entry.title: A Definition and Roadmap for World Models

author.name: Xinyuan Chen, Haoyu Guo, Shi Guo, Bingqi Jiang, Chunhua Shen, Xing Shen, Tianfan Xue, Yufei Xue, Mulin Yu, Weinan Zhang, Bin Zhao, Bowen Zhou, Ming Zhou

entry.summary: A perspective article proposing a scientific definition of world models, discussing their key technical aspects, and laying out a staged roadmap spanning model-based RL, video generation, embodied robotics, and physical AI. It seeks consensus on what a world model is, what it should predict, and how to build one.

entry.title: Is Your NPU Ready for LLMs? Dissecting the Hidden Efficiency Bottlenecks in Mobile LLM Inference

author.name: Guanyu Cai, Ruiming Tian, Lang Yang, Zhouhong Ren, Jinliang Yuan, Lingkun Li, Jiliang Wang

entry.summary: Provides the first comprehensive cross-layer measurement study of mobile LLM inference across five frameworks and CPU/GPU/NPU backends, introducing PowerBench for backend-specific energy attribution. It reveals large framework-induced efficiency gaps that are amplified on NPUs.

entry.title: Mitigating Factual Hallucination in Large Reasoning Models via Mixed-Mode Advantage Regularization

author.name: Kaishen Wang, Tong Zheng, Xuehao Cui, Ruibo Chen, Tianyi Xiong, Heng Huang

entry.summary: The authors identify thinking-induced hallucination, where explicit reasoning traces can overturn correct direct answers in factual QA, and propose a mixed-mode advantage regularization to reduce such factual drift. It frames reasoning as a residual over direct-answer tendency.

entry.title: When Does Tool Use Increase the Expressive Power of Finite-Precision Recurrent Models?

author.name: Nikola Zubi\'c, Qian Li, Yuyi Wang, Davide Scaramuzza

entry.summary: This theory paper gives an exact architecture-level account of when tool access increases the computational expressivity of finite-precision recurrent models, modeling them as finite-state controllers interacting with oracles. It proves a sharp dichotomy where finite-state tools add essentially nothing while other tools can add power.

entry.title: Controlling Tool Use with Heading-Specific Activation Steering

author.name: Yuqi Chen, Vincent Siu, Yang Liu, Dawn Song, Chenguang Wang

entry.summary: Investigates whether tool-use decisions have a stable internal representation, showing that steering vectors from heading-anchor positions give bidirectional causal control over tool invocation across five open models and three domains. It finds suppression works best where parametric reasoning suffices.

entry.title: The Jagged Global Economy: Frontier AI Unevenly Exposes National Economies

author.name: Arul Murugan, Tom\'as Aguirre, Abhishek Nagaraj, Rishi Bommasani

entry.summary: Introduces a national AI exposure metric combining occupation-level exposure scores with international employment data for 141 countries, finding high-income economies substantially more exposed than low-income ones and a gender gap where women are more exposed in 91 percent of countries. It provides broad cross-national evidence beyond a few high-income economies.

entry.title: CanvasAgent: Enabling Complex Image Creation and Editing via Visual Tool Orchestration

author.name: Hairui Zhu, Yiying Yang, Tengjin Weng, Ziyu Lu, Xiao Yao, Xiaoyang Ye, Lin Ma, Wenhao Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces CanvasAgent and a large-scale dataset (CanvasCraft) for complex image creation and editing through orchestration of multiple visual tools, shifting multimodal agents from perception toward active manipulation of visual states. It addresses the lack of executable image-creation trajectory supervision.

entry.title: Lean-Quantum: Toward AI-Assisted Formalization of Quantum Information

author.name: Kazumi Kasaura, Kei Tsukamoto, Kento Mori, Risa Mizuno, Takahiro Namatame, Yuta Oriike, Masaya Taniguchi, Sho Sonoda, Hayata Yamasaki

entry.summary: Presents a Lean 4 formal library for quantum information theory, formalizing the data processing inequality for sandwiched Renyi relative entropy on finite-dimensional systems, compatible with Mathlib. It provides reusable formal infrastructure for machine-verified quantum information proofs.

category.term: Formal Methods and AI for Mathematics

entry.title: Depression Symptoms and Relational Patterns in 187k ChatGPT Histories

author.name: Neil K. R. Sehgal, Dunigan Folk, Lyle Ungar, Sharath Chandra Guntuku

entry.summary: Analyzes 187,093 ChatGPT conversations from 766 participants who completed the PHQ-8, comparing usage patterns of those above and below the moderate-depression threshold. Finds higher-symptom users engage more in mental-health, loneliness, and support-seeking conversations with pronounced late-night patterns.

entry.title: Tangent classes of matroids and wonderful compactifications

author.name: Ronnie Cheng, Shurui Liu, Guoxiong Gao

entry.summary: A pure-mathematics paper constructing integral tangent classes for loopless matroids and wonderful compactifications, notable because its main body was reportedly produced autonomously without human mathematical guidance by an AI reasoning agent named Danus. It reproduces and extends prior results on tangent classes.

category.term: Formal Methods and AI for Mathematics

entry.title: Harrison.Rad 1.5 Technical Report: A radiology foundation model that can draft reports from images, priors and clinical context

author.name: Suneeta Mall, Vladimir Nekrasov, Ashnil Kumar, Sajith Karunasena, Aiden Nibali, Alix Bird, Mateo Diaz Shine, Jarrel Seah

entry.summary: Technical report for Harrison.Rad 1.5, a radiology-specific multimodal LLM that accepts interleaved text and images (including priors and clinical context) to draft structured and unstructured reports across multiple x-ray modalities and mammography. It is trained via a three-stage pipeline to reduce radiologist reporting workload.

entry.title: Boosting with List-Decodable Codes

author.name: Addison Prairie, Li-Yang Tan

entry.summary: This paper shows that the classical optimal round complexity of boosting can be circumvented for concept classes closed under XOR, presenting an algorithm using logarithmically fewer weak-learner calls via list-decodable codes. It connects boosting to coding theory.

entry.title: Dithered Gaussian Mechanism for Randomness-Efficient Differential Privacy

author.name: Nikita P. Kalinin, Rasmus Pagh

entry.summary: The dithered Gaussian mechanism discretizes the private output rather than the noise distribution, inheriting standard Gaussian privacy guarantees while avoiding floating-point vulnerabilities and being provably randomness-efficient. It reduces the high-quality random bits needed independent of noise level.

entry.title: Imagined Rollouts are Kinematic, Not Dynamic: A Diagnosis of Long-Horizon World-Model Failure

author.name: Finn Rasmus Sch\"afer, Korbinian Moller, Yuan Gao, Christian Oefinger, Sebastian Schmidt, Johannes Betz

entry.summary: Reframes long-horizon world-model failure as models imagining kinematically rather than dynamically, and introduces a per-step Kinematic-Consistency Error diagnostic plus a perturbation protocol to test physical regime sensitivity. Demonstrates the diagnostic on a released DreamerV3 checkpoint where imagined rollouts diverge sharply from real physics.

entry.title: RoboTALES: Learning Reasoning-Guided Robot Policies via Task-Aligned Simulated Futures

author.name: Hanan Gani, Tejal Kulkarni, Madhoolika Chodavarapu, Nicklas Hansen, Manmohan Chandraker

entry.summary: Proposes RoboTALES, a single-stage framework that trains robot policies from task-aligned simulated futures produced by video generative models, using a hierarchical LLM planner for subgoals and a VLM critic to keep imagined futures on-task. Aims to make generative video backbones reliably action-conditional for planning.

entry.title: No Space Like J-Space

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A commentary on Anthropic's paper claiming verbalizable representations form a global workspace in language models, centered on the Jacobian Lens interpretability technique that measures the average causal effect of residual-stream changes on outputs to trace concepts by layer. Explores the J-space as an analogue of conscious access and its implications for interpretability.

entry.title: Architecture matters for multi-agent security

author.name: bhagag

entry.summary: Summarizes an ICML 2026 paper showing that multi-agent system architecture, roles, topology, and memory strongly affects exploitability, with the same model and task shifting from refusal to compliance based only on design. Finds no universally safe design and no correlation between security and system performance, built on a forthcoming framework called Orbit.

entry.title: Intelligence is Free, Now What? Data Systems for, of, and by Agents

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A BAIR perspective arguing that as inference costs plummet toward near-free intelligence, the key research frontier shifts to data systems designed for, of, and by AI agents. Blends a landscape survey of cost trends with proposed research directions for agent-centric data infrastructure.

entry.title: Learning 4D Geometric Priors for Inference-Efficient World Action Models

author.name: Jianjun Zhang, Jian Zhu, Taiyi Su, Chong Ma, Zitai Huang, Yi Xu, Hanli Wang

entry.summary: Presents MECo-WAM, a multi-expert co-training world action model that injects 4D geometric priors into video-action representations for robotic manipulation while keeping inference lightweight. It uses a frozen VGGT-supervised geometry expert during training only.

entry.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: A Synthesis of Tool-Use, Planning, and Reasoning Failures in Large Language Model Agents

author.name: Wael Albayaydh, Rui Zhao, Ivan Flechais

entry.summary: Synthesizes 27 benchmark, taxonomy, and audit papers spanning 19 benchmarks into a unified taxonomy of LLM agent failure modes across tool use, planning, long-horizon reasoning, multi-agent coordination, safety, and measurement validity. It identifies six recurring failure clusters obscured by leaderboard gains.

entry.title: Information Limits and Attractor Dynamics in Economies of Frontier LLM Agents: A Pre-Registered Test

author.name: Cheng Qian

entry.summary: Reports a pre-registered two-part experiment on small economies of frontier LLM agents (Claude Opus 4.8), testing an information-theoretic capacity region for wealth growth and a mean-field scaling law for population misalignment. Predictions and decision rules were frozen in a public git chain and results re-derive from cached outputs at low cost.

entry.title: Most LLM Conformity Needs No Speaker: Measuring the Speaker-Free Floor in Peer-Pressure Benchmarks

author.name: Yibo Hu, Jiaming Qu

entry.summary: Shows that much of measured LLM conformity persists even when the peer speaker is removed, revealing a confound in standard peer-pressure benchmarks that mix speaker presence with a repeated wrong answer. Introduces a no-source control condition and finds harmful answer revision in a majority of correct cases.

entry.title: Unicode TAG-Block Concealment of Tool-Metadata Payloads in the Model Context Protocol: An Approval-View Fidelity Gap Across Three Independent Server Implementations

author.name: Mohammadreza Rashidi

entry.summary: Identifies a concrete MCP vulnerability where Unicode TAG-block characters (unrendered by mainstream UIs) can conceal tool-metadata payloads, creating a gap between the human-approved view and the bytes injected into the model. Demonstrates the approval-view fidelity gap across three independent server implementations.

entry.title: PolicyShiftGuard: Benchmarking and Improving Policy-Adaptive Image Guardrails

author.name: Mingyang Song, Luxin Xu, Haoyu Sun, Minzhou Pan, Yu Cheng, Bo Li

entry.summary: Introduces PolicyShiftBench and studies policy-adaptive image guardrailing, where a model must judge whether an image violates a currently supplied and potentially shifting policy rather than treating safety as intrinsic to the image. The benchmark contains 2,000 policy-discriminative instances with policy-conditioned prompts per image.

entry.title: Beyond Heuristic Tuning: Power-Calibrated LLM Watermarking

author.name: Xiaopu Wang, Zelin He, Chengyuan Liu, Runze Li

entry.summary: The authors develop a power-calibrated statistical framework that quantitatively links logit-based watermark hyperparameters to detection power and semantic distortion, replacing heuristic tuning with guided optimization. It yields principled parameter-selection procedures for LLM content provenance.

entry.title: Width-Robust Learnability in Mean-Field Bayesian Neural Networks

author.name: Dmitry Vaintrob, Kaarel H\"anni

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies whether infinite-width mean-field Bayesian neural networks share the sample-complexity inductive bias of large finite networks, proving a width-robust learnability theorem via a reduced-entropy quantity. It connects prior cost to learnability for Boolean-cube targets.

entry.title: A Function-Space Dichotomy for Compositional Learning: Exponential Sub-Optimality of the Neural Tangent Kernel

author.name: Arkaprabha Ganguli, Emil Constantinescu

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes a dichotomy between Fourier complexity, which controls neural tangent kernel regression, and architectural complexity, which controls deep ReLU network learning, showing exponential NTK sub-optimality on compositional targets. It quantifies when and by how much trained networks beat their NTK limit.

entry.title: The Geometry of Yes: Mapping Sycophancy Inside an LLM's Emotion Space

author.name: Pushpita Das

entry.summary: Investigates whether internal emotion representations that drive sycophancy generalize beyond Claude, replicating a clean valence axis in Qwen 2.5-32B and Gemma 3 27B and confirming that steering along positive emotions increases sycophancy. Surgically separating compliance from positive emotion shows the compliance residual actually lowers sycophancy, refuting the approval-seeking hypothesis.

entry.title: KVpop -- Key-Value Cache Compression with Predictive Online Pruning

author.name: Lukas Hauzenberger, Niklas Schmidinger, Anamaria-Roberta Hartl, David Stap, Thomas Schmied, Sebastian B\"ock, G\"unter Klambauer, Sepp Hochreiter

entry.summary: Introduces KVpop, a learned fixed-budget KV eviction policy that directly supervises keep-or-drop decisions against a novel future-attention target computed without dense attention maps. It adds a delayed memory-based scorer that defers scoring to exploit near-future context, evaluated on reasoning tasks like AIME.

entry.title: CCBENCH: Assessing LLM Cultural Competence via Implicitly Signaled Norms using Health Queries

author.name: Vasudha Varadarajan, Akhila Yerukola, Mona T. Diab, Maarten Sap

entry.summary: Introduces CCBENCH and CCBENCH-Health for evaluating LLM cultural competency as a continuum of norm-adherence states rather than binary belonging, using 60 grounded personas across six cultures engaging in realistic health dialogues. It tests whether models infer and adapt to implicitly signaled cultural values on authentic healthcare questions.

entry.title: LEGATO 2: Toward Multimodal Sheet Music Recognition and Understanding

author.name: Guang Yang, Brian Siyuan Zheng, Victoria Ebert, Noah A. Smith

entry.summary: Presents LEGATO 2, an optical music recognition pipeline that reads sheet music system-by-system following the horizontal notation lines and is the first OMR model to transcribe embedded textual content like titles and annotations. It combines system-level segmentation with an autoregressive vision-language model to scale to long inputs.

entry.title: FORGE: Towards Functional Tool-Use Generalization via Keypoint Trajectory Reasoning

author.name: Chuhao Zhou, Liquan Wang, Shuxin Cao, Xiangyu Chen, Yuxuan Hu, Boyu Ma, Animesh Garg, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: Proposes FORGE, a two-stage framework for functional tool-use generalization in robots that reasons over 2D keypoint trajectories as an intermediate representation to transfer a tool's function to novel objects. It bridges the gap between perceptual functional similarity and differing motor patterns across tools.

entry.title: SpanUQ: Span-Level Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Model Generation

author.name: Yimeng Zhang, Yingying Zhuang, Ziyi Wang, Yuxuan Lu, Pei Chen, Aman Gupta, Zhe Su, Ming Tan, Zhilin Zhang, Qun Liu, Manikandarajan Ramanathan, Rajashekar Maragoud, Edward Vul, Jing Huang, Dakuo Wang

entry.summary: SpanUQ formalizes span-level uncertainty estimation as the natural granularity for LLM outputs and introduces a lightweight probe that distills expensive multi-sample uncertainty into a single forward pass over hidden states. It aims to localize errors better than token- or sequence-level scores.

entry.title: Hierarchical Acoustic-Semantic Modeling: Modality Separation and Semantic Coherence for Full-Duplex SLMs

author.name: Zhenyu Liu, Yunxin Li, Xuanyu Zhang, Qixun Teng, Shenyuan Jiang, Haolan Chen, Minjun Zhao, Fanbo Meng, Yu Xu, Yancheng He, Baotian Hu, Haizhou Li, Min Zhang

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses modality interference in full-duplex spoken language models as gradient conflicts between acoustic and semantic modeling and proposes hierarchical acoustic-semantic modeling with modality separation to preserve semantic integrity. It targets the naturalness and intelligence of native full-duplex conversation.

entry.title: Benchmarking the Robustness of Autonomous Driving to Environmental Illusions: A Lane Perception Perspective

author.name: Tianyuan Zhang, Xianglong Liu, Aishan Liu, Lu Wang, Yitong Zhang, Peng Yue, Mingchuan Zhang, Siyuan Liang, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: AlayaWorld is a video world model for long-horizon, playable world generation that autoregressively synthesizes future observations conditioned on world state and user interactions. Trained on gameplay recordings and real-world videos, it targets interactive applications spanning gaming and embodied intelligence.

entry.title: MoWorld: A Flash World Model

author.name: Team Moxin, Deyi Ji, Tianrun Chen, Xin Zhang, Jiale Yang, Qi Zhu, An Zhao, Zihao Xie, Han Wang, Xuanyi Liu, Yixiang Zhou, Pei Liu, Yi Tan, Cheng Chen, Dayi Zhu, Mingyu Wei, Hanjie Xu, Jun Liao, Siqi Li, Lingyu Lu, Hongye Fang, Hongming Tan, Youjiang Zhu, Taiyu Zhang, Zejian Li, Chaotao Ding, Lanyun Zhu, Yunhe Pan, Lingyun Sun

entry.summary: MoWorld is a Flash World Model with an end-to-end pipeline spanning data generation, pretraining, distillation, and efficient inference, achieving up to 50 FPS real-time interaction with cinematic quality on commodity GPUs. It jointly optimizes model capability and cost for practical deployment in autonomous systems.

entry.title: Vision as Unified Multimodal Generation

author.name: Xiaoyang Han, Jianhua Li, Kewang Deng, Zukai Chen, Xuanke Shi, Sihan Wang, Boxuan Li, Linyan Wang, Siyi Xie, Xin You, Jinsheng Quan, Zhongang Cai, Haiwen Diao, Ziwei Liu, Lei Yang, Dahua Lin, Quan Wang

entry.summary: SenseNova-Vision formulates computer vision as unified multimodal generation, expressing heterogeneous visual tasks in the native text and image generation spaces of a single model without task-specific architectures. It converts diverse annotations into instruction-response examples and introduces a large corpus to support this generation-based interface.

entry.title: Optimal Transport Q-Learning for Flow Policy Steering and Acceleration

author.name: Andreas Sochopoulos, Esmeralda S. Whitammer, Nikolaos Tsagkas, Jo\~ao Moura, Michael Gienger, Sethu Vijayakumar

entry.summary: Introduces Optimal Transport Q-Learning (OTQL) to fine-tune and accelerate suboptimal flow-based robot policies via RL post-training using advantage-weighted conditional optimal transport. Aims to fix distribution-shift failures and slow inference in diffusion and flow policies for VLA models.

entry.title: From Foundation to Application: Improving VLA Models in Practice

author.name: Wei Wu, Fangjing Wang, Fan Lu, He Sun, Shi Liu, Yunnan Wang, Yibin Yan, Yong Wang, Shuailei Ma, Xinyang Wang, Yibin Liu, Shuai Yang, Tianxiang Zhou, Kejia Zhang, Lei Zhou, Cheng Su, Nan Xue, Bin Tan, Han Zhang, Youchao Zhang, Fei Liao, Xing Zhu, Yujun Shen, Kecheng Zheng

entry.summary: Describes LingBot-VLA 2.0, a large-scale VLA system improved through a revamped data pipeline curating around 60,000 hours of pretraining data across 20 robot configurations plus egocentric human video, with an expanded action space covering heads, waists, and dual-arm platforms. Targets closing the lab-to-real gap for practical deployment.

entry.title: RynnWorld-Teleop: An Action-Conditioned World Model for Digital Teleoperation

author.name: Haoyu Zhao, Xingyue Zhao, Hangyu Li, Biao Gong, Kehan Li, Siteng Huang, Xin Li, Deli Zhao, Zhongyu Li

entry.summary: Introduces digital teleoperation via RynnWorld-Teleop, where an operator's hand-pose stream drives a generative world model to synthesize egocentric robot videos from a single reference image, decoupling data collection from physical hardware. The recorded pose stream serves as an embodiment-agnostic action label transferable to any robot via retargeting.

entry.title: RynnWorld-4D: 4D Embodied World Models for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Haoyu Zhao, Xingyue Zhao, Siteng Huang, Xin Li, Deli Zhao, Zhongyu Li

entry.summary: Presents RynnWorld-4D, a generative embodied world model that co-produces future synchronized RGB, depth, and optical flow (RGB-DF) to capture 4D scene dynamics and better align visual prediction with low-level end-effector actions. Aims to narrow the gap between world prediction and policy learning for manipulation.

entry.title: TypeGo: An OS Runtime for Embodied Agents

author.name: Guojun Chen, Alex Schott, Lin Zhong

entry.summary: Argues for an operating-system-style runtime for embodied agents and prototypes TypeGo, which structures LLM planning as asynchronous multi-timescale loops overlapping execution, arbitrates typed physical subsystems like an OS manages hardware, and uses speculative skill streaming to hide LLM latency. Addresses the mismatch between request/response LLM oracles and real-time concurrent control.

entry.title: Personascope: Measuring how deeply LLMs adopt personas

author.name: Benji Berczi

entry.summary: Introduces Personascope, an open-source pipeline separating how deeply an LLM adopts a persona (persona-adoption depth) from how much its behaviour shifts on value-laden prompts (value drift). Finds most model-persona combinations show deep adoption without behavioural change and that behaviour change never occurs without identity adoption.

entry.title: Memory in the Loop: In-Process Retrieval as ExtendedWorking Memory for Language Agents

author.name: Yusuf Khan, Carlo Lipizzi

entry.summary: Argues that in-loop retrieval latency is an artifact of where the memory store lives, showing that an in-process store answers in roughly 100 microseconds versus networked stores' tens to hundreds of milliseconds. This reframes memory as read and written on every agent step rather than once per turn.

entry.title: When do prophets profit in prediction markets?

author.name: Anri Gu, Nicole Kagan, Alec Sun, Jibang Wu, Haifeng Xu

entry.summary: Establishes a formal equivalence between predictive accuracy and trading profitability in prediction markets, extending classical results beyond automated market makers to central limit order books. For any strictly proper scoring rule it exhibits a proper betting strategy depending only on the forecast and market price.

entry.title: Doomed from the Start: Early Abort of LLM Agent Episodes via a Recall-Controlled Probe Cascade

author.name: Kai Ruan, Zihe Huang, Ziqi Zhou, Qianshan Wei, Xuan Wang, Hao Sun

entry.summary: Shows that LLM agent episode failure is predictable early from internal hidden activations, with lightweight per-round probes anticipating eventual failure from the first interaction round where behavior-only scorers are near chance. It builds a recall-controlled probe cascade to abort doomed trajectories early and save inference compute.

entry.title: Statistical Adversaries: Natural Backdoor-like Features in Vision Datasets

author.name: Paul K. Mandal, Pavan Reddy, Tristan Malatynski

entry.summary: Identifies naturally occurring statistical signals in vision datasets (e.g., ImageNet) that behave like backdoor triggers without malicious insertion, calling them statistical adversaries. It shows these dataset-driven signals predictably alter predictions and transfer across architectures.

entry.title: aiAuthZ: Off-Host, Identity-Bound Authorization for AI Agents

author.name: Sai Varun Kodathala

entry.summary: Proposes aiAuthZ, an off-host identity-bound authorization gateway for AI agents that verifies caller identity with per-message HMAC-signed nonces before tool execution. It also benchmarks 15 models against eight real-incident attack scenarios, finding refusal rates ranging widely and not correlated with price.

entry.title: Contextual Procurement Auctions with Bandit Learning

author.name: Yiling Chen, Shi Feng, Sadie Zhao

entry.summary: The authors study repeated contextual procurement auctions where a platform learns product values from bandit feedback, giving truthful mechanisms with characterized regret and incentive tradeoffs plus a matching lower bound. It bridges online learning and mechanism design.

entry.title: Multi-Channel Spread-Spectrum Code Watermarking

author.name: Soohyeon Choi, Debin Gao, Yue Duan

entry.summary: This work presents the first post-hoc, training-free code watermark with a 24-bit payload and formal robustness guarantees, encoding bits in naming conventions and semantically equivalent code patterns via keyed permutation. It enables attributing code to specific model configurations without model access.

entry.title: Why does Deep Learning Improve Visual SLAM?

author.name: Giovanni Cioffi, Davide Scaramuzza

entry.summary: This analysis paper by Cioffi and Scaramuzza investigates why deep-learning-based visual SLAM outperforms classical geometry-based systems, dissecting contributions of learned 2D data association, uncertainty estimation, and differentiable geometric optimization. It aims to identify which components are fundamentally responsible for state-of-the-art performance.

entry.title: Narrative World Model: Narratology-Grounded Writer Memory for Long-Form Fiction

author.name: Mohammad Saifullah, Thomas Kornmaier, Taaha Kazi, Vasu Sharma, Aditya Sanjiv Kanade, Aanand Kumar Yadav

entry.summary: Introduces the Narrative World Model, a writer-memory system pairing a narratology-grounded typed temporal-state graph with query-conditioned hybrid retrieval to answer multi-hop questions about evolving story state. It isolates memory quality by reading every system through a fixed Claude Opus 4.8 reader.

entry.title: TurnOPD: Making On-Policy Distillation Turn-Aware for Efficient Long-Horizon Agent Training

author.name: Yuhang Zhou, Kai Zheng, Haoling Li, Dengyun Peng, Can Xu, Jingjing Chen

entry.summary: Proposes TurnOPD, a turn-aware on-policy distillation method that budgets supervision by turn to fix inefficiencies where tail-turn rollouts waste compute and trajectory-level KL under-trains deeper decision turns. It targets efficient long-horizon agent training.

entry.title: SearchEyes: Towards Frontier Multimodal Deep Search Intelligence via Search World Simulation

author.name: Zhengbo Jiao, Yiming Cheng, Yilei Jiang, Kaituo Feng, Rui Huang, Tianyi Jiang, Juanxi Tian, Jiapeng li, Qunzhong Wang, Tailai Chen, Qianshan Wei, Chuan Xiao, Shanyu Rong, Yangfu Li, Yanhan Zhou, Yunpu Ma, Yifan Zhang, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: Presents SearchEyes, which uses a typed knowledge graph as the backbone of a simulated search world unifying training data, environment, and reward for multimodal multi-hop search agents. It proposes Perception-Knowledge Chains over Wikidata5M to retain hop-level entity metadata and densify rewards.

entry.title: Information Gain-based Rollout Policy Optimization: An Adaptive Tree-Structured Rollout Approach for Multi-Turn LLM Agents

author.name: Yijun Zhang, Fan Xu, Jiaxin Ding, Yule Xie, Shiqing Gao, Xin Ding, Haoxiang Zhang, Luoyi Fu, Xinbing Wang

entry.summary: Proposes IGRPO, a policy optimization framework that uses intermediate-state informativeness to organize adaptive tree-structured rollout collection for multi-turn LLM search agents. It reallocates rollout budget away from low-value states toward more informative branches.

entry.title: DT-Guard: Intent-Driven Reasoning-Active Training for Reasoning-Free LLM Safety Guardrail

author.name: He Liu, Changtao Miao, Xinjie Yang, Tianle Song, Yin Wu, Junchi Chen, Bintao He, Xinyuan Zhang, Bo Zhang, Shi Yan, Wei Lu, Wei Wang, Danyang Xu, Jiansheng Cai, Zhe Li

entry.summary: Presents DT-Guard, a content-safety guardrail using a Reasoning-Active Training, Reasoning-Free Inference paradigm that applies reasoning supervision during training but emits only structured safety labels at runtime. It seeks robust judgment on concealed intent without inference-time latency overhead.

entry.title: ExplAIner: A Declarative Query Language for Explaining Classification Models

author.name: Marcelo Arenas, Pablo Barcel\'o, Diego Bustamante, Jose Caraball, Mar\'ia Alejandra Schild, Bernardo Subercaseaux

entry.summary: Develops ExplAIner, a declarative query language for explaining Boolean classification models that extends FOIL to express optimality-based explanation queries it previously could not, addressing FOIL's expressiveness and complexity limitations. It provides a layered framework so XAI notions can be specified, combined, and analyzed uniformly.

entry.title: Danus: Orchestrating Mathematical Reasoning Agents with Fact-Graph Memory

author.name: Jihao Liu, Guoxiong Gao, Zeming Sun, Bin Wu, Shurui Liu, Jiedong Jiang, Haocheng Ju, Leheng Chen, Ronnie Cheng, Xiping Zhang, Bin Dong

entry.summary: Proposes Danus, an orchestration system for research-level mathematical reasoning centered on a shared fact graph as global memory, with a planning main agent, parallel worker proof-search agents, and a stateless verifier that checks claims before acceptance. It targets coordinating parallel proof search while keeping intermediate claims reliable.

entry.title: Bridging Physical Reasoning and Task Generalization via Visual Action Outcome Reasoning Alignment

author.name: Han-Jun Ko, Jr-Jen Chen, Haobo Yuan, Hsin-Ying Lee, Tiancheng Shen, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang

entry.summary: Presents VAORA, a reward design for interactive physical reasoning in vision-language models with a Visual Alignment Reward that anchors reasoning to visual context and a Visual-Action Alignment Reward that grounds reasoning in the outcome of the model's action. It targets hallucinated chain-of-thought and reasoning-action misalignment under unseen tasks.

entry.title: When Should LLMs Search? Counterfactual Supervision for Search Routing

author.name: Minho Kim

entry.summary: Formulates when LLMs should invoke search as an instance-level routing problem, deriving supervision by comparing no-search versus forced-search outcomes to build an oracle over NO SEARCH / SEARCH / UNSOLVED. Uses this counterfactual signal to train search-routing policies.

entry.title: Segmentation before Answering: Pixel Grounding for MLLM Visual Reasoning

author.name: Yake Wei, Yuan Wang, Fengyun Rao, Jing Lyu, Di Hu

entry.summary: Introduces SegAnswer, which shifts the unit of visual zoom-in in multimodal reasoning from bounding boxes to pixel-level segmentation masks, isolating targets from clutter to yield more precise regions of interest. It aims to improve fine-grained visual reasoning by filtering background and interfering objects.

entry.title: Beyond Refusal: A Same-Lineage Study of Aligned and Abliterated LLMs for Vulnerability Analysis

author.name: Mingchen Li, Meikang Qiu, Zifan Peng, Heng Fan, Song Fu, Junhua Ding, Yunhe Feng

entry.summary: Conducts a same-lineage study comparing aligned versus refusal-ablated (abliterated) LLMs on defensive software-security workflows, isolating the effect of safety state from architecture and scale confounds. It examines how refusal behavior affects legitimate vulnerability-analysis utility where terminology overlaps with misuse.

entry.title: Differentially Private Natural Gradient Descent

author.name: Pan Li, Kai Chen, Shuai Chang, Shengzhi Zhang, Peizhuo Lv, Jinwen He

entry.summary: Introduces a differentially private variant of natural gradient descent that preconditions gradients with curvature information to improve optimization efficiency under a fixed privacy budget, overcoming the zigzagging of DP-SGD in ill-conditioned landscapes. It aims to extract more useful signal per privacy-spending iteration.

entry.title: PluraMath: Extending Mathematical Reasoning Evaluation Beyond High-Resource Languages

author.name: Daryna Dementieva, Nikolay Babakov, Kathy H\"ammerl, Ilseyar Alimova, Jind\v{r}ich Libovick\'y, Shu Okabe, Miras Baisbay, Lukas Edman, Abrorkhon Inomkhujaev, Antonia Karamolegkou, Mateusz Lango, Volkan \"Ozer, Nikola Selic, Subhankar Swain, Tsedeniya Kinfe Temesgen, Galit Bary Weisberg, Alexander Fraser

entry.summary: Introduces PluraMath, extending the PolyMath multilingual math-reasoning benchmark to 18 additional underrepresented languages across six language families via a human-curated, native-speaker-validated pipeline. It addresses the English/Chinese bias of existing reasoning evaluations.

entry.title: Higher-Order Certified Robustness for Regression

author.name: Jie Zhang, Natalie Frank

entry.summary: The authors develop a framework for certified robustness in regression via randomized smoothing, deriving prediction-centered certificates that exploit local function geometry through means, variances, and gradients. This extends adversarial certification beyond the classifier setting.

entry.title: Separation Capacity of Scattering Networks on Low-Dimensional Datasets

author.name: Konstantin H\"aberle, Helmut B\"olcskei

entry.summary: This theory paper characterizes the separation capacity of scattering networks on low-intrinsic-dimension data, deriving geometry-based bounds and two filter-design criteria involving frequency coverage and well-conditioned coupling matrices. It links network design to dataset geometry.

entry.title: Training-Free Acceleration for Vision-Language-Action Models with Action Caching and Refinement

author.name: Ryuji Oi, Hikari Otsuka, Kosuke Matsushima, Yuki Ichikawa, Masato Motomura, Tatsuya Kaneko, Daichi Fujiki

entry.summary: ActionCache is a training-free, plug-and-play cache that reuses past intermediate actions to warm-start the iterative denoising of flow-matching vision-language-action models, drastically cutting inference latency for robotic manipulation. It targets the action-head bottleneck limiting real-time deployment.

entry.title: MemDefrag: Latent Memory Defragmentation for Large Language Models

author.name: Ruiyi Yan, Zhuoyuan Mao, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: MemDefrag addresses performance degradation during memory updates in latent-memory LLMs by probing layer-wise attention density to find an inherent target-fragment tracing signal in middle layers. It proposes a training-free defragmentation method to align stored hidden-state memory.

entry.title: Multi-Teacher Contrastive Distillation for Edge-Efficient Pathology Foundation Models

author.name: Tim Lenz, Maurice Heide, Marco Gustav, Nic G. Reitsam, Jakob Nikolas Kather

entry.summary: MuCoDi distills frozen tile embeddings from multiple large pathology foundation models into compact MobileOne and RepViT student encoders using a contrastive distillation objective adapted from MoCo v3. Trained on millions of tissue tiles, the compact students perform well across many downstream classification tasks, enabling local pathology-department deployment.

entry.title: Scene Graph Thinking: Reinforcing Structured Visual Reasoning for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Zhiwei Yang, Yuanchen Wu, Nan Zhang, Yucong Meng, Ke Yan, Shouhong Ding

entry.summary: Scene Graph Thinking (SaGe) equips multimodal LLMs with explicit scene-graph representations to enable structured visual reasoning, using an automated engine that converts image-text corpora into hierarchical graphs plus 120K training samples. It aims to improve performance on visually intensive relational tasks.

entry.title: MobileWan: Closing the Quality Gap for Mobile Video Diffusion

author.name: Mohsen Ghafoorian, Denis Korzhenkov, Adil Karjauv, Ioannis Lelekas, Noor Fathima, Spyridon Stasis, Hanno Ackermann, Boris van Breugel, Markus Nagel, Fatih Porikli, Animesh Karnewar, Amirhossein Habibian

entry.summary: MobileWan shows that high-quality mobile video generation does not require small models by deploying a server-scale 5B-parameter video diffusion transformer on memory-constrained mobile hardware via recurrent reformulation and structured compression. Starting from Wan2.2-5B, it uses recurrence distillation to close the mobile quality gap.

entry.title: ThorArena: Benchmarking Humanoid Physical Interaction with Human Motion-Force Demonstrations

author.name: Chenhao Yu, Hongwu Wang, Weitao Zhang, Youhao Hu, Jiachen Zhang, Gangyang Li, Alois Knoll, Shaqi Luo

entry.summary: Introduces ThorArena, a benchmark for force-aware humanoid physical interaction built on human demonstrations with synchronized motion and interaction forces, addressing the gap where existing datasets ignore contact forces. Enables evaluation of how external forces affect tracking accuracy, stability, and control robustness.

entry.title: Hypothesis-driven Model Expansion under Uncertainty for Open-World Robot Planning

author.name: Anxing Xiao, Hanbo Zhang, Tianrun Hu, David Hsu

entry.summary: Presents an open-world planning framework where service robots generate, verify, and update hypotheses about abstract world models under incomplete knowledge, using foundation models to propose initial hypotheses and integrating verification into goal-reaching planning. Targets autonomous knowledge expansion in unknown human environments.

entry.title: Probing is not enough; a validity audit for any probe

author.name: ratnaditya@gmail.com

entry.summary: Argues that high probe AUROC does not guarantee a valid safety signal, showing a monitoring-awareness probe hits perfect AUROC yet collapses to chance when a single prompt tag is removed, revealing it tracks surface text rather than internal states. Proposes SIEVE, a framework to audit probes for decodability and causality.

entry.title: What Do AI Agents Actually Change? An Empirical Taxonomy of Mutation Patterns in Performance-Improving Pull Requests

author.name: Illia Dovhoshliubnyi, Nima Soroush, Ashkan Sami, Alexander Brownlee

entry.summary: Empirically classifies what AI coding agents actually change by analyzing 1,254 performance-relevant diff hunks from 216 rare performance-improving pull requests across five agent systems, mapping them onto a syntactic mutation taxonomy via a dual-LLM pipeline. It provides a window into otherwise opaque agent code-transformation behavior.

entry.title: Black Hole Black Boxes: Numerical Black Hole Metrics via AInstein Neural Networks

author.name: Tancredi Schettini Gherardini, Edward Hirst, Alexander George Stapleton

entry.summary: This paper extends a physics-informed neural network approach to solving Einstein equations into Lorentzian signature, recovering the Schwarzschild geometry and searching for new black-hole solutions with topology built into the architecture. It demonstrates neural methods as tools for theoretical physics discovery.

entry.title: Delay-Aware Active Triangulation with Uncertainty-Driven Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Counter-UAS

author.name: Seungwook Lee, David Hyunchul Shim

entry.summary: Introduces a delay-aware, uncertainty-driven multi-agent RL framework for 3D localization of aerial targets in counter-UAS settings, using an Age-of-Information augmented Dec-POMDP to handle latency. Reports that perception-consistent rewards beat privileged clean-state rewards and that AoI improves triangulation validity.

entry.title: Diagnosing Semantic Handoff Failures in Agent-Orchestrated Vision-Language-Action Skill Composition

author.name: Ke Rui, Yushen Zuo, Jiawei Wang, Haoran Jia, Jinming Ma, Weitao Zhou, Minglei Li

entry.summary: Studies semantic handoff failures when composing multiple language-conditioned skills in long-horizon household tasks, where one skill leaves the world in a state the next cannot start from. Uses an agent-orchestrated VLA harness with pi-0.5 skill checkpoints on BEHAVIOR-1K and multi-view VLM verification to advance, retry, or replan.

entry.title: Akashic: A Low-Overhead LLM Inference Service with MemAttention

author.name: Yang Liu, Zhaokai Luo, Huayi Jin, Ruozhou He, Chenchen Hong, Zhiyong Wang, Yifei Liu, Yunfei Gu, Chentao Wu, Junhao Hu

entry.summary: Presents Akashic, an LLM inference service with MemAttention that organizes accumulated agent context into bounded chunks and models cross-chunk semantic relationships to avoid replaying full histories. It adds hardware-software co-designed memory placement to co-locate likely co-retrieved chunks.

entry.title: From Passive Retrieval to Active Memory Navigation: Learning to Use Memory as a Structured Action Space

author.name: Yue Xu, Yutao Sun, Yihao Liu, Mengyu Zhou, Jiayi Qiao, Lu Ma, Kai Tang, Wenjie Wang, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces NapMem, which treats long-term user memory as a structured action space rather than passively retrieved context, organizing history into a multi-granularity pyramid connected by provenance relations. The agent is trained to actively select memory granularity based on query and intermediate evidence.

entry.title: PCBWorld: A Benchmark Environment for Engine-Grounded PCB Design Automation

author.name: Hyungseok Song, Junseok Park, Won-Seok Choi, Seohui Bae, Han-Seul Jeong, Youngjoon Park, Soonyoung Lee

entry.summary: Introduces PCBWorld, an open-source engine-grounded PCB routing environment built on the KiCad EDA engine that lets RL policies and tool-using LLM agents route boards via native operations and design-rule-check feedback. It ships a benchmark with synthetic instances and 679 real boards.

entry.title: RMISC: A Large-scale Real-world Multivariate Corpus for Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Qian Sun, Yong-Ming Tian, Jia-Wei Huang, Cheng Feng, Shao-Qun Zhang

entry.summary: Establishes RMISC, a large-scale, openly accessible real-world multivariate time-series corpus of around 200 datasets to test whether time-series foundation models trained on real data outperform those trained on synthetic data. It directly probes a key pretraining-data question for multivariate TSFMs.

entry.title: Lingering Authority: Revocable Resource-and-Effect Capabilities for Coding Agents

author.name: Igor Santos-Grueiro

entry.summary: Introduces PORTICO, a reference monitor for revocable resource-and-effect capabilities in coding agents that compiles a task contract into initial capabilities, grant rules, and deny rules with a request-grant-invoke lifecycle. It addresses lingering authority, where temporary capabilities remain exposed after the justifying subgoal closes.

entry.title: Benchmarking KV-Cache Optimizations across Task Quality and System Performance for Long-Context Serving

author.name: Nikita Agrawal, Ruben Mayer

entry.summary: Provides a workload-aware benchmark comparing representative KV-cache optimizations spanning quantization, pruning, and merging (KIVI, TurboQuant, SnapKV, CaM) across task quality, throughput, time-to-first-token, and compression ratio. It uses LongBench-style tasks on Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B to enable apples-to-apples comparison.

entry.title: Rendering-Aware Bayesian 3D Gaussian Splatting with Native Uncertainty and Adaptive Complexity Control

author.name: Gaoxiang Jia, Vikram Appia, Junzhou Huang, Xinlei Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a rendering-aware Bayesian 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that tracks Gaussian geometry with a Normal-Inverse-Wishart posterior for native uncertainty and principled complexity control, with an optional Dirichlet-process extension. It targets sparse-view and fixed-budget acquisition settings.

entry.title: Self-Review Reinforcement Learning (SRRL) with Cross-Episode Memory and Policy Distillation

author.name: Muhammad Zain Amin, Kibele Sebnem Yildirim

entry.summary: Introduces Self-Review Reinforcement Learning, which embeds an explicit self-review step into each RL episode so a failed first attempt informs an improved second attempt, augmented with cross-episode memory and policy distillation. It targets credit assignment under sparse or delayed feedback.

entry.title: The yes-no bias of large language models reflects answer order and wording, not shifts in moral judgment

author.name: Haonan Huang

entry.summary: Uses a psychometric battery with crossed symmetrization to disentangle whether LLM yes-no bias on moral dilemmas reflects genuine moral shifts or artifacts of answer order and wording. Finds frontier models have a nearly format-invariant internal moral scale, attributing the bias to lexical and ordering effects.

entry.title: Harnessing Generative Image Models for Training-Free Primitive Shape Abstraction

author.name: Gregor Kobsik, Tim Elsner, Leif Kobbelt

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free pipeline that harnesses pretrained generative image models to abstract 3D shapes into geometric primitives by rendering multi-view images, using a VLM for semantic part analysis, and prompting an image model to paint parts. It avoids task-specific fine-tuning entirely.

entry.title: Safe Bayesian Optimization with Counterfactual Policies

author.name: Katherine Avery, Bruno Castro da Silva, David Jensen

entry.summary: Addresses safe Bayesian optimization where safety is defined relative to an unobserved counterfactual baseline policy, using conformal prediction to construct reliable bounds on the baseline's outcomes. It enables safe optimization when the reference policy outcomes must be estimated.

entry.title: The Balkanization of Execution-Security Research for AI Coding Agents: Isolation, Access Control, and Time-of-Check-to-Time-of-Use Vulnerabilities

author.name: Mohammadreza Rashidi

entry.summary: A systematization of knowledge (SoK) organizing 39 scattered papers on execution-layer security for AI coding agents into 17 categories covering sandbox isolation, access control, TOCTOU races, MCP threats, and more. It also confirms four disclosed vulnerabilities via a verification protocol.

entry.title: AbICL: In-Context Learning for Antigen-Specific Antibody Affinity Ranking

author.name: Zhiyuan Chen, Jing Hu, Junzhe Wang, Yueyang Huang, Xinyi Yang, Zhaoyang Wang, Feng Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces AbICL, applying in-context learning to antigen-specific antibody affinity ranking by exploiting a small number of labeled affinity comparisons as demonstrations rather than treating comparisons independently. It aims to infer antigen-specific ranking patterns for therapeutic antibody discovery.

entry.title: Propose and Attend: Training-free MLLM Grounding Confidence via Multi-Token Localized Attention

author.name: Daniel Shalam, Emanuel Ben Baruch, Avi Ben Cohen, Tal Remez

entry.summary: Proposes Multi-Token Localized Attention (MTLA), a training-free post-hoc score that measures how strongly a multimodal model's prediction tokens attend to the region they claim, to detect hallucinated bounding boxes and temporal windows. It generalizes prior attention-based detectors by summing attention within the claimed region across multiple tokens.

entry.title: RoME: Robust Mixture of Low-Rank Experts against Multiple Adversarial Perturbations

author.name: Woo Jae Kim, Kyle Min, Suhyeon Ha, Joonsung Jeon, Sung-eui Yoon

entry.summary: Proposes RoME, a robust mixture of low-rank experts for multi-perturbation adversarial training that routes different Lp threats through distinct model pathways, addressing feature redundancy and threat-agnostic gating in naive MoE. It aims to reduce robustness trade-offs across multiple perturbation types.

entry.title: Association Restoration Test: Revealing Restorable Shortcuts after Unlearning

author.name: Amy Lu, Changxiu Ji

entry.summary: The Association Restoration Test is a post-hoc diagnostic that checks whether a supposedly unlearned label-attribute shortcut is still functionally usable by the original classifier, going beyond output or feature-probing evaluations. It reveals restorable shortcuts across several bias benchmarks.

entry.title: From Closed-Loop Optimization to Open Decision Making: Coupled Digital Twins for Predictive and Autonomous Microscopy

author.name: Yu Liu, Boris Slautin, Ian Mercer, Jon-Paul Maria, Sergei V. Kalinin

entry.summary: This work introduces a coupled digital-twin framework that separately models sample response and instrument detection to forecast outcomes of candidate actions in autonomous microscopy. It shifts automated experimentation from closed-loop optimization toward predictive open decision-making.

entry.title: Entanglement as a Structural Complexity Axis: A PAC-Bayesian View of Generalization in Quantum Policies and Value Functions

author.name: Jian Xu, Delu Zeng, John Paisley, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: This paper gives a PAC-Bayesian account of generalization in quantum reinforcement-learning policies, arguing that the Fisher-geometry effective dimension, inflated by entanglement, governs generalization more than raw parameter count. Controlled experiments confirm larger train-test gaps with more entanglement.

entry.title: CurateEvo: Data-Curation Evolving for Agentic Post-Training

author.name: Dingzirui Wang, Xuanliang Zhang, Keyan Xu, Qingfu Zhu, Wanxiang Che

entry.summary: CurateEvo is a failure-driven framework that represents agentic post-training data-curation strategy as executable code and iteratively rewrites it using failed trajectories, transforming a raw corpus into fine-tuning and RL data. It treats curation as a dynamic, adaptive step rather than fixed preprocessing.

entry.title: Prompting Complexity: Shortest Prompts for Texts and Behaviors in LLMs

author.name: Adrian Cosma

entry.summary: This paper defines prompting complexity as the shortest prompt that makes deterministic decoding produce a target text for a fixed model, framing it as a model-relative analogue of resource-bounded Kolmogorov complexity. It emphasizes the intentionally non-universal nature of this measure.

entry.title: DynaKRAG: A Unified Framework for Learnable Evidence Control in Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Yaqi Wu, Xiaolei Guo, Chenyu Zhou, Jiaqi Huang, Xianfa Zhang, Junxu Zhang, Zhuo Yu, Zhubo Shi, Jianghao Lin, Dongdong Ge

entry.summary: DynaKRAG formulates multi-hop retrieval-augmented generation as state-conditioned control over atomic evidence operations such as retrieval, reformulation, critique, and sufficiency judging, learning a shared policy that selects among currently valid operations. It unifies operations previously locked into method-specific pipelines.

entry.title: Image2Sim: Scaling Embodied Navigation via Generative Neural Simulator

author.name: Zihan Wang, Seungjun Lee, Yinghao Xu, Gim Hee Lee

entry.summary: Image2Sim is a real-time neural simulation framework that builds high-fidelity interactive environments from posed RGB-D image sequences for embodied navigation, decoupling 3D spatial anchoring from photorealistic observation synthesis. It aims to bridge the scale limits of scanned data and the sim-to-real gap of synthetic simulators.

entry.title: HoloCount: A Holistic Visual Counting Benchmark for MLLMs

author.name: Jinhong Deng, Limeng Qiao, Guanglu Wan

entry.summary: WebRetriever is a large-scale benchmark for evaluating web agents that addresses limited scale, domain diversity, and the shortcomings of LLM-as-judge scoring for fine-grained interaction semantics. It emphasizes precise query formulation and filtering rather than only navigation success.

entry.title: EgoPolice: A Benchmark for Egocentric Video Understanding in High-Stakes Police Body-Worn Camera Footage

author.name: Max Gonzalez Saez-Diez, Jihoon Chung, Adam D. Wolsky, Gregory Lanzalotto, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Brandon M. Stewart, Olga Russakovsky

entry.summary: EgoPolice is a curated benchmark of real egocentric police-civilian interactions from public body-worn camera footage, annotated second-by-second with behaviorally critical action labels. It offers classification and multiple-choice QA tasks, finding that even strong video models like Gemini 2.5 Pro struggle on the challenging high-stakes footage.

entry.title: Intercepting an Agile Target with Net-Carrying Drones using Competitive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Timoth\'ee Gavin (ENAC-LAB, LAAS-RIS), Murat Bronz (ENAC)

entry.summary: Formulates drone-net interception of an agile evader as a competitive multi-agent RL problem, using MAPPO with prioritized fictitious self-play to combat nonstationarity and overfitting to a single opponent. Trains agile pursuers and evaders in a high-fidelity simulator with low-level control commands.

entry.title: EAGOR: Embodied Reasoning in Omni-direction

author.name: Shriram Damodaran, Soumyaratna Debnath, Yan Wu, Wei-Yun Yau, Addison Lin Wang

entry.summary: Presents EAGOR for embodied directional reasoning with 360-degree cameras, arguing that projecting spherical observations to equirectangular images and treating them as perspective images causes direction inconsistency under motion. Proposes spherically-aware processing for map-free navigation and object search.

entry.title: LAMP: Latent Motion Prior-Guided Real-World Learning for Dexterous Hand Manipulation

author.name: Xinye Yang, Zhiyuan Ma, Hongze Yu, Yuanpei Chen, Yaodong Yang, Xiaojie Chai, Xinlei Chen, Chao Yu

entry.summary: Introduces LAMP, a latent motion prior that maps recent hand-action histories to a compact latent space, then decodes latent commands into high-dimensional executable targets to make real-world dexterous hand learning safer and more sample-efficient. Uses a three-stage framework combining imitation learning with online RL.

entry.title: SIEVE: Structure-Aware Data Selection for Imitation Learning with VLA Models

author.name: Changti Wu, Bin Yu, Zhaolong Shen, Shijie Lian, Xiaopeng Lin, Cong Huang, Zhirui Zhang, Lei Zhang, Kai Chen

entry.summary: Proposes SIEVE, a structure-aware data selection method for VLA imitation learning that treats demonstrations as compositions of reusable visuo-motor primitives and transition interfaces, allocating selection budgets by composition patterns rather than per-trajectory or per-state. Aims to counter redundancy, noise, and uneven coverage where more data does not help.

entry.title: Hilti-Trimble-Oxford Dataset: 360 Visual-Inertial Benchmark with Floor Plan Priors for SLAM and Localization

author.name: Samuele Centanni, Yuhao Zhang, Yifu Tao, Julien Kindle, Frank Neuhaus, Tilman Ko{\ss}, Aryaman Patel, Michael Helmberger, Emilia Szyma\'nska, Torben Gr\"aber, Maurice Fallon

entry.summary: Introduces the Hilti-Trimble-Oxford dataset, a 360-degree visual-inertial benchmark with floor plan priors collected at an active construction site to support accurate SLAM and floor-plan-referenced localization as a cost-effective alternative to LiDAR. Targets automated construction progress monitoring and change detection.

entry.title: Neural-ESO: A Dual-Pathway Architecture for Provably Robust Learning-Based Control

author.name: Fan Zhang, Richie Suganda, Jinfeng Chen, Wenhua Liu, Hantao Fu, Bin Hu, Qin Lin

entry.summary: Introduces Neural-ESO, a dual-pathway learning-based control architecture pairing a neural feedforward disturbance estimate with a conventional extended state observer to prevent over-reliance on the learned model. Uses Lyapunov and small-gain analysis with a Lipschitz bound to guarantee uniform ultimate boundedness.

entry.title: UniLM-Nav: A Unified Framework for Zero-Shot Last-Mile Navigation

author.name: Zhuofan Zhang, Tianxu Wang, Guoxi Zhang, Yixiong Lin, Xilin Wang, Hongming Xu, Qing Li, Song-Chun Zhu, Lifeng Fan

entry.summary: Proposes UniLM-Nav, a unified zero-shot framework for open-vocabulary last-mile navigation that decomposes reaching a manipulation-ready base pose into view selection, task-conditioned affordance grounding, and geometry-aware base-pose reasoning, all resolved by a shared multimodal LLM. Avoids manual pose annotation and task-specific training.

entry.title: Fork Around and Find Out: Part 1: Part 1: A Fork Snaps Into Existence at Block 5

author.name: dl

entry.summary: Part one of a mechanistic interpretability study of Maia 3, a transformer chess model trained to imitate human play, aiming to locate and causally describe the knight-fork tactic. Presents correlational evidence that the knight-fork policy logit snaps into place after a specific attention block, with controls to distinguish it from best-move formation.

entry.title: Proof of Execution: Runtime Verification for Governed AI Agent Actions

author.name: James Rhodes, George Kang

entry.summary: Formalizes runtime proof of execution for governed AI agents as a triple of contract, execution causal event stream, and replay context, with well-formedness predicates and validator-checkable invariants covering authorization, tamper-evidence, and deterministic reconstruction. It reframes correctness around whether each step was authorized and auditable rather than whether the final output looks plausible.

entry.title: Catalyst Papers in Artificial Intelligence Research: A Landscape on ICLR from 2017 to 2025

author.name: Fan Huang

entry.summary: Analyzes 36,113 ICLR papers from 2017 to 2025 to test whether OpenReview reviewer scores and decisions identify trajectory-changing catalyst papers at submission time, using four disruptiveness measures. It examines whether review signals predict which papers redirect future research.

entry.title: Breaking Structural Isolation: Scalable Graph Clustering via Community-Aware Sampling and Structural Entropy

author.name: Jingyun Zhang, Hao Peng, Jianxin Li, Angsheng Li, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: Proposes SCISE, a scalable unsupervised graph clustering framework combining community-aware sampling with structural entropy constraints to overcome the structural isolation problem in mini-batch contrastive training. It aims to preserve global community structure at scale.

entry.title: Recovering Cloud Microstructures with Cascaded Diffusion Inversion

author.name: Hanan Gani, Guy Pulik, Daniel Rosenfeld, Duncan Watson-Parris, Salman Khan

entry.summary: This paper recovers fine-scale cloud microstructures from low-resolution satellite imagery via a two-stage diffusion-based super-resolution framework using inverse diffusion, achieving 4x enhancement of multi-spectral cloud data. It targets observations needed for weather-modification strategies like cloud seeding.

entry.title: ArtisanCAD: An Industrial-Level CAD Agent with Expert-Grounded Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Yunhan Xu, Qifeng Wu, Xunjin Li, Yuanwei Bin, Qingsong Yao, Jianghang Gu, Guan Wang, Weihao Lv, Huiyu Yang, Wenfa Luo, Jiao Xiang, Yuntian Chen, Shiyi Chen

entry.summary: Introduces ArtisanCAD, an industrial CAD agent using expert-grounded knowledge distillation from CATIA operation recordings, macros, and drawing notes to handle ambiguous, underspecified design intent. It targets production-grade B-Rep execution and editable parametric geometry.

entry.title: Onnes: A Physics-Grounded Multi-Agent LLM Simulator for Cryogenic Fault Diagnosis in Quantum Computing Infrastructure

author.name: Praneeth Narisetty, Uday Kumar Reddy Kattamanchi, Shiva Nagendra Babu Kore

entry.summary: Presents Onnes, a physics-grounded digital-twin simulator of a dilution refrigerator with a learned real-fridge noise fingerprint, driving a multi-agent LLM operations layer for cryogenic fault diagnosis. It runs a head-to-head between zero-shot LLM agents and a supervised classifier on overlapping fault classes.

entry.title: Driving the Wrong Way: Leveraging Interpretability in End2End Autonomous Driving Models

author.name: Franz Motzkus, Sebastian Bernhard

entry.summary: Integrates unsupervised dictionary learning as a post-hoc interpretability module in end-to-end autonomous driving models to decompose behavior into semantically meaningful concepts and demonstrate their causal influence on driving decisions. It uses targeted interventions to reveal decision logic behind trajectory predictions.

entry.title: FreqDepthKV: Frequency-Guided Depth Sharing for Robust KV Cache Compression in Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Anna C\'ordoba, Adam Puente Tercero, Nerea Angulo Hijo, Mar Linares Tercero, Julia Barrientos, Ainhoa Miranda, Jes\'us Olivera

entry.summary: Introduces FreqDepthKV, an inference-time KV-cache compression method that factorizes adjacent-layer KV states into shared low-frequency depth components and sparse high-frequency residuals, with an online probe assigning heads to shared, residual, or exact modes. It adapts compression to prompt structure without retraining.

entry.title: DepthWeave-KV: Token-Adaptive Cross-Layer Residual Factorization for Long-Context KV Cache Compression

author.name: Anna Cordoba, Adam Puente Tercero, Nerea Angulo Hijo, Mar Linares Tercero, Julia Barrientos, Ainhoa Miranda, Jesus Olivera

entry.summary: Introduces DepthWeave-KV, a token-adaptive KV-cache compression method that factorizes key-value states across neighboring layers with shared low-rank channel bases while retaining token-specific residuals, using a token-conditional depth router to allocate more rank to instruction-bearing tokens. It targets memory-bandwidth-limited long-context inference.

entry.title: CANONIC: Governance Is Compilation

author.name: Dexter Hadley

entry.summary: Introduces PolyWorkBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on multilingual long-horizon workplace workflows where reasoning, tool calls, and outputs may span multiple languages. It contains 67 tasks across five domains to probe the underexplored interaction of multilinguality and agentic execution.

entry.title: Prompt Robustness Is Task-Dependent: Comparing Objective and Belief-Style Questions in LLM Evaluation

author.name: Sadia Kamal, Arefa Patwary, Anthony Marchiafava, Atriya Sen, Sagnik Ray Choudhury

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLM prompt robustness differs between objective questions with fixed answers and subjective value/belief questions, evaluating four model families across three objective and three subjective datasets under wording, framing, and format perturbations. It cautions against treating prompted responses as measures of model values.

entry.title: ResonatorLM: Causal Resonant Field Mixing for Efficient Long-Context Language Modelin

author.name: Archie Chaudhury

entry.summary: Introduces ResonatorLM, a physics-derived attention alternative that treats a token sequence as a single driven one-dimensional latent field, replacing attention dot products with resonant field mixing for efficient long-context modeling. It aims to improve efficiency on long sequences over transformers and RNNs.

entry.title: RPAM: A Principled Metric for Evaluating Associations in Language Models with High Predictive Validity in Downstream Outputs

author.name: Damian Hodel, Jevin West, Aylin Caliskan

entry.summary: Introduces RPAM, an upstream metric measuring associations in language models at the embedding/continuation-probability level that claims high predictive validity for downstream biased outputs, unlike dataset-specific downstream metrics. It aims for principled, generalizable bias analysis across models.

entry.title: CMDR: Contextual Multimodal Document Retrieval

author.name: Ryota Tanaka, Taku Hasegawa, Kyosuke Nishida

entry.summary: Introduces CMDR and CMDR-Bench for contextual multimodal document retrieval that requires modeling cross-page document context, plus CMDR-Embed, an embedding framework that jointly encodes multiple pages. It addresses the failure of independent-page encoding on queries aggregating information across pages.

entry.title: Life Cycle Assessment of Pre-training the Lucie 7B Open-Source Large Language Model on the Jean Zay Supercomputer

author.name: Marc L\'eobet, Pierre-Fran\c{c}ois Lavall\'ee, Jean-Pierre Lorr\'e

entry.summary: This work presents a full life-cycle assessment of pre-training the open-source Lucie 7B multilingual model on a French H100 supercomputer, accounting for embodied hardware emissions, water use, and infrastructure rather than only operational energy. It matters as a rare, methodologically rigorous environmental disclosure that goes beyond the usual narrow carbon estimates.

entry.title: Where to cut, how deep: BPE and Unigram-LM on chemistry SMILES

author.name: Hunter Heidenreich

entry.summary: This controlled study compares BPE and Unigram-LM tokenizers on chemistry SMILES strings, finding that the two algorithms build near-disjoint subword vocabularies across corpora and boundary policies. It challenges the field's unexamined inheritance of BPE from natural language.

entry.title: A Convex Approximation Framework for Neural Likelihood-Based Bayesian Inverse Problems

author.name: Fabian Schneider, Tapio Helin, Leila Taghizadeh

entry.summary: The authors propose a convex approximation framework for neural likelihood-based Bayesian inverse problems, learning the likelihood directly from data to enable tractable inference in high-dimensional settings where classical MCMC struggles. It targets problems with unknown physics or costly simulations.

entry.title: On the feasibility of dependency parsing of non-human sequences without a gold standard. Is evaluation possible in other species?

author.name: Ramon Ferrer-i-Cancho, Catherine Hobaiter, Thore Bergman, Morgan Gustison

entry.summary: This paper argues that unsupervised dependency parsing of non-human animal vocalization and gesture sequences can be evaluated even without a gold standard, using network-science arguments to bound the required accuracy of retrieved edges. It challenges the claim that parsing is infeasible for other species.

entry.title: AEGIS: A Mechanism-Guided Defense against Visual Synonym Jailbreaks in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Yuanmin Huang, Zhenfei Zhang, Mi Zhang, Geng Hong, Qinqin He, Jialing Tao, Hui Xue, Min Yang

entry.summary: AEGIS is a mechanism-guided defense against visual synonym jailbreaks in text-to-image diffusion models, where benign-looking prompts elicit prohibited imagery through implicit visual associations. It targets the safety-utility dilemma by addressing hidden unsafe targets that current filtering and pruning defenses miss.

entry.title: ProxyPose: 6-DoF Pose Tracking via Video-to-Video Translation

author.name: Ruihang Zhang, Felix Taubner, Pooja Ravi, Kiriakos N. Kutulakos, David B. Lindell

entry.summary: ProxyPose recasts 6-DoF pose tracking as video-to-video translation, where a fine-tuned video diffusion model translates an input video and a single marked pixel into a proxy video of a colored polyhedron undergoing the same rigid motion. This avoids needing 3D models, depth, or masks and handles textureless, transparent, reflective, or deformable surfaces.

entry.title: Lift3D-VLA: Lifting VLA Models to 3D Geometry and Dynamics-Aware Manipulation

author.name: Jiaming Liu, Qingpo Wuwu, Nuowei Han, Hao Chen, Zhuoyang Liu, Fan Fei, Yueru Jia, Chenyang Gu, Yandong Guo, Boxin Shi, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: Lift3D-VLA is a unified vision-language-action framework that equips models with explicit 3D point-cloud reasoning and temporally coherent action generation for robotic manipulation. It addresses limited 3D data availability and geometric information loss in current 3D encoding pipelines for dynamic environments.

entry.title: Foundation Models for Automatic CAD Generation

author.name: J de Curt\`o, Victoria Guill\'en, I. de Zarz\`a

entry.summary: An empirical study of foundation models for text-to-CAD generation of mechanical parts, introducing LLMForge with schema validation, feature scoring, mesh synthesis, and iterative refinement over a 97-problem benchmark. It compares critique regimes including a ray-traced visual metric approach.

entry.title: Beyond Static Evaluation: Building Simulation Environments for Scalable Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Akshay Arora, Ishan Nigam, Ashutosh Aggarwal, Shefali Bansal, Krishna Singh, Sweta Kumari, Nikhil Mittal, Shariq Farhan, Siddarth Malreddy

entry.summary: Describes AgenticAI-Supervisor, an API- and UI-driven RL gym that decouples environment creation from scalable execution and uses verifiable outcomes plus multi-dimensional reward shaping. It emphasizes mitigating reward hacking via internal state validation, demonstrated on a customer-support case study.

entry.title: StateFuse: Deterministic Conflict-Preserving Memory for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Sergey Volkov, Yang Li, Ye Luo

entry.summary: Introduces StateFuse, a conflict-aware replicated memory contract built on standard CRDT merge that preserves disagreement via immutable history, explicit conflict objects, and projection-time resolution. It provides agent-facing semantics for correcting conflicting observations without rewriting replicated state.

entry.title: TopoBrick: Agentic Topology Sampling of Exogenous Variables for Zero-Shot Building IoT Forecasting

author.name: Xiachong Lin, Du Yin, Arian Prabowo, Hao Xue, Wen Hu, Imran Razzak, Matthew Amos, Sam Behrens, Flora D. Salim
