entry.summary: Introduces TopoBrick, a training-free framework for zero-shot building IoT forecasting that uses building knowledge graphs to build a structural skeleton and an agentic topology sampler to select target-specific exogenous variables. Variables are organized by deployment-time availability, separating past-known sensor states from future-known calendar and weather data.

entry.title: FootsiesGym: A Fighting Game Benchmark for Two-Player Zero-Sum Imperfect-Information Games

author.name: Chase McDonald, Nathan Tsang, Wesley N. Kerr

entry.summary: Introduces FootsiesGym, an open-source vectorized environment based on a minimalist 2D fighting game for studying two-player zero-sum imperfect-information games with cyclic, non-transitive strategic dynamics. It benchmarks several RL algorithms and enables high-throughput training on standard hardware.

entry.title: Decision Protocols in Multi-Agent Large Language Model Conversations

author.name: Lars Benedikt Kaesberg

entry.summary: A thesis introducing the MALLM framework that implements and compares decision protocols (voting, consensus, judge) for multi-agent LLM collaboration and their effect on task performance. It studies how coordination mechanisms trade training cost for test-time discussion.

entry.title: Hierarchical Classification via Cascading Feature Elimination: Application to Human Phenotype Ontology-Aligned Facial Phenotyping (FaceMesh2HPO)

author.name: Fabio Hellmann, Alexander Hustinx, Benjamin D. Solomon, GestaltMatcher Database Consortium, Tzung-Chien Hsieh, Peter Krawitz, Elisabeth Andr\'e

entry.summary: Presents FaceMesh2HPO, a hierarchical PointNet-based pipeline that classifies facial phenotypic descriptors aligned with the Human Phenotype Ontology from 3D facial meshes to support clinical diagnosis of genetic disorders. Uses annotations from 124 clinicians across 10 disorders and reports moderate AUROCs with variable external generalizability.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: How Humans Evaluate Legally Correct but Socially Controversial Legal Advice from Machines

author.name: Benjamin Minhao Chen, Zhiyu Li

entry.summary: Reports a preregistered survey experiment with 3,348 adults in China examining how people evaluate identical legal advice attributed to AI versus a human lawyer, with or without reasoning. Finds no net algorithm aversion but opposing psychological pathways, with AI advice seen as more objective yet less empathetic.

entry.title: Plainbook: Data Science, in Plain Language

author.name: Luca de Alfaro, Mathis Aubert, Ranjit Jhala, Eliana Pastor, Elena Baralis

entry.summary: Introduces Plainbook, a notebook paradigm centered on natural-language descriptions rather than code, automatically generating code from cell descriptions with linear execution semantics and value verification. It aims to make reproducible data science accessible to non-coders.

entry.title: SCOReD: Student-Aware CoT Optimization for Recommendation Distillation

author.name: Haz Sameen Shahgir, Yufei Li, Frank Shyu, Luke Simon, Sandeep Pandey, Xi Liu, Yue Dong

entry.summary: Proposes SCOReD, a chain-of-thought distillation framework tailored to recommendation that parses verbose, uncertain teacher traces into structured forms suited for small student models before RL training. It addresses teacher over-checking and out-of-distribution reasoning traces in the recommendation domain.

entry.title: Complementary Roles of Image Classification and Vessel Segmentation in AI-Based Screening for Retinopathy of Prematurity Plus Disease in a Kenyan Preterm Cohort

author.name: Fred Mutisya, Oscar Onyango, Sarah Sitati, Syokau Ilovi, Aeesha NJ Malik, Brenda W'mosi, Brian Makini, Jalemba Aluuvala, Josiah Onyango, Rachael Kanguha Mmene, Steven Wanyee

entry.summary: Evaluates AI-based screening for Retinopathy of Prematurity Plus disease in a Kenyan preterm cohort (121 infants, 1,635 images), comparing image classification and vessel segmentation approaches under patient-grouped nested cross-validation. Demonstrates complementary roles of classification and segmentation for low-resource ROP screening.

entry.title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection of Information Operations Users via Behavioral and Language Patterns

author.name: Sishun Liu, Sajal Halder, Ke Deng, Yan Wang, Xiuzhen Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes TENSOR, an unsupervised anomaly-detection approach for detecting information-operations users on social media by fusing temporal behavioral and language signals, avoiding oversimplified coordination assumptions of prior unsupervised methods. It frames IO detection as multimodal anomaly detection to capture evolving user behavior.

entry.title: Latency-Constrained Hardware-Aware Quantum Error Correction Co-Design with Adaptive Confidence-Gated Neural Decoding for the Rotated Surface Code

author.name: Sumit Chongder

entry.summary: This work proposes a confidence-gated two-stage decoder for the rotated surface code, using a fast neural network for most syndromes and escalating only low-confidence cases to minimum-weight perfect matching. It targets the real-time decoding bottleneck in scalable quantum error correction.

entry.title: Kernel-based Operator Learning: Error Analysis, Budget Allocation, and a Physics-Informed Extension

author.name: R\"udiger Kempf

entry.summary: This paper analyzes kernel-based operator learning in a two-stage offline-regression, online-reconstruction framework, deriving an explicit budget-allocation condition relating training pairs, input observations, and output resolution, plus a physics-informed extension. It provides theoretical guidance for resource allocation in operator learning.

entry.title: Revisiting the Relation Between Language Model Perplexity and ASR Word Error Rate for Modern End-to-End Speech Recognition

author.name: Mohammad Zeineldeen, Albert Zeyer, Haoran Zhang, Robin Schmitt, Ralf Schl\"uter, Hermann Ney

entry.summary: This paper revisits whether the historically linear log-log relation between language-model perplexity and ASR word error rate still holds for modern end-to-end speech recognition systems with internal language modeling and neural or LLM integration. It re-examines when external LMs still help.

entry.title: Calf-Integrated Arms for Bimanual Quadruped Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Yan Pan, Yuanchuan Ren, Chipui Chan, Jingcheng Sun, Chengxu Zhou

entry.summary: Integrates a manipulator with a prismatic slider, two joints, and a gripper into each front calf of a Unitree Go2 quadruped, enabling bimanual ground-level manipulation with all four feet planted and no rearing. A VLM sequences skills from a predefined library based on head-camera images.

entry.title: Prior-First, Condition-Second: Scalable and Controllable Hand Motion Completion

author.name: Mingyi Shi, Xuelin Chen, Taku Komura

entry.summary: Proposes a prior-first, condition-second framework for body-conditioned hand motion completion that first learns a generic body-hand kinematic prior from large unlabeled motion data, then adds semantic control via lightweight adaptation on the frozen prior. Uses a streaming autoregressive body-hand prior for scalable and controllable synthesis.

entry.title: Calibrating alignment evals

author.name: darshanav

entry.summary: Examines failure modes of current alignment evaluations, emphasizing evaluation awareness where models detect they are being tested and behave differently, citing high detection rates in prior work. Argues that pass rates from safety benchmarks may not reflect robustness under slightly altered conditions.

entry.title: Prompt-to-Paper: Agentic AI System for Bioinformatics

author.name: Ramsha Kamran, Maheera Amjad, Zartasha Mustansar, Arsalan Shaukat, Salma Sherbaz, Muhammad U. S. Khan

entry.summary: Introduces Prompt-to-Paper, a multi-agent framework for automated bioinformatics manuscript generation that tries to ground claims in verifiable literature, execute rather than fabricate experiments, and evaluate publication readiness. It targets known failure modes in end-to-end AI writing systems.

entry.title: Demonstrating TOFFEE: A Learned System for Synthesizing Data Agent Trajectories at Scale

author.name: Ziting Wang, Yin Li, Zuhao Yang, Xiuchang Li, Jiale Bai, Gao Cong

entry.summary: Demonstrates TOFFEE, a system for synthesizing high-quality data-agent trajectories at scale that capture complex analytical workflows, usable both as supervised fine-tuning data and as in-context demonstrations. It targets generalization of data agents to unseen enterprise data environments.

entry.title: Task Decomposition-Guided Reranking for Adaptive Agent Skill Retrieval

author.name: Yanping Chen, Weijie Shi, Wen Yang, Jiajie Xu

entry.summary: Introduces SkillReranker, an inference-time reranking framework for adaptive skill selection that performs semantic decomposition on both tasks and skills and accounts for task difficulty and skill applicability. It targets ambiguous matching in large agent skill libraries.

entry.title: Finding H. pylori in the Fine Print: Evidence-Linked Multi-Agent Case Finding from Gastric Biopsy Reports

author.name: Yufan Wang, Anit Kumar Sahu, Yan Fei Ng, Daniel Kang, Shayan Vassef, Soorya Ram Shimgekar, Koustuv Saha, Piyum Zonooz, Navin Kumar, Chee Leong Cheng, Li Yan Khor

entry.summary: Presents nMAS, a field-name-driven, evidence-linked multi-agent extraction workflow for identifying H. pylori positivity and associated gastritis from heterogeneous coded and free-text gastric biopsy reports. It handles assertion and negation to scale case finding for gastric cancer prevention.

entry.title: Few-Medoids: An Embarrassingly Simple Coreset Selection Method for Few-Shot Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Cemil-Andrei Dilmac, Florinel-Alin Croitoru, Radu Tudor Ionescu

entry.summary: Introduces few-medoids, a simple coreset selection strategy for few-shot knowledge distillation that picks samples closest to each class centroid, and shows it outperforms random selection across four datasets and three teacher-student pairs. It demonstrates strong results from a deliberately minimal method.

entry.title: From Blueprint to Reality: Modeling and Applying Putnam's Social Capital Theory with LLM-based Multi-agent Simulations

author.name: Shiyi Ling, Zhi Zheng, Hui Zheng, Wenjun Xue, Feng Ye, Tong Xu

entry.summary: Presents SocaSim, an LLM-based multi-agent simulation framework that operationalizes Putnam's Social Capital Theory with an environment modeling social network evolution, trust dynamics, and norm propagation for repeated collective-action experiments. It aims to move from theoretical blueprint to theory-aligned simulated reality.

entry.title: EcoVision: AI-Powered Drone Imaging for Salt Marsh Vegetation Monitoring and Dominance Mapping

author.name: Innocent Onyenonachi, Peter J. Lawerance, Nadia Kanwal

entry.summary: Proposes PVCap for 3D dense captioning, introducing PseudoCap augmentation that changes spatial layouts (rather than only rigid transforms) and VoxelCapNet to extract richer semantic information for describing spatial relations between objects. It targets limitations in layout diversity and backbone/detection design.

entry.title: Mitigating Errors in LLM-Generated Web API Invocations via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Constrained Decoding

author.name: Daniel Maninger, Leon Chemnitz, Jannis Brugger, Tushar Lamba, Amir Molzam Sharifloo, Mira Mezini

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates retrieval-augmented generation and constrained decoding as complementary methods to improve the correctness of LLM-generated web API invocation code from OpenAPI specifications. It quantifies mitigation effectiveness for a known weakness in code generation.

entry.title: Learning to Throw Objects Safely in Multi-Obstacle Environments

author.name: Mohammadreza Kasaei, Klemen Voncina, Hamidreza Kasaei

entry.summary: This work trains reinforcement-learning policies to throw objects into a target basket while avoiding randomly placed obstacles, using a potential-field state representation that encodes basket attraction and obstacle repulsion for generalization. It extends prior throwing work beyond obstacle-free settings.

entry.title: How Personas Can Influence Agents to Play Split or Steal

author.name: Carlos Leon, Alexandre Rodrigues, Pedro Gamito, Thomas D. Parsons

entry.summary: This study examines whether persona prompts shape strategic behavior of LLM agents in an iterated Split or Steal social-dilemma game against a fixed virtual human, across four open models and temperature settings. It finds mutual cooperation dominant with occasional exploitation.

entry.title: BlueMagpie-TTS: A Token-Efficient Tokenizer, Language Model, and TTS for Taiwanese-Accent Code-Switching Speech

author.name: Ho Lam Chung, Bo-Xuan Zheng, Cheng-Chieh Huang, Cheng-Han Chang, Jung-Ching Chen, Lok-Lam Ieong, Ting-Lin Hsiao, Yu-Cheng Lee, Yi-Hsin Chung, Yu-Kai Guo, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: BlueMagpie-TTS adapts the text side of speech synthesis for Taiwanese-accent Mandarin-English code-switching, introducing a compact byte-level tokenizer with the lowest token rate and a billion-parameter Traditional Chinese language model as a semantic frontend. It addresses accent, over-segmentation, and code-switching pronunciation problems.

entry.title: VEIL: How Visual Encoding Hijacking Induces Bias In Vision Models

author.name: Suranjana Sooraj, Xuyang Chen, Madhumitha Venkatesan, Dongyu Liu

entry.summary: VEIL systematically studies whether CNNs classifying time-series-as-chart-images learn true temporal patterns or exploit encoding-specific visual cues, using similarity, transferability, and attribution analyses. It finds attention-guided training can mitigate encoding bias only when such sensitivity is consistently detected.

entry.title: Unlearnable Faces: Privacy Protection Surviving Extraction Pipeline

author.name: Byunghoon Oh, Sunghwan Park, Jaewoo Lee

entry.summary: LPID builds the face-extraction pipeline directly into the unlearnable-example objective, confining perturbations to the extracted face region and concentrating energy in frequency bands preserved by cropping and resizing. This makes privacy-protecting perturbations survive the extraction that typically breaks prior methods.

entry.title: Tuning-Free Latent Diffusion Models for Ultrahigh-Resolution Image Editing

author.name: Wanglong Lu, Lingming Su, Kaijie Shi, Minglun Gong, Xiaogang Jin, Hanli Zhao, Xianta Jiang

entry.summary: UltraDiffEdit is a tuning-free framework that extends off-the-shelf latent diffusion models to ultrahigh-resolution image editing up to 8K, addressing the gap between sub-1K training resolutions and modern high-resolution photos. It avoids the blur produced by naively upscaling low-resolution edits.

entry.title: From RGB Generation to Dense Field Readout: Pixel-Space Dense Prediction with Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Zanyi Wang, Xin Lin, Haodong Li, Dengyang Jiang, Yijiang Li, Pengtao Xie

entry.summary: This paper argues that dense prediction should read out pixel-correct task-native fields directly from a pretrained diffusion transformer rather than re-encoding annotations into an RGB latent space and decoding them as images. It shows a pretrained DiT already organizes RGB inputs in a way suited to dense field readout.

entry.title: WristMimic: Full-Body Humanoid Control with Wrist-Guided Manipulation

author.name: Wongyun Yu, Youngwoon Kim, Minsu Cho

entry.summary: WristMimic is a wrist-guided whole-body humanoid control framework that separates contact-free body motion from contact-rich hand manipulation, guiding body and wrist with kinematic pose targets while fingers learn grasping from object tracking rather than direct supervision. This avoids overconstraining finger behavior from position-only hand trajectories.

entry.title: APVI-SLAM: Real-Time Acoustic-Pressure-Visual-Inertial Localization and Photorealistic Mapping System in Complex Underwater Environment

author.name: Hanwen Zhang, Yipeng Zhu, Xiaopeng Guo, Huajian Huang, Sai-Kit Yeung

entry.summary: Presents APVI-SLAM, a real-time multi-sensor fusion SLAM system for extreme underwater environments that combines acoustic, pressure, visual, and inertial data with reliability-aware reweighting and a sliding-window freezing recovery strategy. Delivers robust localization plus photorealistic mapping despite intermittent visual failure.

entry.title: RoboVAST: Automated Scenario-Based Validation of Robots at Scale

author.name: Frederik Pasch, Samuel Wiest, Argentina Ortega, Nico Hochgeschwender

entry.summary: Proposes RoboVAST, a scenario-based methodology and framework for automated, scalable validation of robots via declarative campaign specs, plugin scenario generation, and containerized execution. Demonstrated on a navigation dataset of thousands of scenario configurations and many runs.

entry.title: A unified perspective of Gaussian process approximation for differential equations

author.name: Mengwu Guo

entry.summary: Offers a unified Bayesian perspective that places diverse Gaussian-process methods for approximating differential equations within a common probabilistic framework based on derivative matching in the likelihood. Supports both parameter estimation and solution approximation and shows how existing methods fit within it.

entry.title: Feature Learning for the High Dimensional Stationary Sch\"odinger Equation with Deep Ritz Method

author.name: Yao Yao, Yulong Lu, Gilad Lerman

entry.summary: Analyzes feature learning in the deep Ritz method for the stationary Schrodinger equation with Neumann boundary conditions, proving Riemannian gradient descent reaches an approximate global minimum for single-index hypothesis models and characterizing the loss landscape under single- and multi-index source terms. Provides convergence guarantees for a class of PDE-solving neural methods.

entry.title: FirstResearch: Auditable Question Formation for LLM Scientific Discovery Agents

author.name: Yufeng Wang

entry.summary: Proposes FirstResearch, a framework that forces scientific LLM agents to emit a structured Research Question Certificate recording assumptions, mechanism, falsifier, and a minimal decisive test before downstream work. The goal is to make proposed research questions auditable rather than merely plausible-sounding.

entry.title: Uncovering Latent Depression Severity for Binary Depression Detection via Advantage-weighting Ranking

author.name: Manning Gao, Tingyi Liu, Leheng Zhang, Haifeng Hu, Yuncheng Jiang, Sijie Mai

entry.summary: Proposes a multimodal audio-visual framework for depression detection featuring a temporal encoder, mutual transformer, and a Binary Advantage-weighting Ranking Loss that mines hard pairs and enforces intra-class compactness. It aims to sharpen decision boundaries by uncovering latent severity structure.

entry.title: PatchOptic for Shared-State LLM Workflows with Projected Views and Verified Structured Updates

author.name: Zhaoyu Bai, Jiaqi Cai

entry.summary: Presents PatchOptic, an optic-inspired interface for shared-state agentic LLM workflows that defines a contract for when locally proposed rewrites remain valid against global state under progressive disclosure. It targets the missing validation layer between local edits and global consistency.

entry.title: Whose fairness? Structural concentration in AI bias research

author.name: Abhash Shrestha, Subigya Gautam, Anu Sapkota, Sanju Tiwari, Tek Raj Chhetri

entry.summary: A bibliometric and semantic-clustering study of 692 AI bias/fairness publications showing the field's fairness definitions and benchmarks are produced by a structurally concentrated research community, especially geographically. It questions the assumed universality of inherited fairness methodology.

entry.title: BaFCo: A Document Understanding Benchmark for Complex Bangla Form Comprehension

author.name: Abu Tyeb Azad, Ishita Sur Apan, Fahim Ahmed, Sumaiya Karim Katha, Ezharuddin Jubaer, Armun Alam, Pranjal Kumar Nandi, Amin Ahsan Ali, Aman Chadha, Md Mofijul Islam, AKM Mahbubur Rahman

entry.summary: Introduces BaFCo, a benchmark of 200 multi-page complex Bangladeshi government forms for Document Layout Analysis and Key Information Extraction to evaluate multimodal LLMs on a low-resource language. It targets the scarcity of high-quality annotated data for Bangla document understanding.

entry.title: Decision-Focused Scenario Generation and Selection for Efficient and Robust Grid Dispatch

author.name: Yangze Zhou, Yihong Zhou, Thomas Morstyn, Yi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a decision-focused generative framework for correlated scenario generation in distributionally robust power-grid dispatch, optimizing scenarios for downstream operational decisions rather than purely fitting historical distributions. It also accounts for spatial correlations often neglected by accuracy-oriented pipelines.

entry.title: Decoupled Single-Mask Annotation Noise Detection via Cross-Sectional Patch Self-Consistency

author.name: Yinheng Zhu, Xiaowei Xu

entry.summary: Introduces a decoupled framework for detecting single-mask annotation noise in vascular CT using cross-sectional patch self-consistency, exploiting the recurrence of tubular anatomy patches to flag inconsistent masks as interpretable noise evidence. It avoids costly multi-rater fusion and training-coupled approaches.

entry.title: Faithful or Findable? Evaluating LLM-Generated Metadata for RDF Dataset Search

author.name: Riccardo Terrenzi, Serkan Ayvaz

entry.summary: Studies six settings for LLM-generated metadata for RDF dataset search, jointly evaluating retrieval effectiveness and faithfulness, and finds unconstrained rewriting gives the best retrieval gains but is least faithful due to unsupported semantic expansion. Profile-grounded rewriting offers the most balanced trade-off.

entry.title: Agents That Teach: Towards Designing Incidental Learning Back into AI-Assisted Software Development

author.name: Rohit Mehra, Samdyuti Suri, Prithviraj K Tagadinamani, Kapil Singi, Vikrant Kaulgud, Adam P. Burden

entry.summary: Argues that over-reliance on AI coding agents short-circuits incidental learning and introduces the concept of Knowledge Debt, a developer-level analogue of technical debt where unpracticed skills atrophy and unexplained agent changes accrue. It proposes designing incidental learning back into AI-assisted development.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Velocity Correction for Proprioceptive Vehicle Localization using Evidential Mamba

author.name: Abinav Kalyanasundaram, Karthikeyan Chandra Sekaran, Wolfgang Utschick, Michael Botsch

entry.summary: EVC-Mamba turns onboard vehicle sensor data into a virtual velocity sensor for correcting inertial navigation drift in GNSS-denied settings, using a Mamba state-space model with evidential deep learning for uncertainty. It avoids extra hardware or expensive external sensors.

entry.title: REAN: Reconstruction-aware ECG Anonymization Based on Privacy--Utility Orthogonality

author.name: Taerin Ki, Sunghwan Park, Junyoung Park, Jaewoo Lee

entry.summary: REAN anonymizes raw ECG signals with a 1-D U-Net trained against frozen privacy and utility classifiers, exploiting near-orthogonal privacy and utility gradients to reduce re-identification while preserving diagnostic value. It targets the privacy-utility trade-off in shared biometric signals.

entry.title: Text Distance from Nested and Hierarchical Repetitions: A Compression-Based Perspective

author.name: Xiaojun Hu, Jing Wang, Jingwen Zhang, Fengyao Zhai, Xiao Xie, Hao Liao, Zengru Di, Yu Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a Ladderpath approach grounded in algorithmic information theory that extracts nested hierarchical repetitions to define compression-based text distances, achieving strong performance with a k-nearest-neighbor classifier across in-distribution, OOD, and few-shot tasks. It offers a lightweight structural alternative to embedding-based methods.

entry.title: WordVoice: Explicit and Decoupled Multi-Dimensional Word-Level Control for LLM-Based TTS

author.name: Sihang Nie, Jinxin Ji, Xiaofen Xing, Deyi Tuo, Chengbin Jin, Jialong Mai, Xiangmin Xu

entry.summary: WordVoice proposes a unified framework for explicit, decoupled word-level control of multiple acoustic attributes in LLM-based text-to-speech, addressing the coarse control of implicit end-to-end systems for tasks like audiobook narration and dubbing. It tackles fine-grained annotation scarcity and integration of control signals into autoregressive generation.

entry.title: DexTele: A Dual-Arm Dexterous Teleoperation System Based on Motion Retargeting and Adaptive Force Control

author.name: Yuanchuan Lai, Qing Gao, Ziyan Liang, Xianfeng Cheng, Junjie Hu, Zhaojie Ju

entry.summary: Presents DexTele, a dual-arm dexterous teleoperation system combining vision-based motion retargeting with adaptive force control to enable cross-platform generalization and compliant grasping. Targets the heterogeneity of robot arms and object variety in teleoperation.

entry.title: From Graphs to Gradients: Physics-Inspired Structural Attribution for Cyber-Physical IoT Systems and Beyond

author.name: Spyridon Evangelatos, Christos Diou, Georgios Th. Papadopoulos, Evangelos Markakis, Panagiotis Sarigiannidis

entry.summary: Proposes a statistical-mechanics-inspired framework for causal-style structural attribution in cyber-physical IoT systems where explicit causal graph recovery is impractical. It aims to move interpretability from correlation toward interventional understanding in high-risk domains.

entry.title: Integrating knowledge graphs and multilingual scholarly corpora for domain-adaptive LLMs in SSH

author.name: Adam Faci, Alessio Miaschi, Anne Combe, Pascal Cuxac, Francesca Frontini, Nicolas Larrousse, St\'ephane Pouyllau

entry.summary: Reports an ongoing use case within a European project integrating knowledge graphs and multilingual scholarly corpora to adapt foundation models for Social Sciences and Humanities tasks like QA, comparative analysis, and literature review. It follows a defined evaluation protocol for disciplinary and multilingual challenges.

entry.title: A toy framework for single and multi-agent human-AI curiosity ecosystems

author.name: Ilya E. Monosov

entry.summary: Offers a toy framework treating curiosity as an ecosystem, modeling how a single agent's inquiry policy weights uncertainty reduction, cost, delayed return, and keeping questions open, with weights that shift with experience. It extends this to many agents exploring a shared knowledge landscape.

entry.title: The Large Cancer Assistant (LCA): A Model-Agnostic Orchestration Framework for Scalable Clinical Decision Support in Oncology

author.name: Ghassen Marrakchi, Basarab Matei

entry.summary: Proposes the Large Cancer Assistant, a model-agnostic post-hoc orchestration framework for oncology decision support formalized as a 7-tuple with an Algorithmic Impermeability principle keeping orchestration independent of black-box models. It uses geometric deep learning to standardize multimodal patient data.

entry.title: Physics-Regularized Machine Learning for Proprioceptive Vehicle Localization Using Onboard Sensors

author.name: Abinav Kalyanasundaram, Karthikeyan Chandra Sekaran, Wolfgang Utschick, Michael Botsch

entry.summary: Introduces PRML2, a physics-regularized hybrid of Kalman filtering and data-driven learning to estimate vehicle pose from onboard proprioceptive sensors, maintaining accuracy during satellite-signal outages. It targets robust localization using production-vehicle sensors.

entry.title: IMR: Iterative Mode-World Weighted Regression for Multi-Agent Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Honglin Wang, Shiyao Pan, Yun-Fu Liu

entry.summary: Proposes IMR, an iterative mode-world weighted regression method with a segmental recurrent decoder for multi-agent trajectory prediction that mitigates mode collapse while improving world ranking and top-1 confidence. It targets safety-critical intention prediction for automated vehicles.

entry.title: Think Before You Grid-Search: Floor-First Triage for LLM Serving

author.name: Yihua Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Floor First, a residual-driven triage workflow for LLM serving optimization that models each decode step as a five-dimensional resource vector to compute optimistic and pessimistic performance floors before invoking heavy profilers. It argues estimation should precede grid search to avoid brute-force configuration benchmarking.

entry.title: NegROI: Click-Centric Uncertainty-Guided Refinement with Scene-Conditioned Negative Prompts for Robust Interactive 3D Segmentation

author.name: Shuheng Zhang, Feng Wu

entry.summary: Proposes NegROI, a transformer-based interactive 3D segmentation framework combining click-centric multi-resolution refinement with scene-conditioned negative prompts to handle coarse voxel resolution and hard false positives. It targets robustness across density and scale shifts such as dense RGB-D versus sparse LiDAR.

entry.title: Prompt Coach: An Empirical Evaluation of an Agentic Tutor for Learning Prompt Engineering in Software Development

author.name: Rohit Mehra, Kapil Singi, Vikrant Kaulgud, Vibhu Saujanya Sharma, Swapnajeet Gon Choudhury, Swati Sharma, Adam P. Burden, Majd Sakr

entry.summary: Introduces Prompt Coach, an agentic in-IDE tutor that helps developers learn prompt engineering through Socratic guidance grounded in their codebase and target LLM behavior, evaluating prompt quality across multiple dimensions. Reports an early empirical study with 15 professional developers.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Measurement Credibility Correction for Trustworthy Industrial Process Inference

author.name: Youcheng Zong, Runda Jia, Dakuo He

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-guided approach to correct measurement credibility for trustworthy industrial process inference, addressing biased, delayed, stale, or derived sensor inputs that still look plausible and can undermine prediction before the forecasting model does. It moves beyond numerical correlation, alarms, and explicit process equations that may be unavailable.

entry.title: On the Condition Number Upper Bound of the L-BFGS Inverse Hessian Approximation Matrix with a Two-Sided Geometric Envelope Safeguarding Mechanism

author.name: Don Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces a two-sided geometric-envelope safeguard for L-BFGS that dynamically bounds the condition number of the inverse Hessian approximation while preserving curvature and standard complexity. It aims to prevent numerical instability in ill-conditioned or non-convex optimization.

entry.title: Assessing the Operational Impact of Poisoning Attacks over Augmented 3D Point Cloud Public Datasets for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Marwan Lazrag, Badis Hammi, Lorena Gonzalez-Manzano, Joaquin Garcia-Alfaro

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether data augmentation amplifies or mitigates the impact of poisoning attacks and backdoors on 3D point-cloud datasets used for connected and autonomous vehicles. It empirically assesses how augmentation interacts with poisoned samples.

entry.title: CoPiT: Cognitive Pivot Translation for Digraphic Low-Resource Mongolian in the Traditional Script

author.name: Burte Bayarsaikhan, Serynn Kim, Buru Chang

entry.summary: CoPiT is a cognitively motivated pivot-translation pipeline for Mongolian in the data-scarce Traditional script, routing translation through the better-resourced Cyrillic script after resolving script-induced ambiguity. It exploits the internal resource hierarchy of a digraphic language.

entry.title: Early Language Learning via Spreading Activation and Category Exploration in Complex Networks

author.name: Salvatore Citraro

entry.summary: This work models early child word acquisition as a search over a graph-based mental lexicon driven by spreading activation and enforced category exploration, validated against child-vocabulary norms across four languages. It finds spreading activation outperforms a shortest-path baseline in simulating acquisition order.

entry.title: GaussFusion: Towards Multimodal 3D Gaussian Pretraining

author.name: Zhixuan You, Jihua Zhu, Yiding Sun, Zihao Guo, Haozhe Cheng, Dongxu Zhang, Lin Chen, Hainan Luo

entry.summary: GaussFusion is a multimodal pretraining framework for 3D Gaussian representations that integrates image and text supervision into masked Gaussian modeling via cross-modal semantic alignment. It aims to inject visual and language-level semantics into Gaussian encoders beyond local structural reconstruction.

entry.title: Bridging Diffusion Pruning and Step Distillation with Teacher-Aligned Repair

author.name: Jincheng Ying, Li Wenlin, Minghui Xu, Yinhao Xiao

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether post-pruning retraining of diffusion models can be replaced by step distillation, finding that naive replacement fails and proposing teacher-aligned repair to bridge pruning and step distillation. It targets reducing both network size and denoising step count jointly.

entry.title: Generalized Synthetic Image Detection with Enhanced RGB-Noise Representation Learning

author.name: Zhen Li, Gang Cao, Tian Zhang, Lifang Yu, Shaowei Weng

entry.summary: RNSIDNet is a forensic framework for generalized synthetic image detection using enhanced RGB-Noise representation learning, where attention-refined CLIP RGB semantics dynamically modulate high-frequency noise artifacts. It targets robustness to cross-model generalization and real-world image degradations.

entry.title: PIPBench: A Profile-Inclusive Framework for Personalized Image Generation Evaluation

author.name: Yuhang Wu, Shuxiang Zhang, Wee Hian Ching, Chi Zhang, Miao Liu

entry.summary: PIPBench is a profile-inclusive benchmark for personalized image generation that evaluates whether models align outputs with a user's implicit visual preferences from a few historically preferred images. It introduces a data-construction pipeline using psychological and demographic profiling for real-user and agent-generated data.

entry.title: Point as Skeleton: Accumulated Point Cloud Enhanced Autoregressive Generation for Closed-Loop Autonomous Driving Simulation

author.name: Songbur Wong, Xiaosong Jia, Junqi You, Bo Zhang, Pei Xu, Renqiu Xia, Yuping Qiu, Shaofeng Zhang, Zelin Zhao, Xuechao Yan, Yuchen Zhou, Yurui Chen, Wen Guo, Hang Xu, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: Point as Skeleton is a generative sensor-simulation framework for closed-loop autonomous driving that autoregressively generates driving video from step-wise updated ego and actor states, scene maps, and point-cloud skeleton conditions. It introduces Reset-and-Roll to adapt rolling diffusion inference for stable closed-loop rollout.

entry.title: CAIRN: Cross-Room 3D Scene Understanding with Topology-Aware Large Multimodal Models

author.name: He Liang, Chenyang Ma, Yiming Zhang, Sangyun Shin, Andrew Markham, Niki Trigoni, Yuhang He

entry.summary: CAIRN is a topology-aware 3D large multimodal model for multi-room scene understanding that aligns transformer attention with scene hierarchy, enriching object tokens with room-local relational context via a graph network and introducing learned room tokens. It targets reasoning over interconnected rooms beyond simplified single-room settings.

entry.title: GEM-Occ: From Visual Geometry Evidence to Embodied Semantic Occupancy Memory

author.name: Hu Zhu, Bohan Li, Xianda Guo, Hongsi Liu, Baorui Peng, Mingqi Yuan, Xin Jin, Wenjun Zeng, Chang Wen Chen

entry.summary: GEM-Occ introduces HIOcc, a hierarchical indoor semantic-occupancy benchmark unifying ScanNet, ScanNet++, and Matterport3D under a common sparse occupancy format while preserving native observation geometries. It supports local, room-level, and long-horizon cross-space semantic mapping for embodied agents.

entry.title: GraspIT: A Dataset Bridging the Sim-to-Real gap and back for Validated Grasping SE(3) Pose Generation

author.name: Paul Koch. Adem Karakurt, Andr\'e Sers

entry.summary: GraspIT is a dataset bridging the sim-to-real gap for validated SE(3) grasp pose generation, annotating tabletop scenes in NVIDIA Isaac Sim via a four-stage physical slip-test on parallel Franka Panda instances to produce continuous quality scores beyond force-closure. It provides graded hard negatives and a real-to-sim back-projection loop.

entry.title: Co-STAR: Cognitive Stimulation Therapy by an Autonomous Robot for Dementia -- A One-Week In-Home Study

author.name: Emmanuel Akinrintoyo, Nicole Salomons

entry.summary: Co-STAR is an autonomous social robot delivering cognitive stimulation therapy for dementia, evaluated in a one-week in-home study with nine people living with dementia. Participants completed nearly half the scheduled sessions, an adherence rate higher than typically seen in caregiver-led therapy, highlighting the role of family members.

entry.title: Embodied Human-Robot Interaction via Acoustics: A MARL Approach with AcoustoBots for Spatial Data Physicalization

author.name: Shiqi Liu, Narsimlu Kemsaram, Prateek Mittal, Pengyuan Wei, Sriram Subramanian

entry.summary: Presents AcoustoBots, a mobile acoustophoretic data-physicalization platform where TurtleBot robots carry ultrasonic phased arrays to levitate particles encoding urban scalar values, coordinated by a MADDPG multi-agent RL policy for collision-aware navigation. Explores embodied human-robot interaction through spatial data physicalization.

entry.title: Factor-Augmented Machine Learning Panel Regressions

author.name: Andrii Babii, Luca Barbaglia, Eric Ghysels, Jonas Striaukas

entry.summary: Develops asymptotic theory for high-dimensional panel regressions with cross-sectionally dependent errors driven by common shocks, proposing a factor-augmented sparse-group LASSO estimator that combines MIDAS aggregation with latent factors. Shows it can outperform standard LASSO for prediction and estimation under cross-sectional dependence.

entry.title: Entanglement Between an AI and Its Environment

author.name: VojtaKovarik

entry.summary: Introduces the concept of entanglement, the amount of information an AI has about its environment, distinguishing actual entanglement of a specific instance from the minimum entanglement a task requires. Argues it matters for AI evaluations by bounding the fidelity test environments must have to be credible.

entry.title: AgoraSim: A Hybrid Agent-Based Modeling Framework

author.name: Chung-Chi Chen

entry.summary: Introduces AgoraSim, a hybrid agent-based modeling framework that converts textual or multimodal artifacts into editable ABM configurations and runs mixed populations of LLM, vision-language, classical, and random agents against matched classical reference dynamics. All agents emit a shared structured decision object for comparable metrics.

entry.title: Privilege and confidentiality in generative AI workflows

author.name: V\'aclav Jane\v{c}ek, Thomas Melham

entry.summary: Analyzes how generative AI stores client data (parameters, context window, RAG databases) and maps the distinct confidentiality and legal-privilege risks of each, drawing on early UK and US court decisions. It offers governance guidance for legal professional privilege in GenAI workflows.

entry.title: Full-range Binary Classifier Calibration for Stable Model Updates in Production

author.name: Konstantin Berlin

entry.summary: Introduces a calibration method for binary detection models in adversarial settings that targets a consistent false-positive-rate contract across the whole score range, preserving downstream stability when models are frequently retrained. It builds on existing calibration primitives to give scores a stable FPR meaning.

entry.title: Data-dependent Evaluations for Budgeted Submodular Maximization

author.name: Lejian Zhang, Xueyan Tang, Jing Tang

entry.summary: Develops new data-dependent upper bounds for budgeted (knapsack-constrained) submodular maximization that provably dominate the optimal solution, enabling certification of how close a produced solution is to optimal. Demonstrates advantages empirically on real-world datasets.

entry.title: K-ABENA: K-Adaptive Backpropagation with Error-based N-exclusion Algorithm : (Compensated Loss-Based Sample Exclusion with Unbiased Gradient Estimation)

author.name: Jean-Francois Bonbhel

entry.summary: Presents K-ABENA, a selective gradient computation framework that excludes low-loss samples from the backward pass to cut per-iteration training cost, using Horvitz-Thompson inverse-probability reweighting to keep the gradient estimator design-unbiased. Provides convergence guarantees quantifying residual bias.

entry.title: Energy-Efficient GPU DVFS for Fine-Tuning of SLMs on Resource-constrained Embedded Devices

author.name: Jurn-Gyu Park, Sanzhar Zholdybayev, Aidar Amangeldi, Ademi Zhanuzakova

entry.summary: This work characterizes the fine-tuning energy behavior of small language models on embedded GPUs and proposes an ML-based selector for energy-optimal dynamic voltage-frequency scaling settings. It targets local, privacy-preserving on-device adaptation.

entry.title: SAMPLe: SAM-based Optimizer for Prompt Learning in VLMs

author.name: Hossein Rajoli, Fatemeh Lotfi, Niloufar Alipour Talemi, Hossein Kashiani, Xiaolong Ma, Fatemeh Afghah

entry.summary: SAMPLe integrates sharpness-aware minimization into prompt learning for vision-language models to combat the accuracy-versus-generalization trade-off in prompt tuning. The plug-in optimizer aims to preserve zero-shot generalization while adapting CLIP-style models to downstream tasks.

entry.title: Breaking Spurious Correlations via Generative Randomization and Cross-Variant Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Suraj Yadav, Anjaneya Sharma, Siddharth Yadav

entry.summary: This two-stage framework combats spurious background correlations by segmenting foregrounds with zero-shot segmentation, generating context-shifted variants via structure-preserving diffusion, and using cross-variant self-supervised learning to enforce background-invariant representations. It targets robustness under distribution shift beyond standard augmentation.

entry.title: BitFair: A 12nm Bit-Serial CNN Accelerator with Learnable Early Termination and Adaptive Bit Ordering for Ultra-Low-Power XR Vision

author.name: Ang Li, Chang Gao

entry.summary: BitFair is a 12nm bit-serial CNN accelerator co-designed with learnable bit-level early termination and adaptive bit ordering for ultra-low-power always-on XR vision within tight power and latency budgets. It exploits dynamic bit-level sparsity by learning per-layer thresholds that trigger early termination.

entry.title: Clustering-Embedded Model Predictive Path Integral Control: Avoiding Averaging-Induced Failure and Enabling Efficient Cluster Selection for Dynamic Obstacles

author.name: Zidong Liu, Kaixin Chang, Xu Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Clustering-Embedded MPPI (CE-MPPI) to resolve averaging-induced failures in standard MPPI, where importance-weighted updates blend incompatible rollouts around obstacles causing hesitation or collisions. Clusters rollouts and selects among them to navigate non-convex, dynamic-obstacle environments.

entry.title: CSTutorBench: Benchmarking Small Language Models as Tutors for Block-Based Programming

author.name: H. Chad Lane, Bryson Kageler

entry.summary: Presents CSTutorBench, a benchmark scoring small language models as tutors for block-based programming in a VEX VR robotics environment, using a pedagogical rubric and an LLM-as-judge pipeline. It targets privacy- and cost-sensitive K-12 deployments where small models are attractive.

entry.title: Synthetic Consumer Insight Generation with Large Language Models

author.name: Stephen L. France, Pia. A. Albinsson

entry.summary: Examines whether LLMs can generate synthetic consumer data for projective marketing techniques, comparing model outputs to human responses across prompts, temperatures, and models using linguistic, diversity, and topic-modeling analyses. It probes fidelity of synthetic consumer insight.

entry.title: Auto-DSM Under the Lens: A Black-Box Evaluation Framework for LLM-Based DSM Generation

author.name: Niels Potters, Theo Hofman

entry.summary: Presents a black-box evaluation framework for LLM-generated Design Structure Matrices from technical documentation, benchmarking against validated ground truth with structural, classification, and stability metrics plus a composite quality score. It emphasizes reproducibility against closed-source Auto-DSM pipelines.

entry.title: Reward-Density Heuristic for Dynamic Multi-Vehicle Routing: Performance and Computational Efficiency

author.name: Manish Kolachalam, Rani Malhotra

entry.summary: Proposes a reward-density Efficiency heuristic for a dynamic online variant combining vehicle routing and orienteering, where fleets maximize cumulative reward under a time horizon while replanning as tasks arrive. It is evaluated on drone task allocation and taxi dispatch across fleet and task scales.

entry.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Framework for Elastodynamic Wave Propagation in Bimaterial Systems

author.name: Sonal Ankush Chibire, Jenn-Terng Gau, Bo Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a physics-informed neural network framework for transient elastodynamic wave propagation in bimaterial steel-aluminum systems governed by axisymmetric linear elasticity, embedding initial, boundary, and interface conditions in the loss. It validates against high-fidelity finite-element simulations.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning for Multi Objective Battery Management in Dairy Farms

author.name: Marcos Eduardo Cruz Victorio, Karl Mason

entry.summary: Proposes a two-layer multi-objective control system for battery management in dairy farms combining differential evolution for dynamic pricing at the upper layer with multi-agent deep reinforcement learning at the lower layer. It simulates the electrical response for renewable integration and carbon reduction in a rural distribution setting.

entry.title: Rethinking Indic AI from a Lens of Cultural Heritage Preservation

author.name: Aparna Madva, Sharath Srivatsa, Srinath Srinivasa, Tulika Saha

entry.summary: Argues for rethinking Indic AI through a cultural-heritage-preservation lens, characterizing the tension between AI enabling inclusion and homogenizing worldviews or excluding underrepresented languages. It conducts a longitudinal survey of how NLP techniques have evolved for Indian linguistics tied to cultural practices.

entry.title: Automated Recommendation of Programming Learning Content Using Pattern-based Knowledge Components

author.name: Muntasir Hoq, Griffin Pitts, Zhangqi Duan, Arun Balajiee Lekshmi Narayanan, Mohammad Hassany, Andrew Lan, Peter Brusilovsky, Bita Akram

entry.summary: Investigates using pattern-based Knowledge Components extracted from code samples to automatically link introductory programming learning resources targeting similar concepts. It measures similarity between KC sets to align activities at the level of semantically important programming patterns, reducing reliance on expert curation.

entry.title: EvalLoop: A Methodology for Evaluation-Driven Iterative Improvement of Business AI Systems

author.name: Kenneth Benavides, Josh Fleischer, Danti Chen

entry.summary: Presents EvalLoop, a methodology for evaluation-driven iterative improvement of business LLM systems using dimensional metric grouping, failure-mode classification, and a structured iteration workflow. It reframes evaluation from static model selection to diagnosis and guided fixing.

entry.title: i-EXAM: Instructable and Explainable Attack Connectivity Graph Modeler

author.name: Rakesh Podder, Wadia Ganim, Sarath Sreedharan, Indrajit Ray, Indrakshi Ray

entry.summary: Presents i-EXAM, a planning-powered tool that helps administrators build network security profiles and perform what-if analyses to identify hardening strategies, with soundness and completeness guarantees from planning compilation and natural-language explanations via LLMs. It generates diverse hardening strategies and explains attack paths.

entry.title: Signed-Graph Recommendation as Structural Consistency Maximization

author.name: Zifan Wang, Siyu Chen, Wenzhuo Song

entry.summary: Proposes SSC-Loop, a unified framework treating signed social recommendation as maximization of structural consistency across structural, propagation, and semantic layers, addressing noise and sparsity. It aims to bridge noisy observed topologies with reliable social semantics rather than treating the graph as fixed.

entry.title: On the convergence of graph Laplacians with a symmetric divergence

author.name: Liane Xu

entry.summary: This paper generalizes geodesic-distance estimates used in manifold learning to settings where the metric is induced by a smooth symmetric divergence, proving convergence bounds for graph Laplacians. It broadens the theoretical foundations of manifold-learning algorithms.

entry.title: 6G Sensing Security: Distributed Game-Theoretic RL for Urban Beamforming and Attacker Detection

author.name: Parmida Geranmayeh, Onur G\"unl\"u

entry.summary: This work uses distributed game-theoretic reinforcement learning for joint urban beamforming and detection of active attackers who manipulate beamforming directions in integrated sensing-and-communication systems. It targets security for next-generation 6G sensing.

entry.title: Inject or Navigate? Token-Efficient Retrieval for LLM Analysis of Transactional Legal Documents

author.name: Mahmoud Hany, Mourad ElSheraey, Mahmoud Said, Peter Naoum

entry.summary: This paper compares full-corpus context injection against two structured retrieval modes, embedding retrieval and LLM navigation over a compact structured index, for analyzing transactional legal documents. It reports token-efficiency and answer-quality tradeoffs on a small verified benchmark.

entry.title: From Sinhala to Dhivehi: Cross-Lingual Transfer Learning for Low-Resource Speech Recognition

author.name: Lukmal Ilyas, Nevidu Jayatilleke

entry.summary: This study investigates cross-lingual transfer from the well-resourced related language Sinhala to improve Dhivehi automatic speech recognition, testing five transfer paradigms across seventeen experiments. Continual pre-training on Sinhala followed by Dhivehi fine-tuning with a language model gives the best word and character error rates.

entry.title: DeSeG: Decoupling Semantic Intent and Geometric Constraints for Physically Plausible Human-Scene Interaction

author.name: Jiakun Li, Zhe Li, Wenqiang Wu, Zheng Chang, Mingqi Gao, Jinyu Yang, Feng Zheng

entry.summary: DeSeG is a hierarchical framework for synthesizing physically plausible human-scene interactions that explicitly decouples semantic intent from geometric constraints to avoid shortcut biases. It reduces physical hallucinations like body-scene penetration while honoring both action semantics and spatial cues.

entry.title: TRIG: Trajectory-Rig Decoupled Metric Geometry Learning

author.name: Lizhou Liao, Wentao Xu, Handong Wang, Lirong Yang, Shuai Yang, Weiwei Liu, Chang Huang

entry.summary: TRIG factorizes camera poses into ego-trajectory and static camera-rig components for vision-centric autonomous driving geometry learning, exploiting rigid multi-camera priors that entangled representations ignore. It targets improved pose, depth, and 3D reconstruction accuracy for driving rigs.

entry.title: SparseCtrl-HOI: Sparse Temporal Control for Human-Object Interaction Video Generation

author.name: Shenbo Xie, Mingrui Cai, Xu Yang, Yifei Liu, Changxing Ding

entry.summary: SparseCtrl-HOI enables human-object interaction video generation from sparse temporal guidance rather than dense frame-wise hand-object pose sequences, reducing annotation cost and improving motion diversity. It targets applications such as AI-driven live-streaming e-commerce.

entry.title: PhyMRI-SR: Toward Physics-Aware MRI Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Lihua Wei, Huatong Gao, Jia Gong, Zhiyu Tan, Hao Li, Jun Liu, Zhihua Ren

entry.summary: PhyMRI-SR reframes MRI super-resolution as a physics-aware reconstruction problem, recognizing that spatial resolution and signal-to-noise ratio are inherently coupled during acquisition. It seeks an optimal resolution-SNR configuration before super-resolving, making resolution dynamic rather than a fixed deterministic mapping.

entry.title: Straight-Path Flow Matching for Incomplete Multi-View Clustering

author.name: Yiteng Yuan, Junyan Wang, Zheyuan Liu, Hong Jia, Lei Fan, Zhulin Tao, Lianbo Guo

entry.summary: This paper introduces a straight-path flow-matching framework for incomplete multi-view clustering that uses linear interpolation between paired view representations instead of stochastic diffusion trajectories. It provides theoretical analysis of deterministic ODE dynamics tailored for clustering rather than cluster-agnostic noise initialization.

entry.title: Synthetic-to-Real Translation for Class-Agnostic Motion Prediction

author.name: Yizheng Wu, Hongwei Fan, Kewei Wang, Ruibo Li, Xingyi Li, Xiao Song, Zhe Wang, Chenjing Ding, Dongliang Wang, Zhiguo Cao, Guosheng Lin

entry.summary: This work explores synthetic-to-real translation for class-agnostic motion prediction in autonomous driving, addressing the sensitivity of naive motion regression to synthetic-to-real domain shift. It proposes an objectness-aware motion knowledge translation framework to transfer motion knowledge from synthetic to real data.

entry.title: SSA-3DGS: Unsupervised Removal of Screen-Space Artifacts for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Kristof Overdulve, Lode Jorissen, Nick Michiels

entry.summary: SSA-3DGS is an unsupervised method for removing screen-space artifacts in 3D Gaussian Splatting, addressing static occlusions fixed to the image plane such as sensor defects, lens obstructions, watermarks, and UI overlays. These artifacts otherwise get baked into 3D geometry as floaters that degrade novel-view rendering.

entry.title: OrchardBench: A Physically-Grounded, GPU-Parallel Apple-Orchard Simulation Benchmark for Agricultural Robotics

author.name: Humphrey Munn

entry.summary: OrchardBench is a physically-grounded, GPU-parallel simulation of apple-orchard trees on the Newton engine, where each tree is grown by a stochastic L-system and instantiated as a fully articulated body with compliant torsional spring-damper branches. It addresses the lack of physically plausible trees in robot-learning simulators for fruit harvesting.

entry.title: Neuromorphic Silicon Neuron Controller for Adaptive Deep Brain Stimulation in Parkinson's Disease

author.name: Md Abu Bakr Siddique, Jakub Or{\l}owski, Yan Zhang, Hongyu An

entry.summary: This paper presents SiLIF-DBS, a neuromorphic silicon leaky integrate-and-fire controller in CMOS for adaptive deep brain stimulation in Parkinson's disease, moving beyond algorithm- and software-driven approaches toward low-power implantable circuits. It evaluates a simplified computational model of the controller at the system level.

entry.title: Observation Quality Matters: Robust Multi-Fisheye Calibration via Failure-Oriented Analysis

author.name: Peize Liu, Zhe Tong, Chen Feng, Shaojie Shen

entry.summary: Studies why multi-fisheye camera calibration fails, using a failure-oriented analysis that pins the dominant cause on poor intrinsic initialization from observations with limited radial span rather than detector recall. Offers practical guidance for building robust wide-FOV calibration pipelines.

entry.title: Superhuman Articulacy as an LLM Safety Target

author.name: Dylan Bowman

entry.summary: Argues that current LLMs are poor communicators relative to their agentic capability and that improving articulacy, distinct from truthfulness, is a valuable and possibly necessary safety target. Sketches a path toward improving how precisely and human-readably models communicate their activity.

entry.title: DBNN: Neural Spike Classification Using a Deep Binarized Neural Network

author.name: Binyi Ren, Luca M. Meyer, Majid Zamani

entry.summary: DBNN is a hardware-oriented binarized neural network for on-chip neural spike sorting in implantable brain-computer interfaces, achieving high accuracy with multiplier-free inference on an FPGA. It targets low-power on-node decoding to reduce telemetry demands.

entry.title: Measuring the practice of shared-decision making (OPTION12): An Investigation into Open-sourced Smaller LLMs (OS-sLLMs) for Better Privacy and Sustainability

author.name: Tamara Wit, Lifeng Han, Carly Heipon, David Lindevelt, Anne Stiggelbout, Suzan Verberne

entry.summary: This study evaluates open-source smaller language models for automated assessment of shared decision making using the detailed OPTION12 framework on Dutch melanoma consultation transcripts, prioritizing privacy and sustainability. It finds general-domain models outperform medical-domain ones which show more hallucination.

entry.title: ARMS: Anchor-Relational Motion Streaming for Seamless Solo-Social Motion Transitions

author.name: Huakun Liu, Qing Yu, Kent Fujiwara, Hideaki Uchiyama, Kiyoshi Kiyokawa

entry.summary: ARMS is a streaming framework for generating continuous human motion that unifies solo motion and human-human interaction within one causal generative process, handling transitions as people enter and leave interactions. It uses a partner-referenced relative representation to support long-horizon incremental generation.

entry.title: OBBSeg: Irregular Lesion Segmentation under Oriented Bounding Box Annotations

author.name: Jun Wei, Xinchang Liu, Yu Liu, Chuhua Yang, Shuhui Wang, Hui Huang

entry.summary: OBBSeg is a weakly supervised medical lesion segmentation paradigm using oriented bounding boxes that encode both spatial extent and orientation, with a differentiable Mask-to-OBB loss to enforce geometric consistency. It targets elongated and anisotropic lesions where axis-aligned boxes are ambiguous.

entry.title: From Application-Layer Simulation to Native Meta-Architecture: Structural Tension as an Endogenous Driver for Heterogeneous AI Evolution

author.name: Heting Mao

entry.summary: Proposes submerging application-layer cognitive protocols into a native model meta-architecture via structural tension (an endogenous loss from conflict between new information and manifold topology), an offline recurrent self-processing loop, and related mechanisms. It argues current LLMs are fundamentally stateless and require architectural change.

entry.title: A Guiding Framework for K-12 Teachers in Creating AI-powered Learning Technologies through Vibe Coding

author.name: Yukyeong Song, Seoyeon Choi, Jinhee Kim, Yeongje Kim, Lauren Weisberg, Jewoong Moon

entry.summary: Proposes GAIDE, a framework built on Design Thinking and INTERACT to guide K-12 teachers in creating AI-powered learning technologies through vibe coding, validated via interaction analysis of teachers and mentors in an eight-week workshop. It aims to support teachers-as-designers and foster AI literacy.

entry.title: VisTCP: A Visualization Framework to Construct Knowledge-Graph-Based Representation for Traditional Chinese Painting

author.name: Zhiguang Zhou, Fengling Zheng, Miaoxin Hu, Lina You, Jin Wen, Huan Liu, Wei Zhang, Dekun Qian, Yuhua Liu, Wei Chen, Yigang Wang, Yong Wang

entry.summary: Presents VisTCP, a visualization framework combining a domain-specific intelligent model with expert editing to build knowledge-graph-based structured representations of Traditional Chinese Paintings. It addresses the poor performance of general image-structuring methods on the distinctive semantics of TCPs.

entry.title: Agentic AI for IPoDWDM Network Lifecycle Automation: An MCP-Enabled Architecture

author.name: Chunmin Xia, Jakub Harbaczewski, Nikhil Dsilva, Julie Raulin, Dominic Schneider, Achim Autenrieth

entry.summary: Presents a distributed, vendor-agnostic multi-MCP architecture for SDN-based automation and autonomous control of multi-vendor multi-layer IPoDWDM optical networks, enabling end-to-end service lifecycle automation and closed-loop cross-layer control validated on a testbed. It applies agentic AI with MCP to telecom network operations.

entry.title: SHARC: SHAP-Based Interpretability in Machine Learning Risk Models for Regulatory Capital under ICAAP and CCAR

author.name: Ujjwala Vadrevu

entry.summary: SHARC applies SHAP-based explanations to a hybrid Gaussian Process regression model used for regulatory capital estimation under banking stress-testing frameworks. It aims to make black-box ML auditable enough for supervisory adoption.

entry.title: Is Domain Adaptation Always Helpful? A Frozen-Backbone Study of Cross-Domain Sentiment Transfer

author.name: Phat Tran, Artin Lahni, Pranav Kulkarni, Yaolun Zhang

entry.summary: A frozen-backbone case study asks whether explicit domain adaptation still helps cross-domain sentiment transfer when embedding models already encode target-domain knowledge, testing DANN, MMD, and supervised contrastive learning across model scales. It questions the assumed benefit of adaptation.

entry.title: Discovering Frequent Closed Embedded Sub-DAGs in Spatio-Temporal Event Data

author.name: Piotr S. Maci\k{a}g

entry.summary: This paper proposes mining frequent closed embedded sub-DAGs from spatio-temporal event data, with a DigDag algorithm producing compact non-redundant interaction patterns and comparisons against related mining methods. It targets recurring following relationships among event instances.

entry.title: Determinantal point process sampling for bioacoustic active learning

author.name: Hugo Magaldi, Gabriel Dubus

entry.summary: CARE-DPP is a batch active-learning method for bioacoustic monitoring that combines class-balanced predictive uncertainty with embedding-space novelty and a determinantal point process for diverse batch selection, annealing between coverage and uncertainty over the budget. It was submitted to a bioacoustics active-learning challenge.

entry.title: Population-Level Profiling of DSM-5 Depressive Symptoms Among Self-Reported ADHD and ASD Users on Twitter: An Exploratory Study Using Advanced NLP and Statistical Analysis

author.name: Muhammad Rizwan, David Nabergoj, Jure Dem\v{s}ar

entry.summary: This exploratory study profiles DSM-5 depressive symptom expression among self-reported ADHD and ASD users on Twitter using zero-shot filtering and a fine-tuned mental-health RoBERTa classifier across over a million tweets. It examines population-level differences in symptom expression between the two groups.

entry.title: Umm... With Transformers? Insights from Filled Pause Use across Four Slavic Parliaments

author.name: Ivan Porupski, Branimir Dropulji\'c, Nikola Ljube\v{s}i\'c

entry.summary: This study analyzes filled pauses across roughly 4,000 hours of parliamentary speech in four Slavic languages using transformer-based detection and generalized estimating equations, replicating age and speech-rate effects while finding language-specific gender effects. It also explores links to sentiment and political orientation.

entry.title: Automated Compliance Mapping in Cloud Security with Domain-Adapted Sentence Transformers

author.name: John Bianchi, Luca Petrillo, Fabio Martinelli, Marinella Petrocchi

entry.summary: This paper fine-tunes sentence-transformer models to automate mapping of cloud security controls to technical metrics, building a domain corpus from European standards and expanding it with back-translation and LLM paraphrasing. Fine-tuned models substantially outperform zero-shot baselines on control-to-metric and cross-standard tasks.

entry.title: Progressive Reasoning with Primitive Correction for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning

author.name: Ziyi Chen, Haoyan Shi, Sunhan Xu, Congyan Lang

entry.summary: PRPC is a progressive reasoning framework for compositional zero-shot learning that models bidirectional attribute-object dependencies through step-wise chain-of-thought inference with primitive correction. It aims to suppress error propagation from unidirectional conditional modeling.

entry.title: KOAL: Knowledge-Driven Prostate Cancer Grading with Ordinal-Aware Learning

author.name: Zheng Guo, Jiaqi Cui, Haocheng Xiong, Jize Han, Bo Liu, Qianwen Zhang, Rui Chen, Yan Wang

entry.summary: KOAL is a knowledge-driven, ordinal-aware framework for non-invasive prostate cancer Gleason grading from multiparametric MRI that incorporates clinical variables like age and PSA plus radiology-report priors. It models the intrinsic hierarchy of primary and secondary Gleason patterns rather than flat categorical labels.

entry.title: Revisiting Scene Graph Generation from the Perspective of Detector-Conditioned Reachability

author.name: Runfeng Qu, Pia K Bideau, Ole Hall, Julie Ouerfelli-Ethier, Klaus Obermayer, Olaf Hellwich

entry.summary: This paper analyzes prediction discrepancies between detector-based and query-based scene graph generation through detector-conditioned reachability, finding complementary behaviors. It proposes Dual-SGG, which consolidates both reasoning mechanisms via a dual-query design.

entry.title: EeveeDark: A Binary Neural Framework for Low-Light Video Enhancement via Event-Guided Sensor-Level Fusion

author.name: Onur Eker, Erkut Erdem, Aykut Erdem

entry.summary: EeveeDark is a binary neural network framework for extreme low-light video enhancement that fuses sensor-level RAW spatial data with event-stream temporal precision. It uses modality-specific binary encoders, a lightweight fusion block, and event-guided skip gating to balance restoration quality and efficiency.

entry.title: WING: A Window-Prior-Based Generative Network with Gated Inception for Cross-Modality CT Synthesis

author.name: Siyuan Mei, Yan Xia, Yipeng Sun, Siming Bayer, Zirong Li, Chengze Ye, Daiqi Liu, Fuxin Fan, Yixing Huang, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: WING synthesizes CT volumes from MRI and CBCT for adaptive radiotherapy by reformulating regression into multiple windowed representations, leveraging the structure-deterministic and window-separable nature of CT intensities. This addresses the high dynamic range and long-tailed distribution that averages out clinically important structures.

entry.title: MAC-XA: Multi-view Anatomy-Correspondence Fusion for Coronary Stenosis Reporting from X-ray Angiography

author.name: Chen Jia, Baochang Zhang, Fatia Kusuma Dewi, Amir Yousefi, Heribert Schunkert, Reza Ghotbi, Nassir Navab

entry.summary: MAC-XA performs multi-view coronary stenosis report generation from X-ray angiography by treating cross-projection reasoning as a geometric problem and enforcing anatomically consistent multi-view fusion. It addresses the challenge that cross-view alignment is unobservable and cannot be directly supervised.

entry.title: FADRA: Frequency-Aware Diffusion with Residual Adaptation for Video Face Restoration

author.name: Jin Jiang, Jia Wang, Panwen Hu, Weiran Zhao, Shengcai Liao

entry.summary: FADRA is a frequency-aware diffusion framework with iterative residual adaptation for video face restoration, using a pretrained text-to-video diffusion prior with lightweight LoRA adapters and a low-quality pixel-alignment fusion module. It targets balancing spatial fidelity and temporal coherence under complex degradations.

entry.title: Andha-Dhun: A First Look at Audio Descriptions in Hindi

author.name: Ritabrata Chakraborty, Divy Kala, Nisheeth Bhooshan Gupta, Ganji Sreeram, Pailla Balakrishna Reddy, Makarand Tapaswi

entry.summary: Andha-Dhun presents the first systematic study of audio descriptions in Hindi for blind and low-vision audiences, contributing a dataset of human-authored descriptions from eight movies and exploring generation approaches. It responds to Indian regulatory mandates to expand accessibility beyond English.

entry.title: MonoIR-RS: Infrared Remote Sensing Vision-Language Learning with CLIP and VLM Adaptation

author.name: Jiaju Han, Ma Yaqi, Yahui Chai, Xuemeng Sun, Xin Li, Qike Zhang, Yingying Zhao, Xiang Chen, Luwei Yang, Chengyin Hu, Jiahuan Long

entry.summary: MonoIR-RS is a large-scale infrared remote-sensing vision-language dataset and benchmark that couples IR-aware data construction with CLIP-style contrastive adaptation and VLM instruction tuning. It provides 600K synthesized infrared images and IR-aware captions to address the visible-band bias of existing resources.

entry.title: Abductive Corroboration of Probabilistic AI Models for Forensic Synthetic Media Detection

author.name: Junade Ali

entry.summary: This single-author paper applies abductive reasoning to forensic synthetic-media detection, corroborating outputs of multiple probabilistic AI models to identify the most likely conclusion and disproportionately lower false-positive risk. It contrasts abductive corroboration with inductive and infeasible deductive approaches in forensic settings.

entry.title: A Hardware-Aware Open-Source Framework for Design Space Exploration of Mixed-Signal Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Sayma Nowshin Chowdhury, Vineeta Nair, Taseen Forhad, Aishwarya Natarajan, Corey Hart, Sahil Shah

entry.summary: This work presents an open-source hardware-aware simulation framework for mixed-signal spiking neural networks that captures device non-idealities and supports design-space exploration across neuron models, analog synapses, and architectures. It incorporates device-level nonlinearities directly into PyTorch-based training and inference.

entry.title: MP-MPPI: A Motion Primitive Guided Sampling-Based Optimizer for Model Predictive Control

author.name: Marlon Mathisen, Aksel Vaaler, Olav Egeland, Eleni Kelasidi

entry.summary: Extends Model Predictive Path Integral control with motion primitives for structured sampling to improve convergence toward global optima and obstacle-field navigation. Demonstrated on a quadcopter simulator.

entry.title: Approximate Risk Minimization Over Shrinking-Thresholding Rules in Normal Mean Estimation

author.name: Wei Jiang

entry.summary: Develops an approximate risk minimization framework for shrinkage-thresholding estimators in the normal mean model, defining a functional class covering James-Stein and lasso-type rules and constructing a feasible data-driven risk criterion. The resulting estimator, NOMAD, minimizes approximate risk over the class.

entry.title: Trying to grok Anthropic's Global Workspace paper and the J-space

author.name: TheManxLoiner

entry.summary: An explainer attempting to reconstruct the conceptual methodology behind the J-space and Jacobian Lens in Anthropic's Global Workspace paper, focusing on the derivation in an early section rather than empirical findings. Aims to help readers understand the core ideas.

entry.title: A conceptor by any other name

author.name: Keenan Pepper

entry.summary: Notes that a specific idea the author had for representation steering already exists under the name conceptor, drawing on prior work applying conceptors to semantic steering. A short conceptual note connecting steering ideas to established constructions.

entry.title: Structured-Condensed Prompt Tuning in Vision-Language Models for Fine-grained Image Recognition

author.name: Xinda Liu, Qinyu Zhang, Weiqing Min, Guohua Geng, Shuqiang Jiang

entry.summary: This work proposes structured-condensed prompt tuning for vision-language models in fine-grained recognition, modeling hierarchical dependencies and inter-class correlations rather than treating class labels as isolated entities. It aims to help CLIP-style models capture subtle distinctions among visually similar categories.

entry.title: Temporal Modeling of Optically Variable Devices in Identity Documents

author.name: Glen Pouliquen (IDnow Research Center, France, EPITA Research Lab), Joseph Chazalon (EPITA Research Lab), Guillaume Chiron (IDnow Research Center, France), Oriol Ramos Terrades (Computer Vision Center), Thierry G\'eraud (EPITA Research Lab), Ahmad Montaser Awal (IDnow Research Center, France)

entry.summary: This industry-affiliated work models the temporal dynamics of Optically Variable Devices (holograms) in identity documents captured in user videos, moving beyond isolated-frame analysis to resist swapping attacks and verify specific OVD types. It addresses the economic infeasibility of frame-by-frame video annotation.

entry.title: Verification of Dynamic Holographic Behavior in Identity Documents

author.name: Glen Pouliquen (IDnow Research Center, France, EPITA Research Lab), Joseph Chazalon (EPITA Research Lab), Guillaume Chiron (IDnow Research Center, France), Thierry G\'eraud (EPITA Research Lab), Ahmad Montaser Awal (IDnow Research Center, France)

entry.summary: This paper addresses remote verification of authenticity of Optically Variable Devices on identity documents, focusing on detecting dynamic fraud such as handcrafted holograms that prior work has not evaluated due to lack of public datasets. It contributes methods aiming to generalize to unseen attack types.

entry.title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Calcification Classification in Mammography Across Multi-Site Datasets

author.name: Xuan Liu, Derek L. Nguyen, Emily C. Barre, Jennifer Thomas, Thomas Lynch, Jeffrey R. Marks, E. Shelley Hwang, Marc D. Ryser, Joseph Y. Lo, Lars J. Grimm

entry.summary: This work proposes an unsupervised domain adaptation framework for mammography calcification classification across multi-site datasets, using style-transfer models to generate vendor- and technique-specific training samples without extra annotation. A supervised classifier then improves malignant-versus-benign discrimination on unseen domains.

entry.title: TMF-RSE: Tri-Modal Fusion with Regional Semantics and Evidential Uncertainty for Lung Severity Scoring

author.name: Fadi Abdeladhim Zidi, Salah Eddine Bekhouche, Abdellah Zakaria Sellam, Gaby Maroun, Fadi Dornaika, Cosimo Distante

entry.summary: TMF-RSE is a tri-modal deep learning framework for lung disease severity scoring that fuses appearance features from chest images, structural features from lung segmentation masks, and semantic features from vision-language models. It uses evidential regression to provide both severity predictions and uncertainty estimates.

entry.title: Stochastic generator of trajectories from record data: application to the fluctuations of a glacier's frontal position from a sample of moraines

author.name: Megret Maud (LSCE, ESTIMR), Mike Pereira (GEOSCIENCES), Nicolas Eckert (INRAE, UGA), Naveau Philippe (LSCE, ESTIMR), Jomelli Vincent (CEREGE)

entry.summary: Proposes a Brownian stochastic simulator to reconstruct entire non-stationary time series from record values alone, with a neural-inference-like procedure to select generator hyperparameters. Applies it to reconstructing glacier frontal position fluctuations from moraine samples.

entry.title: Taxlifier: Leveraging Disease Taxonomy for Enhanced Multi-Label Classification in Chest Radiography

author.name: Mohammad S. Majdi, Jeffrey J. Rodriguez

entry.summary: Taxlifier proposes loss-based and logit-based hierarchical multi-label classification methods that inject disease taxonomy relationships into chest X-ray diagnosis. It leverages parent-child pathology structure to improve multi-label accuracy.

entry.title: Linking Hadith Narrator Identities Across Heterogeneous Arabic Biographical Databases: A Multi-Signal Entity Resolution Pipeline

author.name: Taufiq Wirahman

entry.summary: This work presents a two-phase multi-signal entity-resolution pipeline linking hundreds of thousands of Hadith narrator name variants across independently maintained Arabic biographical databases lacking common identifiers. It reports partial linkage rates using name-similarity and cross-referencing.

entry.title: Robust Face Super-Resolution and Recognition Through Multi-Feature Aggregation in Diffusion Models

author.name: Marcelo dos Santos, Rayson Laroca, Jo\~ao Carlos Raposo Neves, David Menotti

entry.summary: The work proposes a diffusion-based face super-resolution method that aggregates features from multiple low-quality surveillance frames to improve both image quality and identity preservation for recognition. It targets robustness under pose, illumination, and occlusion variation common in surveillance footage.

entry.title: Realistic Compound-Lens Defocus Blur Synthesis

author.name: Yunkyu Lee, Woohyeok Kim, Sunghyun Cho

entry.summary: The paper presents a pipeline for synthesizing realistic defocus deblurring datasets across diverse compound lenses using wave-optics point-spread-function computation, depth-aware rendering with occlusion handling, and camera ISP simulation. It aims to improve cross-camera generalization of deep deblurring models.

entry.title: AVA-VLM: Adaptive Visual Attention-Vision Language Model for In-the-Wild Construction Site Monitoring

author.name: Younggun Kim, Taeheon Kim, Youngseo Kim, Seunghee Park

entry.summary: AVA-VLM is a construction-site monitoring vision-language model that uses a human-inspired coarse-to-fine strategy, reasoning over low-resolution global images and selectively requesting high-resolution crops only when detailed inspection is needed. It targets better operational range, reliability, and inference efficiency for in-the-wild deployment.

entry.title: SpecTrack: Spectral Prompt Guided Adaptive Experts for Multispectral Object Tracking

author.name: Xingyu Tan, Yunrong Qin, Mengjie Hu

entry.summary: SpecTrack is a complexity-aware multispectral and hyperspectral object tracker that adapts computational capacity per frame using spectral prompt guidance and adaptive experts. It allocates lightweight processing to clear regions and stronger contextual reasoning to ambiguous or spectrally similar cases.

entry.title: High-Resolution Artwork Outpainting with Global Blueprint Guidance and Layout Control

author.name: Junha Kim, Hyunjoon Park, Donghyeon Cho

entry.summary: This work performs high-resolution artwork outpainting using global blueprint guidance and layout control to address structural instability, error accumulation, and limited spatial controllability in progressive expansion. It adds a global planning mechanism and object placement control beyond text prompts.

entry.title: Mitigating Domain Shift in Conditioned Floor Plan Generation: Synthetic Pre-training for Data-Efficient Adaptation

author.name: Matthieu Ospici, Arnaud Gueze, Luc Bourrat, Adrien Bernhardt

entry.summary: This paper studies domain-shift robustness in conditioned floor-plan generation, showing state-of-the-art models from two generative paradigms degrade by up to an order of magnitude across three datasets. It proposes synthetic pretraining for data-efficient adaptation to new architectural domains.

entry.title: Efficient Transfer Learning of Robot Dynamic Models Using Morphological Similarity

author.name: Pavlo Kupyn, Yuya Hamamatsu, Roza Gkliva, Asko Ristolainen, Maarja Kruusmaa

entry.summary: This study proposes an autoencoder-based transfer-learning framework that adapts a dynamic model trained on a larger soft fin-actuated underwater robot to a smaller morphologically similar one with limited labeled data. It learns a shared latent representation aligning the dynamics of both robots for label-efficient state estimation.

entry.title: Closed-form fractional radial links for elliptical Mahalanobis discriminant analysis

author.name: Serhii Zabolotnii
