  • The group-standard-deviation identity proves GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO differ only in how they treat one term
  • Two AI Metrics Diverged (Thompson, MIT) analyzes when frontier capabilities diverge from budget-constrained models

Domain application: RareDxR1 performs end-to-end rare disease diagnosis directly from unstructured clinical notes, bypassing pipeline bottlenecks.
entry.content:
Today's most significant research spans a frontier model release, safety/alignment mechanisms, and RL training theory.

Frontier models & robotics:

  • Seed2.0 (ByteDance) is a frontier model series using a needs-grounded evaluation system for real-world complexity
  • ASPIRE (Fan, Zhu, Goldberg) enables continual robot skills discovery via code-as-policy, compounding learned control programs

Safety & alignment dominates, with strong mechanistic and empirical results:

  • Perplexity differencing surfaces hidden finetuning objectives (backdoors, false facts, unsafe behaviors) in public model organisms, with code
  • HARC shows jailbreaks succeed by suppressing separable harmfulness and refusal directions
  • Introspective Coupling (Andreas, MIT) finds self-explanation training tracks behavioral change despite fixed supervision
  • RMCT consistency training reduces obfuscation under evaluation-awareness cues
  • Constructive Alignment reframes alignment as governing preferences that evolve through interaction

RL theory & scaling:

  • The group-standard-deviation identity proves GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO differ only in how they treat one term
  • Two AI Metrics Diverged (Thompson, MIT) analyzes when frontier capabilities diverge from budget-constrained models

Domain application: RareDxR1 performs end-to-end rare disease diagnosis directly from unstructured clinical notes, bypassing pipeline bottlenecks.

entry.title: Seed2.0 Model Card: Towards Intelligence Frontier for Real-World Complexity

author.name: Bytedance Seed

entry.summary: ByteDance Seed presents Seed2.0, a frontier model series targeting real-world complexity with a needs-grounded evaluation system and improvements in long-tail knowledge, complex instruction following, reasoning, vision, and search. The model card emphasizes reliability on long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: ASPIRE: Agentic /Skills Discovery for Robotics

author.name: Runyu Lu, Yubo Wu, Ethan Kou, Letian Fu, Wenli Xiao, Ajay Mandlekar, Yinzhen Xu, Guanya Shi, Ken Goldberg, Ang Chen, Mosharaf Chowdhury, Yuke Zhu, Linxi "Jim" Fan, Guanzhi Wang

entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social buzz from Jim Fan, ASPIRE is a continual-learning robotics system that autonomously writes and refines robot control programs in a code-as-policy paradigm, compounding experience into a reusable skill library across tasks, sim/real, and embodiments. It integrates closed-loop execution with failure diagnosis and repair synthesis.

entry.title: Most Current Model Organisms Leak: Perplexity Differencing Often Reveals Finetuning Objectives

author.name: Luca Baroni

entry.summary: Presents a simple contrastive perplexity-differencing method that surfaces instilled behaviors (backdoors, false facts, unsafe behaviors) in publicly available model organisms across families and sizes (N=76). Top-ranked completions ranked by perplexity difference against a reference model often reveal the finetuning objective, even using unrelated reference models.

entry.title: Constructive Alignment: Governing Preference Dynamics in Human-AI Interaction

author.name: Max Kanwal, Caryn Tran

entry.summary: This paper reframes AI alignment from satisfying fixed human preferences to governing preferences that are themselves shaped over time through interaction with adaptive systems, treating alignment as a control problem over preference trajectories. It draws on behavioral economics and constructivist theory to model layered, dynamic preferences, which matters as personalized AI increasingly influences what users value.

entry.title: HARC: Coupling Harmfulness and Refusal Directions for Robust Safety Alignment

author.name: Shei Pern Chua, Fangzhao Wu

entry.summary: HARC analyzes how aligned LLMs represent harmfulness and refusal as separable directions and shows jailbreaks succeed by suppressing one before generation, with attack classes occupying distinct regions of the harmfulness-refusal plane. It leverages response-token recognition of harmful content to inform more robust alignment.

entry.title: Two AI Metrics Diverged: Will it Make All the Difference?

author.name: Alex Fogelson, Zachary A. Brown, Hans Gundlach, Jayson Lynch, Neil Thompson

entry.summary: This paper (including MIT's Neil Thompson) analyzes whether frontier model capabilities diverge from budget-constrained models depending on how capability is measured, showing validation loss gaps shrink while other metrics widen indefinitely. It gives mathematical conditions classifying which metrics favor smaller models.

entry.title: Introspective Coupling: Self-Explanation Training Tracks Behavioral Change Despite Fixed Supervision

author.name: Zifan Carl Guo, Laura Ruis, Jacob Andreas, Belinda Z. Li

entry.summary: This paper studies when training LMs to explain their predictions yields faithful introspection, using counterfactual behavior as supervision. Surprisingly, models trained on explanations from earlier or similar checkpoints often explain their own current behavior more faithfully than the training targets, an effect termed introspective coupling.

entry.title: Consistency Training while Mitigating Obfuscation via Rate Matching

author.name: Sohaib Imran

entry.summary: Introduces Rate Matching Consistency Training (RMCT), an RL-based method to make models behave identically whether or not extraneous cues (like evaluation-likeness or a user's preferred answer) are present, while avoiding the obfuscation side effect where models stop verbalizing cues they still act on. It reports matching or exceeding behavioral consistency training on a sycophancy benchmark while preserving cue verbalization.

entry.title: RareDxR1: Autonomous Medical Reasoning for Rare Disease Diagnosis Beyond Human Annotation

author.name: Deyang Jiang, Haoran Wu, Ziyi Wang, Yiming Rong, Yunlong Zhao, Ye Jin, Bo Xu

entry.summary: RareDxR1 is an end-to-end reasoning-centric LLM for rare disease differential diagnosis directly from unstructured clinical notes, avoiding pipeline-based phenotype extraction and retrieval bottlenecks. It uses a progressive training framework combining knowledge and reasoning to handle vast diagnostic search spaces.

entry.title: Agentic generation of verifiable rules for deterministic, self-expanding reaction classification

author.name: Daniel Armstrong, Maarten Dobbelaere, Valentas Olikauskas, Helena Avila, Octavian Susanu, J\'er\^ome Waser, Philippe Schwaller

entry.summary: A multi-agent LLM pipeline classifies chemical reactions and autonomously writes verifiable reaction rules validated against a 665,901-reaction patent corpus, expanding a taxonomy from 68 to 14,073 classes without human curation. It couples deterministic verification with self-expanding rule generation for synthesis planning.

entry.title: Learning Dexterous Manipulation Using Contact Wrench Guidance From Human Demonstration

author.name: Xinghao Zhu, Zixi Liu, Shalin Jain, Chenran Li, Milad Noori, Huihua Zhao, John Welsh, Michael Andres Lin, Wei Liu, Tingwu Wang, Xingye Da, Zhengyi Luo, Vishal Kulkarni, Naema Bhatti, Yuke Zhu, Linxi Fan, Bowen Wen, Danfei Xu, Soha Pouya, Yan Chang

entry.summary: CHORD (with NVIDIA-affiliated authors) transfers human demonstrations to dexterous robot manipulation using object-centric contact-wrench-space guidance—representing motions by the forces/torques they induce on objects—to make reinforcement learning scalable for contact-rich, long-horizon tasks. It introduces a large-scale simulation benchmark.

entry.title: Right in the Right Way: LM Training with Verifiable Rewards and Human Demonstrations

author.name: Mehul Damani, Isha Puri, Idan Shenfeld, Jacob Andreas

entry.summary: Augments RL with verifiable rewards by adding a learned adversarial signal from human demonstrations, using a generator-discriminator setup to capture non-verifiable qualities like style and structure. Aims to counter RLVR failure modes such as diversity collapse, unnatural responses, and reward hacking.

entry.title: HealthAgentBench: A Unified Benchmark Suite of Realistic Agentic Healthcare Environments for Challenging Frontier AI Agents

author.name: Qianchu Liu, Sheng Zhang, Guanghui Qin, Jeya Maria Jose Valanarasu, Maximilian Rokuss, Mingyu Lu, Timothy Ossowski, Juan Manuel Zambrano Chaves, Cliff Wong, Peniel Argaw, Yashna Hasija, Mu Wei, Wen-wai Yim, Qin Liu, Zilin Jing, Jason Entenmann, Naoto Usuyama, Tristan Naumann, Hoifung Poon

entry.summary: HealthAgentBench is a suite of 54 agentic healthcare tasks across 7 categories, each with its own environment replicating end-to-end clinical workflows requiring exploration of raw data and multi-step execution. It provides a single task-success metric to measure frontier agents on realistic healthcare workflows.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Metacognitive Feedback Elicits Faithful Uncertainty Expression in LLMs

author.name: Gabrielle Kaili-May Liu, Avi Caciularu, Gal Yona, Idan Szpektor, Arman Cohan

entry.summary: This work introduces reinforcement learning with metacognitive feedback (RLMF), refining preference rankings using the model's ability to judge its own performance to elicit faithful uncertainty expression. It targets systemic LLM metacognitive deficits like confident hallucination and poor knowledge-boundary awareness.

entry.title: Bounded Morality: Defining the Space of Moral Computation

author.name: Max Kanwal, Caryn Tran, Patrick Mineault

entry.summary: The authors propose a formal framework extending bounded rationality to moral cognition, characterizing moral problems along breadth (scope of morally relevant entities) and depth (inferential integration) dimensions with an unavoidable resource tradeoff. It offers a computational lens on how finite agents approximate ethical theories, relevant to designing value-sensitive AI.

entry.title: Graph-Native Reinforcement Learning Enables Traceable Scientific Hypothesis Generation through Conceptual Recombination

author.name: Subhadeep Pal, Shashwat Sourav, Tirthankar Ghosal, Markus J. Buehler

entry.summary: Graph-PRefLexOR fine-tunes graph-native reasoning models with GRPO to structure scientific hypothesis generation into explicit phases (mechanism exploration, graph construction, pattern extraction, synthesis), linking neural generation to symbolic relational structure. It aims for traceable, causally grounded materials-discovery hypotheses.

entry.title: GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO Are Three Operations on One Number: The Group-Standard-Deviation Identity

author.name: Yong Yi Bay, Kathleen A. Yearick

entry.summary: This paper proves that GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO differ only in how they treat one quantity—the group standard deviation of correctness across sampled answers—via dividing by it, not dividing, or discarding zero-variance groups. It unifies three popular RL-for-reasoning methods under a single identity.

entry.title: AutoTrainess: Teaching Language Models to Improve Language Models Autonomously

author.name: Zhaojian Yu, Penghao Yin, Shuzheng Gao, Shilin He, Kai Cai, Xiao-Ping Zhang

entry.summary: AutoTrainess is an LLM agent that autonomously performs post-training by exposing planning, data preparation, training, evaluation, and logging as structured agent-computer interfaces rather than raw CLI. It aims to reduce the heavy human labor in training language models across long-horizon jobs.

entry.title: Learning from Failure: Inference-Time Self-Improvement for Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Xueqiao Sun, Xiaohan Wang, Ludwig Schmidt, Serena Yeung-Levy, Yuhui Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a failure-driven self-improvement loop for computer-use agents, arguing that failed trajectories, usually discarded, carry rich information about model weaknesses. It complements the standard success-only fine-tuning paradigm with a data-centric approach that learns from failure at inference time.

entry.title: Discovering Concept-Editing Algorithms With LLM Agents

author.name: Adam Scherlis

entry.summary: Reports on using LLM agents to invent concept-erasure algorithms that outperform existing methods like LEACE, especially against nonlinear probes, while keeping edits surgical. It frames concept erasure as a quantitative target for automated model-internals research.

entry.title: Staleness-Learning Rate Scaling Laws for Asynchronous RLHF

author.name: Jingwei Song, Haofeng Xu, Jie Xiao, Chengke Bao, Jingwei Shi, Pengbin Feng, Weixun Wang, Yuhang Han, Chuan Wu, Linfeng Zhang, Bill Shi

entry.summary: Analyzes the effect of stale rollouts in asynchronous GRPO for RLHF, deriving that staleness introduces a per-step surrogate-gradient bias of order proportional to rollout lag times learning rate. Provides a scaling-law relationship to guide learning-rate choices under staleness.

entry.title: A Contextual-Bandit Oversight Game with Two-Sided Informational Asymmetry

author.name: Yunjin Tong

entry.summary: This paper models runtime human oversight of an AI agent as a contextual-bandit team game where both parties hold private information (human knows the reward, agent knows action quality), yielding exact one-shot characterizations of a play/ask/trust/oversee interface. It extends cooperative inverse RL and oversight-game theory to two-sided asymmetric information.

entry.title: From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents

author.name: Yashar Talebirad, Eden Redman, Ali Parsaee, Osmar R. Zaiane

entry.summary: Using Lewis signaling games with LLM agents, this study finds that memory architecture matters more than communication channel capacity for emergent language coordination, with persistent private notebooks avoiding the high-capacity collapse seen in stateless agents. It suggests externalizing conventions frees agents from context-window limits.

entry.title: Coachable agents for interactive gameplay

author.name: Roberto Capobianco (Sony AI, Zurich, Switzerland), Harm van Seijen (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Nolan D. Bard (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Neil Burch (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Fatima Davelouis (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Josh Davidson (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Alisa Devlic (Sony AI, Zurich, Switzerland), Yunshu Du (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Ishan Durugkar (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Siddhant Gangapurwala (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Daniel Hernandez (Sony AI, North America, various locations), G. Zacharias Holland (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Sahil Jain (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Kenta Kawamoto (Sony AI, Tokyo, Japan), Raksha Kumaraswamy (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Patrick MacAlpine (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Dustin R. Morrill (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Declan Oller (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Francesco Riccio (Sony AI, Zurich, Switzerland), Akanksha Saran (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Craig Sherstan (Sony AI, Tokyo, Japan), Kaushik Subramanian (Sony AI, Zurich, Switzerland), Thomas J. Walsh (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Samuel Barrett (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Kizza N. Frisbee (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Mady Govil (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Johannes G\"unther (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Varun R. Kompella (Sony AI, North America, various locations), James A. MacGlashan (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Maxwell Svetlik (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Michael D. Thomure (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Jaden B. Travnik (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Kevin Waugh (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Elahe Aghapour (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Florian Fuchs (Sony AI, Zurich, Switzerland), Andreanne Lemay (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Shruti Mishra (Sony AI, Zurich, Switzerland), Takuma Seno (Sony AI, Tokyo, Japan), Peter Stone (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Michael Spranger (Sony AI, Tokyo, Japan), Peter R. Wurman (Sony AI, North America, various locations)

entry.summary: Sony AI presents a framework combining universal value function approximators with tailored training scenarios and data augmentation to coach agents into exhibiting controllable behavioral styles in complex domains, in real time. It addresses the need for controllable rather than single near-optimal RL behaviors.

entry.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill

author.name: Shengguang Wu, Hao Zhu, Yuhui Zhang, Xiaohan Wang, Serena Yeung-Levy

entry.summary: AutoMem treats memory management as a trainable cognitive skill (metamemory), promoting file-system operations to first-class memory actions so the model itself decides what to encode, retrieve, and organize. It jointly improves the supporting structure and the model's proficiency for long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: UltraFlux: Data-Model Co-Design for High-quality Native 4K Text-to-Image Generation across Diverse Aspect Ratios

author.name: Tian Ye, Song Fei, Lei Zhu

entry.summary: UltraFlux is a Flux-based diffusion transformer trained natively at 4K across diverse aspect ratios via data-model co-design, introducing a 1M-image 4K corpus and techniques like Resonance 2D RoPE with YaRN to address coupled positional-encoding, VAE, and optimization failures. It targets high-quality native high-resolution text-to-image generation.

entry.title: FLYNN: Robust Neural Network for Robot Navigation using Fly Brain Topology

author.name: Benquan Wang, Jingdao Chen

entry.summary: FLYNN is a recurrent network whose architecture is derived directly from the synaptic-resolution connectome of the fruit fly brain, trained for vision-based navigation in MuJoCo with performance comparable to hand-crafted networks of similar size. Crucially, it shows superior robustness to out-of-distribution data and sensory deprivation.

entry.title: Phantom References: Hallucinated Citations That Survive Peer Review at Top-Tier Conferences

author.name: Mark Russinovich, Ram Shankar Siva Kumar, Ahmed Salem

entry.summary: Measures citation hallucination in peer-reviewed AI proceedings using a conservative identity-level definition (non-existent works, substantial author-list mismatches) and an automated large-scale auditing pipeline. It documents that hallucinated references survive peer review at top-tier venues.

entry.title: Logit-Contribution Scoring Identifies Non-Literal Retrieval Heads

author.name: Aryo Pradipta Gema, Beatrice Alex, Pasquale Minervini

entry.summary: Introduces LOCOS, a write-aware detector that scores attention heads by how their output-value circuit projects onto the answer-token direction, identifying heads that synthesize non-literal answers rather than copy tokens. Argues prior literal-copy detectors miss the mechanism behind long-context synthesis.

entry.title: SeKV: Resolution-Adaptive KV Cache with Hierarchical Semantic Memory for Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Amirhossein Abaskohi, Giuseppe Carenini, Peter West, Yuhang He

entry.summary: SeKV is a resolution-adaptive KV cache that organizes long context into entropy-guided semantic spans and can recover token-level detail from compressed spans when they become relevant during decoding. It targets the linear KV memory bottleneck in long-context inference.

entry.title: Moral Safety in LLMs: Exposing Performative Compliance with Puzzled Cues

author.name: Mohammadamin Shafiei, Shuyue Stella Li, Yulia Tsvetkov

entry.summary: This paper shows LLM fairness evaluations overestimate moral safety: models appear fair when demographic identity is stated explicitly but become measurably less fair when identity must be inferred, a failure the authors call performative compliance. A cue-variation methodology isolates how identity presentation, not the dilemma, drives the shift.

entry.title: Bridging the Gap Between Latent and Explicit Reasoning with Looped Transformers

author.name: Ying Fan, Anej Svete, Kangwook Lee

entry.summary: This paper shows looped (recurrent-depth) Transformers can close the gap between latent and explicit chain-of-thought reasoning, where prior latent methods underperformed beyond 1B parameters. A looped padded Transformer processing K latent blocks matches explicit CoT, bridging efficient latent reasoning with performance.

entry.title: The Illusion of High Utility in Safety Alignment of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Adeel Yousaf, Soumik Ghosh, James Beetham, Amrit Singh Bedi, Mubarak Shah

entry.summary: Shows that apparent high-utility safety alignment of text-to-image diffusion models is illusory: fine-grained TIFA evaluation reveals substantial drops in semantic fidelity (object counts, attributes, relationships) masked by coarse metrics like FID and CLIPScore. It diagnoses the source in the text-conditioning pathway.

entry.title: LeVLJEPA: End-to-End Vision-Language Pretraining Without Negatives

author.name: Lukas Kuhn, Giuseppe Serra, Randall Balestriero, Florian Buettner

entry.summary: LeVLJEPA is the first fully non-contrastive end-to-end vision-language pretraining method, learning via cross-modal prediction with stop-gradient targets and per-modality distributional regularization, without negatives, temperature, momentum encoder, or teacher. It targets dense patch-token representations for use as frozen backbones.

entry.title: CausalMix: Data Mixture as Causal Inference for Language Model Training

author.name: Zinan Tang, Yukun Zhang, Shaomian Zheng, Zhuoshi Pan, Qizhi Pei, Dingnan Jin, Jun Zhou, Yujun Wang, Biqing Huang

entry.summary: Proposes CausalMix, which reframes LLM pretraining data mixture optimization as causal inference, treating data-pool statistics as covariates and domain mixture as the treatment. Fits a causal model on 512 Qwen2.5-0.5B runs so mixture weights transfer without costly retraining when the data pool shifts.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Agents with Anytime-Valid Certificates

author.name: Biswa Sengupta

entry.summary: SEA confines agent self-modification to a small steering adapter and versioned harness around a frozen base model, admitting changes only through anytime-valid statistical gates that emit auditable certificates against a fixed error budget. It provides learning-theoretic guarantees for otherwise ungovernable self-evolving agents.

entry.title: Aligning Sentence Embeddings to Human Concepts via Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Wonseok Shin, Songkuk Kim

entry.summary: This work disentangles dense sentence-transformer embeddings (e.g., E5) into human-interpretable concepts using Top-k sparse autoencoders and shows the features map to semantic, syntactic, and pragmatic categories. It adds an activation-steering mechanism to intervene precisely in retrieval by clamping concept features.

entry.title: SNAP-FM: Sparse Nonlinear Accelerated Projection for Physics-Constrained Generative Modeling

author.name: Alaina Kolli, Theodoros Xenakis, Utkarsh Utkarsh, Pengfei Cai, Rafael Gomez-Bombarelli, Alan Edelman, Christopher Vincent Rackauckas

entry.summary: SNAP-FM enforces physical constraints (conservation laws, boundary conditions, nonlinear invariants) exactly at inference time for generative surrogate models via sparse nonlinear accelerated projection, avoiding costly retraining. It exploits the sparse structure that physical constraints induce for efficient batched nonlinear optimization.

entry.title: EgoSafetyBench: A Diagnostic Egocentric Video Benchmark for Evaluating Embodied VLMs as Runtime Safety Guards

author.name: Siddhant Panpatil, Arth Singh, Mijin Koo, Chaeyun Kim, Haon Park, Dasol Choi

entry.summary: Introduces EgoSafetyBench, an egocentric robot-view video benchmark of 1,200 half-second-annotated scenarios for evaluating VLMs as streaming runtime safety guards, distinguishing genuine hazards from routine but alarming activity. It matters because binary safety benchmarks obscure the false-alarm versus miss tradeoff critical for deployable embodied guards.

entry.title: SWE-Doctor: Guiding Software Engineering Agents with Runtime Diagnosis from Multi-Faceted Bug Reproduction Tests

author.name: Yaoqi Guo, Yang Liu, Jie M. Zhang, Yun Ma, Yiling Lou, Zhenpeng Chen

entry.summary: Studies whether bug reproduction tests can help the patch-generation stage of LLM software engineering agents, finding that naive use of even fail-to-pass tests gives limited or negative gains. Proposes SWE-Doctor, which uses multi-faceted runtime diagnosis to more effectively guide patch generation.

entry.title: MemSyco-Bench: Benchmarking Sycophancy in Agent Memory

author.name: Zhishang Xiang, Zerui Chen, Yunbo Tang, Zhimin Wei, Ruqin Ning, Yujie Lin, Qinggang Zhang, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: Proposes MemSyco-Bench, a benchmark for measuring memory-induced sycophancy in LLM agents, where retrieved memories cause over-alignment with users at the cost of factual accuracy. Focuses on how memories influence downstream reasoning rather than just storage and retrieval correctness.

entry.title: Autonomous Scientific Discovery via Iterative Meta-Reflection

author.name: Bingchen Zhao, Sara Beery, Oisin Mac Aodha

entry.summary: Introduces DiscoPER, an LLM-powered autonomous research framework that generates and executes code to explore datasets without pre-specified research questions and uses meta-reflection to synthesize accumulated findings. Targets more open-ended scientific discovery than prior constrained systems.

entry.title: Triospect: A Three-Dimensional Framework for Robust Statistical AI-Generated Text Detection Against Diverse Attacks

author.name: Guangsheng Bao, Lihua Rong, Yanbin Zhao, Xiao Yu, Qiji Zhou, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: Triospect is a statistical AI-text detection framework that adds content and expression perspectives to improve robustness against paraphrasing and adversarial attacks. It reports sizable AUROC and TPR gains across 17 attacks, 12 domains, and 17 source models over strong baselines.

entry.title: Theory of Mind and Persuasion Beyond Conversation: Assessing the Capacity of LLMs to Induce Belief States via Planning and Action

author.name: Ben Slater, Matteo G. Mecattaf, Lucy G. Cheke, John Burden, Winnie Street

entry.summary: This work defines Non-Conversational Planning Theory of Mind (NCP-ToM): an agent's ability to induce specific belief states in others through actions rather than persuasive conversation, evaluated with a novel ExploreToM-based framework. It highlights both assistive uses and manipulation/misinformation risks.

entry.title: RaBitQCache: Rotated Binary Quantization for KVCache in Long Context LLM Inference

author.name: Wenhao Li, Jinhao Dong, Hailin Zhang, Wenhang Shi, Wei Lu, Xiaoyong Du

entry.summary: RaBitQCache is a sparse-attention framework for long-context inference that uses randomized rotated binary quantization and binary-INT4 arithmetic to estimate attention weights as an unbiased proxy with a proven error bound. This enables adaptive Top-p KV retrieval that adjusts the token budget to actual attention sparsity.

entry.title: Personalization as Inverse Planning: Learning Latent Design Intents for Agentic Slide Generation via Structural Denoising

author.name: Tianci Liu, Zihan Dong, Linjun Zhang, Haoyu Wang, jing Gao, Emre Kiciman, Ranveer Chandra, Wei-Ting Chen

entry.summary: SPIRE formulates page-level slide personalization as an inverse planning problem, learning latent design intents via structural denoising without assuming knowledge of the underlying rendering tool. It addresses the intractability of end-to-end optimization by corrupting and reconstructing design structure.

entry.title: Multi-scale Mixture of World Models for Embodied Agents in Evolving Environments

author.name: Jinwoo Jang, Daniel J. Rho, Sihyung Yoon, Hyunsuk Cho, Honguk Woo

entry.summary: MuSix is a mixture-of-world-models framework for embodied agents that adds scale-aware routing grounded in situational novelty and differential update rates for knowledge at different scales in evolving environments. It addresses two gaps in applying Mixture of Experts to embodied multi-scale reasoning.

entry.title: Can Agents Generalize to the Open World? Unveiling the Fragility of Static Training in Tool Use

author.name: Song-Lin Lv, Weiming Wu, Rui Zhu, Zi-Jian Cheng, Lan-Zhe Guo

entry.summary: This paper formalizes OpenAgent, an open-world tool-use setting with distributional shifts across query, action, observation, and domain dimensions, and builds a sandbox with a four-tier shift hierarchy to diagnose the fragility of statically trained tool-use agents. It reveals systematic generalization failures.

entry.title: DigitalCoach: Communication and Grounding Gaps in Human and Agentic Computer Use Coaching

author.name: Meng Chen, Anya Ji, Tsung-Han Wu, Tobias Maringgele, David M. Chan, Alane Suhr, Amy Pavel

entry.summary: DigitalCoach is a multimodal dataset of 72 expert-novice computer-use coaching sessions (22,752 dialogue turns grounded in screen and input recordings) used to evaluate whether models can teach humans to use software. Models give more direct instructions but fewer explanations, diagnoses, and knowledge checks than human coaches.

entry.title: Libra: Training the Environment for Agentic Information Retrieval

author.name: Xuan Zhao, Andy Chiu, Gengyu Wang

entry.summary: Libra is a self-evolving framework that optimizes the agent's working environment—not just the agent—by introducing mutable hierarchical Markdown catalogs into repositories, with a Prompter, frozen Solver, and Healer loop that rewrites catalogs in response to localization failures. It shows environment-side optimization improves agentic information retrieval.

entry.title: SWE-Router: Routing in Multi-turn Agentic Software Engineering Tasks

author.name: Seongho Son, Sangwoong Yoon, Jiahua Tang, Shuhan Wang, Lorenz Wolf, Ilija Bogunovic

entry.summary: SWE-Router is a value-based temporal router for multi-turn agentic software engineering that lets a cheap model run a few exploratory turns, then reads the partial trajectory to decide whether to continue cheaply or escalate to an expensive model. It proves a Bayes-optimality result overcoming the information-theoretic floor of description-only routers.

entry.title: AlgoBench: Benchmarking Algorithmic Adaptation in Code Generation

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Zekun Cai, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: AlgoBench automatically constructs novel algorithmic problems from known competitive-programming problems via structured constraint-shifting transformations that force the original reference algorithm to fail, mitigating benchmark contamination. It adds complexity-aware metrics beyond pass@k to test genuine algorithmic adaptation.

entry.title: Scaling Up Thermodynamic AI Models

author.name: Andrew G. Moore

entry.summary: This paper turns the theoretical correspondence between high-temperature Gibbs-sampled Ising systems and feed-forward inference into a scalable backpropagation-based training algorithm for deep convolutional networks on Ising-machine hardware, reaching 94.9% on CIFAR-10 and 76.0% on CIFAR-100 under binary Gibbs sampling. It advances low-power thermodynamic AI inference.

entry.title: Learning Generalizable Skill Policy with Data-Efficient Unsupervised RL

author.name: Jongchan Park, Seungjun Oh, Seungho Baek, Yusung Kim

entry.summary: Flow-Map GRPO is an online RL post-training framework for deterministic few-step flow-map generators (e.g., consistency models, MeanFlow), using Anchored Stochastic Composition to introduce well-defined stochastic trajectories and likelihood ratios. It extends RL post-training to a class of fast samplers previously incompatible with policy-gradient methods.

entry.title: Beyond the Prompt: Jailbreaking Function-Calling LLMs via Simulated Moderation Traces

author.name: Junlong Liu, Haobo Wang, Weiqi Luo, Xiaojun Jia

entry.summary: Demonstrates SMT, a black-box jailbreak against function-calling LLMs that exploits the interleaving of developer schemas, structured arguments, and untrusted tool outputs in a shared context, distributing adversarial intent across multi-turn execution. It reveals a structural vulnerability beyond prompt-level attacks.

entry.title: Post-Training Pruning for Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Chengzhi Hu, Xuewen Liu, Jing Zhang, Mengjuan Chen, Zhikai Li, Qingyi Gu

entry.summary: Develops a post-training pruning method tailored to Diffusion Transformers, arguing that LLM-derived pruning metrics fail because of DiTs' distinct weight magnitudes and structure. Proposes saliency and granularity choices suited to DiT architecture to cut compute with less performance loss.

entry.title: Muon as a Residual Connection

author.name: Hao Huang

entry.summary: Offers a mechanistic interpretation of the Muon optimizer as an implicit residual connection, arguing that orthogonalizing updates sacrifices immediate gradient fidelity to better preserve representations for downstream layers. Studies this trade-off in controlled linear settings.

entry.title: When Reranking Hurts: Uncertainty-Based Gating for Few-Shot Reranking

author.name: Orian Dabod, Amir DN Cohen, Gabriel Stanovsky

entry.summary: This work challenges the assumption that reranking retrieved few-shot examples always helps, showing it can degrade performance, and proposes a training-free gating rule that reranks only under high model uncertainty. Across 8 LLMs and many datasets it cuts compute 15-80% while slightly improving accuracy.

entry.title: Can LLMs Imagine Moral Alternatives Beyond Binary Dilemmas?

author.name: Jongchan Choi, Nari Yang, Sung Soo Park, Jaemin Cho, Han Seoyoung, Haerin Shin, Jun-Hyung Park

entry.summary: This paper introduces MoralAltDataset (307 dilemmas) to test whether LLMs can imagine compromise or reframed alternatives beyond given binary moral options, mirroring a key aspect of human moral cognition. Across 15 LLMs, compromise alternatives are often preferred, substantially reshaping model moral choices.

entry.title: Beyond Compilation: Evaluating Faithful Natural-Language-to-Lean Statement Formalization

author.name: Ke Zhang, Patricio Gallardo Candela, Sudhir Murthy, Yi Xie, Zhi Wang, Maziar Raissi

entry.summary: This paper studies faithful natural-language-to-Lean statement formalization, noting compilation alone does not guarantee correctness since a type-checking declaration may drop hypotheses or be vacuous. On a 400-entry graduate benchmark it combines compilation, cross-model semantic judging, and human calibration to attribute bottlenecks.

entry.title: QVal: Cheaply Evaluating Dense Supervision Signals for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Sergio Hern\'andez-Guti\'errez, Matteo Merler, Ilze Amanda Auzina, Joschka Str\"uber, Ameya Prabhu, Matthias Bethge

entry.summary: QVal provides a cheap way to evaluate dense supervision signals for long-horizon LLM agents without running full training pipelines, disentangling supervision quality from training-engineering confounders. It enables fair comparison across intrinsic-confidence, self-distillation, and embedding-similarity methods that otherwise require distinct setups.

entry.title: Persona Without Substrate: Regime-Dependence and the LLM Individuation Problem

author.name: Shuaizhi Cheng

entry.summary: This paper challenges the assumption that a persona direction refers to the same content across prompting, fine-tuning, and inference-time steering, presenting four empirical wedges from persona-topology experiments on Qwen3-4B and Mistral-7B showing regime-dependence. It bears on the LLM individuation problem and persona-vector interpretability.

entry.title: PRA-RAG: Provably Robust Aggregation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation against Retrieval Corruption

author.name: Xue Tan, Yi Zheng, Chang Huo, Yunruo Zhang, Yu Liu, Hao Luan, Zhuyang Yu, Xiaoyan Sun, Ping Chen, Jun Dai

entry.summary: PRA-RAG is a provably robust retrieval aggregation algorithm defending RAG against corpus poisoning by sampling combinations of retrieved texts and using embedding-space geometry to identify a robust subset. It provides theoretical robustness guarantees where prior defenses lacked them.

entry.title: Harnessing the Latent Space: From Steering Vectors to Model Calibrators for Control and Trust

author.name: Nishant Subramani

entry.summary: This paper (dissertation-style) summarizes contributions on harnessing LLM latent spaces: steering vectors for behavioral control and latent-space-based calibrators for trust, aiming to establish control over model behavior and know when to trust outputs. It targets demystifying internal representations of large models.

entry.title: SLIM-RL: Risk-Budgeted Random-Masking RL for Diffusion LLMs Without Trajectory Slicing

author.name: Ruikang Zhao, Zhenting Wang, Han Gao, Ligong Han

entry.summary: SLIM-RL is a reinforcement-learning method for diffusion LLMs that avoids expensive trajectory reconstruction by bounding the commit risk of each rollout step with a budgeted decoder and training on risk-controlled rollouts using a trace-free random-masking objective. It challenges the assumption that random masking must be trajectory-aligned.

entry.title: NeuroCogMap Reveals Cognitive Organization of Large Language Models

author.name: Zhongxiang Sun, Haolang Lu, Qiang Ma, Qi Li, Qipeng Wang, Liang Pang, Chenyu Liu, Qiankun Li, Hao Sun, Kun Wang, Yi Zeng, Jun Xu, Guoqi Li, Ji-Rong Wen

entry.summary: NeuroCogMap organizes internal LLM features into functional parcels linked to interpretable cognitive functions and a cognitive hierarchy, drawing on cognitive-neuroscience methods. It finds stable, semantically coherent functional organization partly conserved across models.

entry.title: Active-GRPO: Adaptive Imitation and Self-Improving Reasoning for Molecular Optimization

author.name: Xuefeng Liu, Mingxuan Cao, Qinan Huang, Thomas Brettin, Rick Stevens, Le Cong

entry.summary: Active-GRPO proposes active reasoning for instruction-based molecular optimization, where the policy actively imitates and self-improves beyond dataset references, overcoming the performance ceiling imposed by weak reference-guided policy optimization. It combines SFT robustness with RLVR self-improvement for scientific reasoning.

entry.title: FinPersona-Bench: A Benchmark for Longitudinal Psychometric Stability of Autonomous Financial Agents

author.name: Muhammad Usman Safder (Steve), Ayesha Gull (Steve), Rania Elbadry (Steve), Fan Zhang (Steve), Yankai Chen (Steve), Xueqing Peng (Steve), Xue (Steve), Liu, Preslav Nakov, Zhuohan Xie

entry.summary: FinPersona-Bench measures Mandate Salience Decay, the tendency of autonomous financial agents to gradually ignore initial behavioral mandates over long horizons, using a simulated market that decouples price from hidden fundamentals. It enables falsifiable evaluation across failure modes like panic-selling and trading without signal.

entry.title: STEB: Style Text Embedding Benchmark

author.name: Rafael Rivera Soto, Anna Wegmann, Cristina Aggazzotti

entry.summary: STEB introduces a comprehensive open benchmark for style text embeddings spanning 96 datasets and 7 languages, covering authorship verification, AI-text detection, and stylistic probing. It finds semantic embeddings fail on stylistic tasks and no single style embedding dominates.

entry.title: When LLMs Read Tables Carelessly: Measuring and Reducing Data Referencing Errors

author.name: Yuqing Yang, Qi Zhu, Zhen Han, Boran Han, Zhengyuan Shen, Shuai Wang, Vassilis N. Ioannidis, Huzefa Rangwala

entry.summary: This paper provides the first systematic study of data referencing errors, where LLMs miscite or omit table values despite understanding structure, showing DREs occur across all tested models (1.7B-20B). Using data referencing as a critic improves answer accuracy by up to 12%.

entry.title: Segmenting, Fast and Slow: Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Video Instance Segmentation with Dual-Path Processing

author.name: Luca Barsellotti, Martin Sundermeyer, Mattia Segu, Nikita Araslanov, Muhammad Ferjad Naeem, Marcella Cornia, Yongqin Xian, Maxim Berman

entry.summary: SegFS is a dual-stream fast-slow framework for real-time open-vocabulary video instance segmentation, running an object-based open-vocabulary model on sparse keyframes and projecting representations to condition a lightweight fast network on other frames. It targets high-frame-rate on-device inference without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: Testing Frontier Large Language Models' Physics Literacy in Parallel Physical Worlds

author.name: Dong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a four-stage auditable diagnostic (induction, formulation, prediction, review) to test whether frontier LLMs can reason within unfamiliar physics frameworks rather than recall patterns, using counterfactual and historical physics worlds. It uses pre-registrations, fresh sessions, and dual-LLM judging to isolate genuine reasoning.

entry.title: What's Hidden Matters: Identifying Planning-Critical Occluded Agents using Vision-Language Models

author.name: Amirhosein Chahe, Tyler Naes, Jovin D'sa, Faizan M. Tariq, Sangjae Bae, Lifeng Zhou, David Isele

entry.summary: Introduces a framework using Planning KL-divergence to let VLMs identify and rank occluded agents by their impact on an autonomous vehicle's planned trajectory, bridging perception and planning. It reduces overly conservative driving by focusing attention on planning-critical hidden agents.

entry.title: When AI meets quantum information: A comprehensive review

author.name: Min Chen, Yu Gan, Xin Jin, Yuqing Li, Junqi Wang, Zeguan Wu, Yunfei Wang, Bingzhi Zhang, Priyam Srivastava, Tianlong Chen, Ankit Kulshrestha, Yuan Liu, Juan Jos\'e Mendoza-Arenas, Kaushik P. Seshadreesan, Sarvagya Upadhyay, Xueyue Zhang, Quntao Zhuang, Junyu Liu

entry.summary: A comprehensive bidirectional review of the AI and quantum information interface, covering AI for quantum (learning from measurements, algorithm discovery, hardware stabilization) and quantum for AI (quantum computation and representations for learning). It organizes a rapidly co-evolving field.

entry.title: Self-conditioned Flow Map Language Models via Fixed-point Flows

author.name: Jaehoon Yoo, Wonjung Kim, Floor Eijkelboom, Chanhyuk Lee, Nicholas M. Boffi, Seunghoon Hong, Jinwoo Kim

entry.summary: Shows that self-conditioning in continuous flow-based language models can be understood as a fixed-point iteration that bootstraps the denoiser, and introduces fixed-point flows, a two-dimensional class of self-conditioned flows extending the idea to few-step flow-map generators. It provides theoretical grounding for a previously ill-understood empirical technique.

entry.title: Human-Machine Collaboration on Generative Meta-Learning: Model and Algorithm

author.name: Midhun Parakkal Unni, Samuel Kaski

entry.summary: Proposes GMHF, a generative meta-learning framework that uses human beliefs about target-domain physics to guide synthetic data generation via a conditional Neural ODE digital twin plus RL. Derives generalization bounds showing that aligning generated data with expert intuition reduces risk under domain shift.

entry.title: FAR: Failure-Aware Retry for Test-Time Recovery and Continual Policy Improvement

author.name: Haoran Hao, Shahram Najam Syed, Jeffrey Ichnowski, Jeff Schneider

entry.summary: Introduces FAR, a framework letting robots learn from prior failures at test time via failure-contrastive preference adaptation and lightweight action perturbations, then folds successful recoveries into a continual training loop. Aims for autonomous recovery without human intervention.

entry.title: TAG-DLM: Diffusion Language Models for Text-Attributed Graph Learning

author.name: Lingjie Chen, Yuanchen Bei, Haobo Xu, Yanjun Zhao, Yuzhong Chen, Hanghang Tong

entry.summary: TAG-DLM unifies textual reasoning and graph message passing inside a single masked diffusion language model for text-attributed graphs, linearizing local neighborhoods into token sequences with topology-aware attention. It avoids the common split between shallow text encoders and separate graph modules.

entry.title: BlockPilot: Instance-Adaptive Policy Learning for Diffusion-based Speculative Decoding

author.name: Hao Zhang, Yiming Hu, Yong Wang, Mingqiao Mo, Xin Xiao, Xiangxiang Chu

entry.summary: BlockPilot learns an instance-adaptive policy for choosing block sizes in diffusion-based speculative decoding, showing the optimal block size varies per sample and exhibits local structure. This yields lossless acceleration improvements over fixed-block-size baselines.

entry.title: Revising RVL-CDIP: Quantifying Errors and Test-Train Overlap

author.name: Stefan Larson, Attila Nagy, Sam Desai, Cyrus Desai, Nicole C. Lima, Yixin Yuan, Siddharth Betala, Kaushal K. Prajapati, Jamiu T. Suleiman, Sharad Duwal, Kevin Leach

entry.summary: The authors audit the widely used RVL-CDIP document-classification dataset, finding roughly 12% label error and about 35% test-train overlap, then release corrected variants and rebenchmark. Fixing these issues changes measured classification performance.

entry.title: Robust Text Watermarking for Large Language Models via Dual Semantic Embeddings

author.name: Jonas Sch\"afer, Cezary Pilaszewicz, Gerhard Wunder

entry.summary: DEW is a semantic LLM watermarking scheme that combines contextual and token-level embeddings with signal-processing vector operations and pseudo-random projections to survive paraphrasing and translation. It reports improved robustness to semantic shifts across multiple LLMs.

entry.title: CLExEval: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Qualitative Evaluation of LLM Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Ajmal M., Abin Roy, Afthab Salam Kanniyan, Jawadh Abdul Kabeer, Jerin James, Preslav Nakov, Zhuohan Xie

entry.summary: CLExEval is a human-in-the-loop framework evaluating LLM clinical reasoning under progressive information masking, using 5,600 physician annotations over 200 reasoning traces from 40 rare cases. It exposes failure patterns such as verbosity bias, where accuracy collapses under information scarcity.

entry.title: Explicit Fuzzy Logic in the Feed-Forward Layer: Self-Forgetting Quantifiers Discover Legible Grammatical-Licensing Detectors

author.name: Mark Oskin

entry.summary: This paper replaces transformer feed-forward units with explicit fuzzy-logic operations on sigmoid-bounded memberships, including a negation-capable set-difference operation, to make FFN computation legible. At 125M scale it matches GELU perplexity while every unit carries explicit logical form, and it discovers interpretable grammatical-licensing detectors.

entry.title: Scalable Behaviour Cloning on Browser Using via Skill Distillation

author.name: Kaisen Yang, Zheng Jiang, Yuzhao Peng, Houde Qian, Boshi Zhang, Youjie Zheng, Shijin Hong, Qingle Liu, Ruoyu Han, Bohan Lyu, Bingxiang He, Eren Cai, Calvin Xiao, Qinhuai Na

entry.summary: This paper argues browser-agent bottlenecks are decision-making under incomplete information, and proposes scalable behavior cloning that distills human interaction traces into compact natural-language skills agents can retrieve and compose. It leverages abundant human browsing as a source of reusable priors.

entry.title: Generative Skill Composition for LLM Agents

author.name: Xinyu Zhao, Zhen Tan, Vaishnav Tadiparthi, Nakul Agarwal, Kwonjoon Lee, Ehsan Moradi Pari, Hossein Nourkhiz Mahjoub, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: This work frames selecting an appropriate skill composition for LLM agents as a joint, structural decision rather than either exposing the full skill library or embedding-based retrieval. It proposes a generative approach to compose skills as growing libraries make selection the central bottleneck.

entry.title: ADAPT: Attention Dynamics Alignment with Preference Tuning for Faithful MLLMs

author.name: Zhiyuan Yao, Zheren Fu, Zhixiao Zheng, Jiajun Li, Yi Tu, Zhendong Mao

entry.summary: ADAPT identifies an internal signature of MLLM hallucination, progressive degradation of text-to-image cross-attention, and directly intervenes on cross-attention dynamics via preference tuning with a refined visual anchor. It targets this failure mode more explicitly than outcome-driven mitigation strategies.

entry.title: Modality-Driven Search with Holistic Trace Judging for ARC-AGI-2

author.name: Johan Land

entry.summary: This solver for the ARC-AGI-2 abstract-reasoning benchmark treats text, image, and code channels as independent search operators to generate diverse candidates, then uses a judge model to holistically compare all reasoning traces in one long-context prompt. It reliably recovers correct minority hypotheses that self-consistency or majority voting miss.

entry.title: PixelEyes: Decoupling Perception and Reasoning for Pinpoint Visual Evidence Seeking

author.name: Dengxian Gong, Yuanzheng Wu, Haobo Yuan, Zhengdong Hu, Tao Zhang, Yikang Zhou, Shihao Chen, Quanzhu Niu, Kai Wang, Jason Li, Haochen Wang, Lu Qi, Shunping Ji, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: PixelEyes is a multi-turn visual reasoning agent that decouples reasoning from perception: a reasoner decides what to look for while a specialized referring-segmentation tool answers where it is, avoiding the redundant trajectories caused by entangled reasoning and localization. It uses mask-guided visual search for pixel-precise grounding.

entry.title: AI Native Games: A Survey and Roadmap

author.name: Zhiyue Xu, Fandi Meng, Kaijie Xu, Clark Verbrugge, Simon Lucas, Jian Zhao

entry.summary: This survey defines AI-native games by a counterfactual criterion—whether runtime generative AI is constitutive of the core play loop—and analyzes 53 games and prototypes to distinguish them from AI-augmented titles. It provides a roadmap for the emerging field.

entry.title: Self-GC: Self-Governing Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Xubin Hao, Hongjin Meng, Xin Yin, Jiawei Zhu, Chenpeng Cao

entry.summary: Self-GC turns long-horizon agent context (user turns, tool spans, skill state) into indexed objects and lets the system govern their lifecycle rather than relying on chronological pruning or final self-summary. The garbage-collection analogy captures managing dependencies and preserving exact evidence.

entry.title: Why Advanced Encoders Lag on Sparse Retrieval? The Answer and an Approach to Bridging Vocabulary Gaps

author.name: Zhichao Geng, Yang Yang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a vocabulary gap explaining why modern encoders like ModernBERT underperform older BERT on learned sparse retrieval—raw case-sensitive tokenizers waste capacity on morphological noise—and proposes vocabulary coarse-graining supported by a generalization-bound analysis. It offers a theory plus mitigation for lexical matching.

entry.title: Multi-Hypothesis Test-Time Adaptation to Mitigate Underspecification

author.name: Afshar Shamsi, Xiao-Yu Guo, Hamid Alinejad-Rokny, Arash Mohammadi, Damien Teney, Ehsan Abbasnejad

entry.summary: Reinterprets test-time adaptation through a posterior lens and introduces a particle-based diversification method to address underspecification, where multiple low-entropy parameter updates yield divergent decision boundaries. Aims to make TTA more robust and less prone to collapse.

entry.title: Validating Causal Abstraction Metrics on Simulated Complex Systems

author.name: Maxime M\'eloux, Tiago Pimentel, Fran\c{c}ois Portet, Maxime Peyrard

entry.summary: Builds a benchmark of ten complex systems with ground-truth causal explanations and evaluates over thirty candidate causal-abstraction metrics, finding only causal-family metrics reliably distinguish valid from invalid high-level explanations. This provides much-needed rigor to measuring explanation validity.

entry.title: LLVM-Bench: Benchmarking and Advancing Large Language Models for LLVM Compiler Issue Resolution

author.name: Zhao Tian, Yingquan Zhao, Chenyao Suo, Meng Wang, Junjie Chen

entry.summary: Introduces LLVM-Bench (423 validated real-world tasks) and LLVM-Gym (automated reproduction, patch, build, test) to evaluate LLMs on complex system-level compiler issue resolution, studying four LLMs and six retrieval configurations. It extends software-issue-resolution evaluation to a demanding compiler codebase.

entry.title: CAT: Confidence-Adaptive Thinking for Efficient Reasoning of Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Qizhi Jiang, Shuo Wang, Pei Ke, Yuhang Song, Ke Qin

entry.summary: CAT (Confidence-Adaptive Thinking) incorporates a model's intrinsic self-certainty signals into preference optimization to autonomously modulate chain-of-thought length by problem difficulty, reducing overthinking on simple queries. It addresses token overhead in large reasoning models without degrading hard-problem performance.

entry.title: EchoRisk: A Multicentre Echocardiography Dataset and Benchmark for Cardio-Oncology

author.name: Grigorios Kalliatakis, Georgia Karanasiou, Georgios Manikis, Manolis Tsiknakis, Dimitrios Fotiadis, Dorothea Tsekoura, Kalliopi Keramida, Vasileios Bouratzis, Lampros Lakkas, Katerina Naka, Andri Papakonstantinou, Anastasia Constantinidou, Kostas Marias

entry.summary: Releases EchoRisk, a curated multicentre longitudinal echocardiography dataset with explicit cardiotoxicity labels from 422 breast cancer patients across five European sites, serving as the reference for a MICCAI 2026 challenge. Targets automated early risk stratification for therapy-induced cardiotoxicity.

entry.title: Probing Stylistic Appropriation using Large Language Models: An Evaluation Framework for Copyright Infringement under EU Law

author.name: Noah Scharrenberg, Chang Sun

entry.summary: PSALM is an LLM-as-a-judge framework operationalizing EU copyright doctrine (substantial similarity across style, narrative, and content) through ten evaluators, going beyond verbatim-memorization safeguards. It aims to close the compliance gap between what detectors catch and what law protects.

entry.title: From Search to Synthesis: Training LLMs as Zero-Shot Workflow Generators

author.name: Gan Luo, Zihan Qin, Bin Dong, Wotao Yin

entry.summary: This paper trains LLMs to generate reusable, task-level workflows that encode recurring algorithmic patterns instead of instance-specific solutions, improving robustness, interpretability, and reusability. It aims to overcome both manual workflow design and the poor generalization of existing automatic methods.

entry.title: Revocable Learned State via Process Sidecars

author.name: John Sweeney

entry.summary: This work studies revoking learned memory after a later safety-training phase has transported the memory direction, showing simple update subtraction is insufficient. It introduces process sidecars, a two-coefficient edit family that corrects for how the safety optimizer moved the memory update.

entry.title: ShopX: A Foundation Model for Intent-to-Item Fulfillment in Agentic Shopping

author.name: Jiacheng Chen, Tao Zhang, Manxi Lin, Dunxian Huang, Teng Shi, Honghao Fu, Mengyan Li, Xinming Zhang, Chenchi Zhang, Xuan Lu, Xiaoxiong Du, Haibin Chen, Shaolin Ye, Hao Chang, Xiaoqi Li, Shuwen Xiao, Yujin Yuan, Jingxuan Feng, Shaopan Xiong, Huimin Yi, Ju Huang, Qiu Shen, Ying Chen, Junjun Zheng, Xiangheng Kong, Yuning Jiang

entry.summary: ShopX is a foundation model for agentic shopping that unifies intent understanding, execution planning, and semantic-ID-native item-space operations, moving beyond wrapping an LLM around existing search/recommendation pipelines. It aims to translate flexible intents directly into item-space fulfillment rather than only generating retrieval candidates.

entry.title: Decompose, Compare, and Decide: Multimodal LLMs are Implicit Few-Shot Learners

author.name: Yunhan Wang, Eshika Khandelwal, Edson Araujo, Walid Bousselham, Nina Shvetsova, Hilde Kuehne

entry.summary: DeCoDe turns off-the-shelf MLLMs into strong few-shot image classifiers without training by decomposing classification into pairwise same-class binary comparisons and using the affirmative logit as a similarity score. It reframes few-shot classification as a set of image comparisons that MLLMs handle implicitly.

entry.title: Model access for third-parties — it's a big deal!

author.name: Cleo Nardo

entry.summary: Argues that a growing gap between insider (frontier-lab) and outsider model access threatens external safety work, and that securing model access parity should be a top priority for the safety community over the next year. It frames parity as potentially more valuable than scaling outsider headcount.

entry.title: Mnemosyne: Agentic Transaction Processing for Validating and Repairing AI-generated Workflows

author.name: Edward Y. Chang, Longling Geng, Emily J. Chang

entry.summary: Mnemosyne introduces Agentic Transaction Processing, treating AI-generated workflow actions as untrusted proposals admitted only after deterministic checks against an executable constraint set, with reactive repair for unforeseen disruptions. It aims to prevent stale, infeasible, or destructive committed actions in agent workflows.

entry.title: Managed Autonomy at Runtime: Gear-Based Safety and Governance for Single- and Multi-Agent Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: Srini Ramaswamy, Wang Miaosheng

entry.summary: This work presents a discrete-time gear-based control system with five execution modes and utility-gated dispatch to enforce safety and governance for single- and multi-agent cyber-physical systems, proving stability, safety, and MDP-equivalence properties. It targets failure modes of agents operating without continuous human oversight.

entry.title: PHREEQC-MCQ-200: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Tool-Augmented Scientific Simulator Agents

author.name: Ke Zhang, Sahchit Chundur, Mohammad Javad Qomi, Maziar Raissi

entry.summary: PHREEQC-MCQ-200 is a benchmark of 200 multiple-choice questions over 21 geochemistry simulation scenarios to test whether tool-augmented LLM agents can construct simulator inputs, run PHREEQC, and interpret outputs. Results confirm simulator access substantially improves scientific-computation accuracy.

entry.title: Holographic Quantum Transformer: A Generalist Neuro-Symbolic Architecture for Solving Frustrated Systems via Generative Attention

author.name: Xingran Guo, Tiaojie Xiao, Jie Liu, Keqin Li

entry.summary: Introduces the Holographic Quantum Transformer, a generative-attention neural network for simulating 2D frustrated quantum matter, reaching accurate ground-state energy on the J1-J2 Heisenberg model at the critical point. It also shows the model recovers underlying physical interactions.

entry.title: MindEdit-Bench: Benchmarking Object-Level Counterfactual Spatial Reasoning in VLMs from In-the-Wild Photos

author.name: Leyuan Yu, Xiao Tang, Minghao Liu, Xinyuan Li, Xiaokai Bai, Sheng Zhou, Qunshu Lin, Weihao Xuan, Naoto Yokoya

entry.summary: MindEdit-Bench introduces object-level counterfactual spatial reasoning tasks (spatial editing and cross-view visibility editing) built from in-the-wild smartphone photo triplets, going beyond observational spatial reasoning in VLMs. It probes whether models can predict consequences of hypothetically moving or rotating objects.

entry.title: Cross4D-JEPA: Dense Cross-modal Correspondence Distillation for 4D Point Cloud Representation Learning

author.name: Trung Thanh Nguyen, Hai Nguyen-Truong, Tu Vo, Hoang M. Truong, Tuan-Anh Vu

entry.summary: Cross4D-JEPA distills frozen 2D foundation models (DINOv2, V-JEPA 2) into a 4D point encoder via dense cross-modal correspondence, preserving per-patch semantics rather than a single global embedding for self-supervised 4D point cloud representation learning. It targets transferable representations without dense annotation.

entry.title: Aionoscope: Debugging Latent-State Accessibility in Time-Series Representations

author.name: Alexander Chemeris, Ming Jin, Randall Balestriero

entry.summary: Introduces Aionoscope, a generator-based diagnostic that tests whether frozen time-series representations preserve inspectable process state such as phase, amplitude, and regime, using seeded synthetic streams with exact labels. Evaluates 37 model-plus-adapter systems with a common linear-probe protocol.

entry.title: Skills Are Not Islands: Measuring Dependency and Risk in Agent Skill Supply Chains

author.name: Changguo Jia, Tianqi Zhao, Runzhi He, Minghui Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces the concept of Agent Skill Supply Chains and SkillDepAnalyzer to capture natural-language dependency evidence and model reusable LLM agent skills as dependency-bearing artifacts, analogous to software bills of materials. Evaluated on a SKILL-DEP benchmark to recover skill metadata and dependencies.

entry.title: Adversarial Pragmatics for AI Safety Evaluation: A Benchmark for Instruction Conflict, Embedded Commands, and Policy Ambiguity

author.name: Brett Reynolds

entry.summary: Introduces adversarial pragmatics as a benchmark and annotation protocol to evaluate LLM behavior under instruction conflict, embedded commands, quotation, scope ambiguity, deixis, and multi-turn agentic interaction. Aims to move safety evaluation beyond opaque pass/fail labels toward diagnosing why failures occur.

entry.title: Diffusion-GR2: Diffusion Generative Reasoning Re-ranker

author.name: Zhuoxuan Zhang (Yang), Kangqi Ni (Yang), Yuhang Chen (Yang), Mingfu Liang (Yang), Xiaohan Wei (Yang), Yunchen Pu (Yang), Fei Tian (Yang), Chonglin Sun (Yang), Frank Shyu (Yang), Adam (Yang), Song, Sandeep Pandey, Luke Simon, Tianlong Chen, Xi Liu

entry.summary: Presents Diffusion-GR2, a block-diffusion reasoning re-ranker for recommendation that decodes reasoning tokens in parallel to cut the latency of autoregressive generative re-rankers. Addresses structural gaps where parallel decoding produces invalid rankings with duplicated or dropped identifiers.

entry.title: Seeing Is Not Sharing: Some Vision-Language Models Overestimate Common Ground in Asymmetric Dialogue

author.name: Nan Li, Albert Gatt, Massimo Poesio

entry.summary: Using 13,077 annotated reference expressions from MapTask dialogues, this paper tests whether vision-language models distinguish what could be shared from what has actually been grounded between dialogue partners. It finds VLMs over-predict alignment, overestimating common ground in asymmetric dialogue.

entry.title: ViTL: Temporal Logic-Guided Zero-Shot Natural Language Navigation via Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kaier Liang, Hengde Dai, Cristian-Ioan Vasile

entry.summary: ViTL enables zero-shot natural-language robot navigation to multiple targets under temporal and logical ordering constraints by extracting temporal-logic specifications from commands and guiding VLM-based frontier exploration. It handles multi-target, temporally constrained commands that prior single-target systems cannot.

entry.title: When Does Learning to Stop Help? A Cost-Aware Study of Early Exits in Reasoning Models

author.name: Zhe Dong (University of Maine at Presque Isle), Fang Qin (Stanford University), Manish Shah (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: This cost-aware study introduces LearnStop, a hidden-state-free checkpoint stopper that predicts prefix correctness from online features (confidence, entropy, vote share, stability, backtracking density) to decide when reasoning models should stop. Across 18 task-model settings, whether learned stopping beats simple thresholds is task-dependent.

entry.title: RCT: A Robot-Collected Touch-Vision-Language Dataset for Tactile Generalization

author.name: Jingbo He, Michael F\"arber, Roberto Calandra

entry.summary: RCT is a robot-collected touch-vision-language dataset with 29,279 tactile frames from full robot presses on 122 industrial materials across 7 categories using three DIGIT sensors. It preserves each press as a contact sequence, enabling held-out evaluation across materials, sensors, and positions, and shows that removing contact-sequence overlap is crucial for honest generalization estimates.

entry.title: MECoBench: A Systematic Study of Multimodal Agent Collaboration in Embodied Environments

author.name: Qingyun Liu, Jiwen Zhang, Jingyi Hu, Siyuan Wang, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: MECoBench is a multimodal embodied cooperation benchmark with an evaluation platform spanning diverse tasks, two cooperation structures, and three collaboration modes to study how MLLM agents collaborate in visually grounded environments. Findings include that collaboration generally helps but benefits depend on balancing gains against coordination complexity.

entry.title: Theoria: Rewrite-Acceptability Verification over Informal Reasoning States

author.name: Ben Slivinski, Michael Saldivar

entry.summary: Theoria is a verification architecture that rewrites candidate solutions into sequences of typed state transitions, each licensed by an explicit auditable justification, enforcing completeness of change so hidden premises surface. It seeks a middle ground between formal proof assistants and opaque scalar LLM judges.

entry.title: LLMs in the Real World: Evaluating "AI" in Emergency Contexts

author.name: Sara Court, Lara Downing, Micha Elsner

entry.summary: This position paper and case study examines a text-to-911 machine-translation deployment advertising 55 languages, identifying common public misconceptions about such AI and offering concrete recommendations for responsible development and communication. It urges researchers to better articulate findings to the public in high-stakes contexts.

entry.title: BaseRT: Best-in-Class LLM Inference on Apple Silicon via Native Metal

author.name: Prabod Rathnayaka, Fabian Waschkowski, Lukas Wesemann

entry.summary: BaseRT is a native Metal inference runtime for LLMs on Apple Silicon, using chip-specific kernel fusion and unified-memory-aware optimization to reportedly achieve the highest inference throughput to date on that hardware. It supports Qwen3, Llama 3.2, and Gemma 4 across eight quantization formats.

entry.title: LUMA: Benchmarking Segmentation via a Lightweight Universal Mask Adapter

author.name: Tobias Christian Nauen, Anosh Billimoria, Federico Raue, Stanislav Frolov, Brian B. Moser, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: LUMA is a lightweight, backbone-agnostic mask-transformer head that treats any backbone as a black-box feature extractor, enabling fair benchmarking of 20 backbones and 11 pretraining schemes for segmentation while matching state-of-the-art efficiency. It disentangles backbone quality from decoder and recipe confounds.

entry.title: Recovering Input Text from Hidden States: Study of Gradient-Based Inversion of Decoder-Only Language Models

author.name: Miko{\l}aj S{\l}owikowski, Maciej Witold Majewski

entry.summary: Studies gradient-based inversion of decoder-only LLMs to recover original input token sequences from last-layer hidden states, treating it as continuous embedding-space optimization with token commitment only at the end. It exposes internal signals like ground-truth rank trajectories and per-position loss curves.

entry.title: Sequentially-Controlled Interactive Multi-Particle Flow-Maps for Online Feedback-Driven Search

author.name: Binglin Ji, Anindya Sarkar, Hengchang Lu, Jens Sj\"olund, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik

entry.summary: duplicate

entry.title: What Counts as an Error? Dual-Reference Benchmarking for Atypical ASR

author.name: Hawau Olamide Toyin, Srinivasan Umesh, Hanan Aldarmaki

entry.summary: The paper argues that atypical (e.g., stuttered) speech has two valid transcription references, verbatim and intended, and that conflating them biases ASR evaluation toward deleting disfluencies. It benchmarks 11 ASR models under both references to expose this evaluation gap.

entry.title: CHERRY: Compressed Hierarchical Experts with Recurrent Representational Yield

author.name: Dohyeon Kwon, Youngjin Park

entry.summary: CHERRY studies three techniques for compute-efficient LM training, notably Selective Ground Truth Token Training that concentrates supervision on ~15% of semantically meaningful tokens yet still improves the other 85% via gradient coupling. It provides a theoretical guarantee for this transfer effect.

entry.title: UniSAE: Unified Speech Attribute Editing on Speaker, Emotion and Low-Level Content via Discrete Phonetic Posteriorgram Modelling

author.name: Chuanbo Zhu, Wuyou Zhou, Rongxiu Zhong, Shilei Zhang, Kun Qian, Yike Guo, Wei Xue

entry.summary: UniSAE is a unified speech-attribute editing framework supporting composable speaker, emotion, and content edits from sub-phoneme to word level via a Discrete Phonetic PosteriorGram representation. This factorizes content into tokens encoding phoneme identity, pronunciation variants, and duration for fine-grained editing.

entry.title: PruneGround: Plug-and-play Spatial Pruning for 3D Visual Grounding

author.name: Duc Cao Dinh, Khai Le-Duc, Florent Draye, Chris Ngo, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Zhijing Jin

entry.summary: PruneGround is a plug-and-play framework for 3D visual grounding that uses a frozen VLM to identify language-relevant spatial regions, pruning the scene to reduce ambiguity and computation. It exploits the observation that referential expressions often correspond to restricted spatial regions.

entry.title: The Decomposition Is the Fingerprint: Per-Component Identity for Agent Skills

author.name: Hongliang Liu, Yuhao Wu, Tung-Ling Li

entry.summary: This work proposes a locality-sensitive fingerprint for governing runtime-acquired agent skills, embedding each skill component and projecting to bits via multi-bank SimHash into a compact 120-byte signature comparable by Hamming distance. Keeping the fingerprint as a per-component triple (prompt, code, tools) is what makes it useful for recognizing near-duplicate or modified skills.

entry.title: A CERN for AI is a distraction; push for an IAEA instead

author.name: Charbel-Raphaël

entry.summary: Argues that the politically realistic version of a CERN for AI would do little for safety, while the safety-effective versions are unrealistic, so it is a distraction. It advocates instead for an international treaty with red lines followed by an IAEA-style verification body, drawing on precedents like the NPT and Montreal Protocol.

entry.title: LLM-Guided ODE Discovery and Parameter Inference from Small-Cohort Aggregate Data

author.name: Hanning Yang, Meropi Karakioulaki, Lennart Purucker, Tim Litwin, Cristina Has, Moritz Hess

entry.summary: Presents an LLM-guided method that jointly discovers ODE structure and refines parameter distributions from small-cohort population-level summary statistics, targeting rare-disease modeling where individual data is scarce, noisy, and privacy-constrained. It models parameters as distributions to capture heterogeneity.

entry.title: Cheap Code, Costly Judgment: A Case Study on Governable Agentic Software Engineering

author.name: James C. Davis, Paschal C. Amusuo, Tanmay Singla, Berk \c{C}akar, Kirsten A. Davis

entry.summary: A 12-week first-person case study in which an expert engineer used frontier AI coding agents to build an accessibility remediation system, generating 420 KLOC of code and detailed field notes. Argues the central engineering challenge shifts from writing code to keeping AI-mediated development inspectable, correctable, and maintainable.

entry.title: Building an ASR Solution for Training and Assessing Children's Reading

author.name: Yacouba Diarra, Nouhoum Souleymane Coulibaly, Mamadou Dembele, Aymane Dembele, Michael Leventhal

entry.summary: This work presents an open-source ASR system for assessing children's reading in Bambara, spanning field data collection, a public benchmark (55 hours from 60 children), model adaptation, and classroom validation. It fine-tunes a Bambara-adapted Fast-Conformer against baselines.

entry.title: Tone-Conditioned Curriculum Learning for Low-Resource Bantu Speech Recognition

author.name: Kesego Mokgosi, Vukosi Marivate, Sitwala Mundia, Unarine Netshifhefhe, Tsholofelo Hope Mogale, Thapelo Sindane

entry.summary: This work proposes a tone-conditioned curriculum framework for six Southern Bantu languages, combining hybrid difficulty scoring, tone-driven gated adapters, and staged training to improve low-resource ASR. It finds strong architecture-language interactions (W2V-BERT better on Nguni, Whisper better on Sotho-Tswana).

entry.title: Signed-Permutation Coordinate Transport for RMSNorm Transformers

author.name: John Sweeney

entry.summary: This paper formalizes the residual-stream gauge for coordinate-indexed objects (steering vectors, SAEs, neuron sets) as architecture-dependent, showing RMSNorm charts carry a signed-permutation gauge rather than permutation-only. It introduces sign-marginalized Hungarian matching and proves permutation-only alignment is symmetry-incomplete for RMSNorm models.

entry.title: Making Failure Safe: A Constrained, Verifiable Agent Framework for Open-Web Data Collection

author.name: Bo Chen

entry.summary: This work replaces free-form LLM code generation for web scraping with typed JSON collector configurations constrained by a six-type taxonomy, templates, and rule-based quality checks to make failures safe and verifiable. It shows on 138 tasks that structured constraints improve reliability of open-web data collection agents.

entry.title: Agri-SAGE: Simulation-Grounded Multi-Agent LLM for Context-Aware Agricultural Advisory Generation

author.name: Vedant Balasubramaniam, Geetha Charan, Manojkumar Patil, Rohit P Suresh, V Priyanka, Kodur Sai Vinay Sathvik, Y. Narahari

entry.summary: Agri-SAGE integrates retrieval-grounded multi-agent LLM reasoning with APSIM biophysical crop simulation to generate and validate context-aware agricultural advisories, comparing Plan-and-Solve, Tree of Thoughts, and Reflexion. It aims to close the gap between static agronomic guidelines and dynamic in-season conditions.

entry.title: AGI Maze as a Benchmark Framework for World-Modeling Agents

author.name: Alexey Potapov

entry.summary: AGI Maze is a lightweight grid-based benchmark framework for evaluating whether agents build persistent, manipulable world-state representations under partial observability, rather than relying on next-token pattern completion. It offers a clean API and multiple difficulty regimes.

entry.title: Bayesian Uncertainty Propagation for Agentic RAG Pipelines: A Proof-of-Concept Study on Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Louis Donaldson, Connor Walker, Koorosh Aslansefat, Yiannis Papadopoulos

entry.summary: This proof-of-concept propagates uncertainty through planner, evaluator, and generator stages of an agentic RAG pipeline using a Bayesian network to estimate system-level and node-level failure likelihood on multi-hop QA. It provides interpretable indicators of where reasoning may break down.

entry.title: SchemaRAG: Dynamic Large Schema Reduction for LLM-driven Structured Information Extraction

author.name: Sin Yu Bonnie Ho, Arlie Coles, Erik Larsson, Eric Marshall, Nathan Bodenstab, Paul Vozila

entry.summary: SchemaRAG dynamically prunes large output schemas for LLM information extraction using schema metadata and few-shot examples, reducing prompt cost and lost-in-the-middle effects. It reports up to 8.8% micro-F1 gains and roughly 47% latency reduction on healthcare and e-commerce data.

entry.title: Learning User-Aware Recall: Personalized Retrieval in Long-Term Conversational Memory

author.name: ZhiShu Jiang, Haibo Liu, Xin Shen, Guanqiang QI, Chenxi Miao, Weikang Li, Liwei Qian, Xin Pei, Jizhou Huang

entry.summary: PPRO makes long-term conversational memory retrieval user-aware by building episodic and semantic memory banks, deriving a user profile as an explicit personalized prior, and making retrieval optimizable rather than fixed by similarity or ranking rules. It targets recalling the right evidence for the right user.

entry.title: AGE: Adaptive-masking for Graph Embedding in Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Bao Long Nguyen Huu, Atsushi Hashimoto

entry.summary: AGE introduces adaptive-masking graph embedding using a Transformer with mask-based self-supervised learning, designed like text-embedding encoders to reduce the misalignment between graph-based and text-based latent features for frozen-LLM GraphRAG. It aims to better fuse concise graph representations with language models.

entry.title: Play Like Champions: Counterfactual Feedback Generation in Latent Space

author.name: Andrzej Bia{\l}ecki, Adam Mastalerz, Han Zhou

entry.summary: This work introduces Latent Maps of Performance to generate counterfactual feedback for human players in real-time strategy games, shifting focus from defeating players to improving them by translating expert-agent knowledge into actionable feedback. It addresses the lack of principled coaching frameworks for RTS games.

entry.title: HydraCollab: Adaptive Collaborative-Perception for Distributed Autonomous Systems

author.name: Luke Chen, Cheng-Ju Wu, David R. Martin, Qilin Ye, Pramod Khargonekar, Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque

entry.summary: HydraCollab is an adaptive collaborative-perception framework for multi-robot systems that selectively transmits the most informative sensor features and dynamically chooses collaboration strategies to balance bandwidth against perception accuracy. It targets real-world communication constraints in distributed autonomous systems.

entry.title: Adaptive Perturbation Selection for Contrastive Audio Decoding

author.name: Aaron Isidore Grace, Zhouyuan Huo, Weiran Wang

entry.summary: Proposes adaptive selection of structured audio perturbations for contrastive decoding to reduce hallucinations in large audio-language models, moving beyond blunt masking or noise. Shows a simple yes/no constraint plus targeted transformations reduces false confirmation of absent audio features.

entry.title: SEFORA: Student Essays with Feedback Corpus and LLM Feedback Evaluation Framework

author.name: Shayan Peyghambari Oskoui, Norah Almousa, Zhaoyi Joey Hou, Carolina Gustafson, Gayle Rogers, Raquel Coelho, Diane Litman, Xiang Lorraine Li

entry.summary: Releases SEFORA, a corpus of 564 college-writing drafts with 8,240 instructor inline feedback annotations, plus UniMatch, a reference-based framework to evaluate whether LLM-generated feedback aligns with instructor feedback. It targets scaling writing support with reliable feedback evaluation.

entry.title: MEPA: Multi-Scale Representation Alignment for Visual Autoregressive Modeling with Mixture of Experts

author.name: Nuoyan Zhou, Zhijun Tu, Lei Yu, Kun Cheng, Jie Hu, Nannan Wang, Xinghao Chen

entry.summary: MEPA introduces a scale-aware token-routed Mixture-of-Experts architecture with multi-scale representation alignment for Visual Autoregressive image generation, mitigating optimization conflicts and error propagation across coarse-to-fine scales. It improves multi-scale representation learning in VAR.

entry.title: A Multi-Resolution Finite-Volume Inspired Deep Learning Framework for Spatiotemporal Dynamics Prediction

author.name: Xin-Yang Liu, Xiantao Fan, Jian-Xun Wang
