entry.title: TDGT: A Tabular Data Generation Toolkit supporting adaptive GPU-accelerated Bayesian mixture models, diffusion-based models, and latent-space generative modeling

author.name: Vasileios C. Pezoulas, Nikolaos S. Tachos, Eleni Georga, Kostas Marias, Manolis Tsiknakis, Dimitrios I. Fotiadis

entry.summary: TDGT is a web-based toolkit for synthetic tabular data generation and fidelity assessment, featuring an Adaptive Bayesian Mixture Synthesizer that auto-selects mixture components, alongside diffusion and latent-space generators. It targets privacy-preserving data sharing with integrated multi-metric evaluation.

entry.title: From Materials Database to Materials Bank: Assetizing Data for AI Driven Materials Innovation

author.name: Chenyao Ma, Di Zhang, Weibo Gong, Wei Du, Rui Su, Yuhang Chen, Kan Xu, Huan Gu, Limin Li, Piao Ma, Zhenghao Li, Hao Li

entry.summary: Proposes a Materials Bank concept that adds a value-filtering and assetization layer on top of conventional materials databases, distinguishing high-potential materials from raw archived records to accelerate industrial translation. Reframes materials data as curated assets for AI-driven innovation.

entry.title: DA-Studio: An Agentic System for End-to-End Data Analysis

author.name: Yizhe Liu, Shaolei Zhang, Ju Fan

entry.summary: DA-Studio is an interactive web-based agentic system for end-to-end data analysis that autonomously organizes multi-step workflows, executes code in a sandbox, and remains inspectable via visible action traces. It targets complete execution-grounded analysis rather than isolated subtasks.

entry.title: Temperature Field Reconstruction of Tungsten Monoblock Divertor on EAST using Physics-aware Neural Operator Transformer

author.name: Zikang Yan, Xiao Wang, Qingquan Yang, Zhendong Yang, Gaoting Chen, Zehua Chen, Bo Jiang, Jin Tang, Guosheng Xu

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-aware neural operator transformer to reconstruct the divertor temperature field on the EAST tokamak in real time, modeling boundary heat-flux relations as a graph with graph attention. Provides a fast alternative to expensive finite-element methods for fusion device control.

entry.title: Automating Cause-Effect Specification with Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models

author.name: Javal Vyas, Milapji Singh Gill, Mehmet Mercang\"oz

entry.summary: Presents a semantic-AI framework combining a knowledge graph with a constrained LLM to automatically generate cause-and-effect matrices and operator-ready safety narratives plus SWRL rules for process control. Automates a traditionally manual, error-prone engineering-specification task.

entry.title: When to Truncate a Feature Ranking: A Residual-Overlap Stopping Rule for Subset Selection

author.name: Jesus S. Aguilar-Ruiz

entry.summary: Develops a distributional, risk-calibrated stopping rule for truncating supervised feature rankings based on accumulated class-separation evidence, replacing arbitrary cardinality thresholds or cross-validation. Provides an interpretable criterion for when to stop selecting features.

entry.title: Cross-lingual Relation Extraction with Large Language Models: Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, and Fine-Tuned Evaluation on Romanian

author.name: Dragos-Mitrut Vasile, Elena-Simona Apostol, Stefan-Adrian Toma, Adrian Paschke, Ciprian-Octavian Truica

entry.summary: Evaluates cross-lingual relation extraction for low-resource Romanian by translating SemEval-2010 Task 8 with an LLM pipeline and testing Gemma 4 31B under zero-shot, few-shot, and QLoRA fine-tuning against encoder baselines. Reports a modest performance drop from English to Romanian.

entry.title: Better Understanding, Understanding Better

author.name: Yu Wei (Department of Philosophy, East China Normal University)

entry.summary: Introduces a comparative epistemic logic of understanding with level-indexed understanding modalities and a connective for comparing how well agents understand why a proposition holds, addressing understanding's neglect in epistemic logic despite its centrality in epistemology and AI debates. Formalizes that understanding comes in degrees.

entry.title: Knowledge-Driven Dimension Estimation from a Single Image -3D Asset Generation Technology for Digital Twin Construction

author.name: Hidenori Sakaniwa, Akihito Akai, Akihiko Hyodo

entry.summary: This paper estimates real-world object scale from a single monocular image by decomposing objects into structural elements and integrating design-rule and geometric knowledge, targeting traffic-sign sizing for digital-twin/simulation construction. It addresses scale mismatch between virtual and real environments in in-vehicle camera verification.

entry.title: Horseshoe Priors for Spatial Small Area Estimation: Regular Variation, Tail Robustness, and Deep Learning

author.name: Dhiman Bhadra, Nicholas Polson

entry.summary: This paper studies horseshoe (heavy-tailed global-local) priors in the Fay-Herriot model for spatial small area estimation, analyzing regular variation, tail robustness, and connections to deep learning. It contributes theoretical characterizations of when heavy-tailed pooling outperforms Gaussian smoothing.

entry.title: Who Determines the Meaning of an Emotion? Affective Sovereignty as an Epistemic Consequence of Measurement Limits

author.name: Keito Inoshita

entry.summary: This philosophical paper asks who holds final authority to determine the meaning of one's own emotion as emotion-sensing AI becomes embedded in society, coining the term Affectosphere. It analyzes measurement limits by decomposing annotation uncertainty into reducible and irreducible components.

entry.title: PGUDA: Pressure-Guided Unsupervised Domain Adaptation with Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation for sEMG-Based Gesture Recognition

author.name: Yurui Liu, Xiao-Cong Zhong, Qisong Wang, Xuefu Wang, Dan Liu, Jinwei Sun

entry.summary: PGUDA is an unsupervised domain-adaptation framework for sEMG gesture recognition that uses stable pressure signals to guide cross-modal knowledge distillation, mitigating cross-subject and cross-session distribution shifts. Aims to improve deployment robustness of EMG-based human-computer interfaces.

entry.title: Von Mises Based Uncertainty Quantification for Closely Spaced Automotive Radar Targets

author.name: Vinay Kulkarni, V. V. Reddy

entry.summary: Compares a von Mises circular-statistics ensemble against evidential deep learning for uncertainty-aware direction-of-arrival estimation of closely spaced automotive radar targets. Reports the ensemble yields interpretable directional uncertainty and better out-of-distribution behavior.

entry.title: Improving multichannel speech enhancement through accurate room-acoustic simulations

author.name: Georg G\"otz, Alessia Milo, Steinar Gu{\dh}j\'onsson, Daniel Gert Nielsen, Jesper Pedersen, Finnur Pind

entry.summary: Studies how room-acoustic simulation fidelity affects multichannel speech enhancement, training SpatialNet on datasets from geometrical, wave-based, and hybrid acoustic modeling and evaluating on measured data. Finds higher-fidelity wave-based simulation improves real-world performance.

entry.title: A Tutorial on Autonomous Fault-Tolerant Control Using Knowledge-Grounded LLM Agents

author.name: Javal Vyas, Milapji Singh Gill, Artan Markaj, Felix Gehlhoff, Mehmet Mercang\"oz

entry.summary: A tutorial framework treating LLM agents as constrained supervisory planners for autonomous fault-tolerant control in process plants, proposing recovery actions that are validated by external symbolic or simulation-based checkers before actuation. Develops design dimensions for knowledge-grounded fault recovery.

entry.title: Agency is not a natural kind (and why that might matter for alignment)

author.name: SJ_Beard

entry.summary: This post argues that agency is not a natural kind, contending that humans and other systems we attribute agency to are really messy hierarchies of processes rather than unified thought-driven agents, and explores why this matters for alignment. It challenges folk-psychological framings underlying agent-based safety thinking.

entry.title: Q&A: What is agentic AI today, and what do we want it to be?

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: In this MIT News Q&A, MIT's Phillip Isola explains what agentic AI is (AI that takes actions in the world, physical or digital) versus generative AI, discussing the underlying models and mechanisms as businesses rapidly deploy AI agents. It provides accessible context on a fast-growing deployment trend.

entry.title: Team MKC at CLPsych 2026: Capturing and Characterizing Mental Health Changes through Social Media Timeline Dynamics

author.name: Kyomin Hwang, Hyeonjin Kim, Hyunho Lee, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: Describes a CLPsych 2026 shared-task LLM pipeline for capturing and characterizing mental-health changes across sequentially ordered social-media timelines, aiming to support early detection and continuous monitoring of psychological well-being. Focuses on temporal timeline dynamics for mental-health analysis.

entry.title: Neuro-Bayesian-Symbolic Residual Attention Shallow Network: Explainable Deep Learning for Cybersecurity Risk Assessment

author.name: Nicolaie Popescu-Bodorin, Madeleine Togher

entry.summary: NBS-RASN is a hybrid shallow neural architecture combining neural, Bayesian, and symbolic components for explainable cybersecurity risk assessment, enforcing epistemological axioms as hard constraints. It claims deep-learning behavior from a shallow interpretable network.

entry.title: From Idea to Prototype in an Afternoon: Scaffolded, AI-Assisted Rapid VA Prototyping

author.name: Gennady Andrienko, Natalia Andrienko

entry.summary: A case study showing that combining a workflow-scaffolding language (ATWL) with an AI assistant reduced visual-analytics prototyping from months to an afternoon. Derives lessons about the necessity of both structured scaffolds and human expertise for effective AI-assisted development.

entry.title: Cluelessness: Summary of the argument, why it matters, and counterarguments

author.name: Anthony DiGiovanni

entry.summary: This post summarizes the unawareness argument for cluelessness in effective altruism, breaking it into normative and epistemic premises and outlining the most productive lines of critique. It aims to orient participants in a critique competition on whether we can justifiably rank actions by long-run consequences.

entry.title: Why Prefer Any Decision Theory?

author.name: J Bostock

entry.summary: This post defends Functional Decision Theory, arguing that critics who construct scenarios where FDT fails are falling foul of symmetry arguments and applying inconsistent standards of rigor. It contends FDT ties or beats CDT across the abstract-to-practical spectrum.

entry.title: Information-Aided DVL Calibration

author.name: Zeev Yampolsky, Itzik Klein

entry.summary: Presents an information-aided method to calibrate Doppler velocity logs for underwater vehicle navigation when GNSS reference signals are unavailable, replacing conventional Kalman-filter calibration. Targets robustness of AUV navigation in GNSS-denied environments.

entry.title: Calibrating the Evaluator: Does Probability Calibration Mitigate Preference Coupling in LLM Agent Feedback Loops?

author.name: Zewen Liu

entry.summary: Investigates whether probability calibration of LLM evaluators can reduce evaluator preference coupling, where evaluator biases propagate into agent-learned strategies during feedback-loop training. Reports the first study comparing binary versus confidence-calibrated feedback in a small controlled experiment.

entry.title: Is it ethical to work on general-purpose robots given the risk of cyberhacking?

author.name: Master Chief

entry.summary: This post raises the ethical question of whether developing general-purpose robots is responsible given the risk that mass-deployed robots could be hacked and repurposed for repression, enabling totalitarian control. It notes the near-absence of assessments of this specific risk pathway.

entry.title: Minimizing Quantized Semantic Age of Information (QSAoI) in Foundation Model-Based Semantic Communications

author.name: Huanyu Zhang, Yulin Hu, Xiaopeng Yuan, Aydin Sezgin, Anke Schmeink

entry.summary: Introduces Quantized Semantic Age of Information, a metric capturing freshness versus semantic efficiency tradeoffs for foundation-model-based semantic communications in 6G finite-blocklength regimes, and a co-designed resource-allocation framework to minimize it. Bridges semantic and physical layers for low-latency transmission.

entry.title: Unjournal tool hub (finding & assessing high-impact research questions, cruxes, papers, etc.)

author.name: david reinstein

entry.summary: The Unjournal announces a hub of tools for finding and assessing high-impact research, including a prioritization dashboard, a cruxes and pivotal-questions explorer, and LLM-assisted evaluation guides. It aims to help researchers choose impactful questions and improve research evaluation.

entry.title: Expanding our Heat Resilience data to 50+ global cities

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google announces the expansion of its Heat Resilience dataset to more than 50 global cities, supporting climate adaptation efforts. The post is a brief update on applied climate and sustainability data infrastructure.

entry.title: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning based Intrusion Detection in Realistic IoT Networks

author.name: Rana Alharbi, Chuadhry Mujeeb Ahmed

entry.summary: Compares machine-learning intrusion detection methods on the realistic Gotham2025 IoT dataset generated from 78 emulated devices across MQTT, CoAP, and RTSP protocols. Aims to help safeguard resource-constrained IoT networks against attacks.

entry.title: In partial defence of p(doom)

author.name: Mikhail Samin

entry.summary: Mikhail Samin defends p(doom) as a useful shorthand for surfacing disagreements and identifying whether someone is engaging with core AI risk arguments, while acknowledging it is less useful among informed rationalists. It advocates using the number as a communication and double-crux tool.

entry.title: Creating Intelligence: A Computational Foundation for AGI

author.name: Peter Overmann

entry.summary: This work proposes a computational theory of mind grounded in set theory and hyperdimensional computing, representing information as sparse binary sets with learning driven by topological plasticity rather than scalar weight updates. It claims associative memory emerges naturally from combinatorially expanded network topologies.

author.name: Shiyi Chen, Nicholas Saban, Collin Hargreaves, Huiqi Wang

author.name: Benjamin Breen, Austin Letson, Borja Requena Pozo, Leopoldo Sarra

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.32007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study agentic code generation in Dafny, where a model must generate both executable code and the proof artifacts for verification. We present AxDafn...

author.name: Sk Md Ahnaf Akif Alvi, Jan Janssen, Danny Perez, Douglas Allaire, Raymundo Arroyave

author.name: Chukwuemeka Ugwu, Oluwafemi Richard Oyeleke

author.name: Xinze Zhang

author.name: Carlos Eduardo Sanoja, Oscar Enrique Moreno Mayz

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.30650v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Educational support services often face a qualified-capacity problem: staff time is scarce, qualifications decay, new support needs can appear before...

author.name: Xinyu Qin, Vicky Ye, Ruiheng Yu, Lu Wang

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.30651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Delirium is common in hospitalized patients and is often missed in routine care. We present a user-centered interactive machine learning (UC-iML) fra...

author.name: Muneera Bano, Didar Zowghi

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.30652v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transparency is increasingly mandated for public-sector AI systems, with organisations required to publish statements describing their AI use and ove...

author.name: Marina Mancoridis, Zo\"e Hitzig

author.name: Anshumali Shrivastava

author.name: Abayomi O. Agbeyangi, Jose M. Lukose

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.30656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has the potential to be transformative for development, but Africa is currently facing a fragmented and challenging "AI ...

author.name: Pietro Mascagni, Lalith Sharan, Deepak Alapatt, Nicolas Padoy

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.30657v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Surgical outcomes depend not only on patient factors and postoperative care but are also strongly influenced by the quality of the operation itself. ...

entry.title: Separation of Knowledge and Reasoning?

author.name: HGross

entry.summary: This post asks whether AI research has attempted to surgically remove specific pretrained knowledge from a model without degrading reasoning, then retrain it to reacquire that knowledge via reasoning and tools, aiming for small models capable when tool-augmented. It probes the separation of memorized knowledge from reasoning.

entry.title: The Slogan Strikes Again

author.name: mrdodson

entry.summary: This essay examines the compression-is-intelligence slogan, framing LLM training as compressing the human text corpus into weights and using the compression of mathematics as an intuition for how learning arises when a model cannot simply memorize. It offers an information-theoretic perspective on why LLMs appear intelligent.

entry.title: That Which Cannot Be Poked With A Stick Is The Mind-Killer

author.name: Firinn

entry.summary: This rationalist essay extends the politics-as-mind-killer theme, arguing that empirically untestable disagreements (those that cannot be poked with a stick) are especially prone to distorted reasoning. It uses a parable of two rationalist houses debating prison abolition to illustrate the difficulty of resolving non-experimental cruxes.

entry.title: Interpersonalized recommendations

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Katja Grace muses on why recommendation services like Netflix do not offer joint recommendations for groups or pairs of users despite having individual profiles, noting how useful and seemingly feasible this would be. It is a light observation on a gap in recommender-system products.

entry.title: Connect to your past selves

author.name: PatrickDFarley

entry.summary: This personal-development post frames introspection as connecting to one's past selves for reflection, accountability, and consistency, treating identity as a four-dimensional entity. It offers a productivity-coaching perspective on self-understanding.

entry.title: Should authors or readers fill the gaps in mathematical arguments?

author.name: knowledgeMaintenance

entry.summary: This post argues about whether authors or readers should fill gaps in mathematical arguments, contending that large gaps increase total time cost across many readers while small one-line gaps are acceptable. It offers qualitative and quantitative reasoning about mathematical exposition norms.

entry.title: More Failed Eggless Choux

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: This post documents repeated failed attempts to make eggless choux pastry using vegan egg white protein, noting the batter looked right but did not puff, with a hypothesis about eggs' multiple proteins setting at different temperatures. It is a personal cooking experiment.
